
```python
def main():
    Log(exchange.GetRate())
    # Output: 1 (default when SetRate has not been called)
    exchange.SetRate(7)
    Log(exchange.GetRate())
    # Output: 7
```

```rust
fn main() {
    Log!(exchange.GetRate());
    // Output: 1 (default when SetRate has not been called)
    exchange.SetRate(7);
    Log!(exchange.GetRate());
    // Output: 7
}
```

If the conversion rate has not been set by calling ```exchange.SetRate()```, the ```exchange.GetRate()``` function will return the default rate value ```1```, meaning that the data related to the currently displayed quote currency (quoteCurrency) has not been converted by any exchange rate.

If an exchange rate value has been set using ```exchange.SetRate()```, for example ```exchange.SetRate(7)```, then the prices in the data obtained through the ```exchange``` object—such as tickers, market depth, K-lines, orders and positions—will be multiplied by the set rate ```7``` for conversion; prices passed when placing orders are taken as converted prices and divided by the rate before being sent, see `exchange.SetRate`.

If ```exchange``` corresponds to an exchange that uses the US dollar as its quote currency, after calling ```exchange.SetRate(7)```, all prices in live trading will be multiplied by ```7```, converting them to prices close to the Chinese yuan (CNY). At this point, the rate value obtained through ```exchange.GetRate()``` is ```7```.

See also: `exchange.SetRate`

#### exchange.SetRate

```
exchange.SetRate(rate)
```

Set the current exchange rate of the exchange object.

Parameters:

- `rate` (number, required): Conversion rate; a value less than or equal to 0 is treated as 1 (no conversion).

Returns (number): The exchange rate before this call.

Set the rate to 7 so prices are multiplied by 7, then restore it to 1.

```javascript
function main(){
    Log(exchange.GetTicker())
    // Set exchange rate conversion
    exchange.SetRate(7)
    Log(exchange.GetTicker())
    // Set to 1, no conversion
    exchange.SetRate(1)
}
```

```python
def main():
    Log(exchange.GetTicker())
    exchange.SetRate(7)
    Log(exchange.GetTicker())
    exchange.SetRate(1)
```

```rust
fn main() {
    Log!(exchange.GetTicker(None));
    // Set exchange rate conversion
    exchange.SetRate(7);
    Log!(exchange.GetTicker(None));
    // Set to 1, no conversion
    exchange.SetRate(1);
}
```

If an exchange rate has been set with ```exchange.SetRate()```, for example 7, then the prices in the ticker, depth, K-line, order and position data obtained through this ```exchange``` object, as well as the quote-currency ```Balance``` and ```FrozenBalance``` of the account, are multiplied by 7; amounts are not converted.
When placing orders (```exchange.Buy()```, ```exchange.Sell()```, ```exchange.CreateOrder()```), the price you pass is taken as a converted price and is divided by the rate back into the original currency before being sent to the exchange; non-positive prices such as ```-1``` for market orders are not converted. Prices for ```exchange.ModifyOrder()``` and condition orders are not converted and must be given in the exchange's original currency.
For example, if ```exchange``` is an exchange quoted in US dollars, after ```exchange.SetRate(7)``` all live prices are multiplied by 7 and become close to **CNY**-denominated prices.

See also: `exchange.GetRate`

#### exchange.SetBase

```
exchange.SetBase(s)
```

Sets the base URL of the exchange API interface used by the `exchange` object.

Parameters:

- `s` (string, required): Base URL of the exchange API interface.

Switch the API base URL and fetch the ticker before and after.

```javascript
function main() {
    // Use the default base URL
    Log(exchange.GetTicker())
    // Switch to https://aws.okx.com
    exchange.SetBase("https://aws.okx.com")
    Log(exchange.GetTicker())
}
```

```python
def main():
    Log(exchange.GetTicker())
    exchange.SetBase("https://aws.okx.com")
    Log(exchange.GetTicker())
```

```rust
fn main() {
    // Use the default base URL
    Log!(exchange.GetTicker(None));
    // Switch to https://aws.okx.com
    exchange.SetBase("https://aws.okx.com");
    Log!(exchange.GetTicker(None));
}
```

The backtesting system does not support switching the base URL of the exchange API interface, because the backtesting system is a sandbox simulation environment and does not actually access the exchange's API interface.

See also: `exchange.IO`

#### exchange.GetBase

```
exchange.GetBase()
```

Gets the base address of the current exchange API interface.

Returns (string): The base address of the current exchange API interface.

Print the API base URL used by the current exchange object.

```javascript
function main() {
    Log(exchange.GetBase())
    // Output: https://api.binance.com (Binance spot, for example)
}
```

```python
def main():
    Log(exchange.GetBase())
    # Output: https://api.binance.com (Binance spot, for example)
```

```rust
fn main() {
    Log!(exchange.GetBase());
    // Output: https://api.binance.com (Binance spot, for example)
}
```

See also: `exchange.SetBase`

#### exchange.SetProxy

```
exchange.SetProxy(proxy)
```

Sets the proxy configuration of the `exchange` object.

Parameters:

- `proxy` (string, required): Proxy configuration in the form ```scheme://[username:password@]host:port```; pass an empty string to remove the proxy.

Returns (bool / null value): Returns ```true``` on success; if the proxy format is invalid (unsupported scheme or missing host and port), returns a null value, the error message can be obtained with `GetLastError`, and the previous proxy setting stays unchanged.

Configure a ```socks5``` proxy for the `exchange` object.

```javascript
function main() {
    exchange.SetProxy("socks5://192.168.1.10:8080")
    // If the exchange market data API is unreachable, set a working socks5 proxy to reach it
    Log(exchange.GetTicker())
}
```

```python
def main():
    exchange.SetProxy("socks5://192.168.1.10:8080")
    Log(exchange.GetTicker())
```

```rust
fn main() {
    exchange.SetProxy("socks5://192.168.1.10:8080");
    // If the exchange market data API is unreachable, set a working socks5 proxy to reach it
    Log!(exchange.GetTicker(None));
}
```

Each `exchange` object can have one proxy. Once set, the exchange object's network requests to the exchange (REST requests and the WebSocket connections opened by the exchange connector) go through the proxy.

Supported proxy schemes: ```http://```, ```https://```, ```socks5://```, ```socks5h://``` (domain names resolved by the proxy server) and ```ssocks5://``` (socks5 over TLS), all of which can carry a username and password. Taking the first added exchange object `exchange`, i.e. ```exchanges[0]```, as an example:
- Set a proxy without username or password: ```exchange.SetProxy("socks5://127.0.0.1:8889")```.
- Set a proxy with username and password: ```exchange.SetProxy("socks5://username:password@127.0.0.1:8889")```, where ```username``` is the username and ```password``` is the password.
- Switch back to normal mode without a proxy: ```exchange.SetProxy("")```.

Specifying the source IP address of requests per exchange object (the legacy ```ip://``` form) is not supported. To specify the outgoing IP, set it globally with the ```-I``` command-line option when starting the docker.

See also: `exchange`

#### exchange.SetTimeout

```
exchange.SetTimeout(timeout)
```

Sets the timeout for ```rest``` requests of the `exchange` object.

Parameters:

- `timeout` (number, required): Timeout in milliseconds.

Set the REST request timeout to 3 seconds, then fetch the ticker.

```javascript
function main() {
    exchange.SetTimeout(3000)
    Log(exchange.GetTicker())
}
```

```python
def main():
    exchange.SetTimeout(3000)
    Log(exchange.GetTicker())
```

```rust
fn main() {
    exchange.SetTimeout(3000);
    Log!(exchange.GetTicker(None));
}
```

The ```timeout``` parameter is a value in milliseconds, where 1000 milliseconds equals 1 second. This setting only applies to the ```rest``` protocol and is used to set the timeout for ```rest``` requests; it only needs to be set once to take effect. For example: ```exchange.SetTimeout(3000)``` sets the ```rest``` request timeout of the ```exchange``` object to 3 seconds; when calling functions that involve network requests such as ```exchange.GetTicker()```, if no response is received within 3 seconds, it is determined to be a timeout, and the timed-out function call will return a null value.

```SetTimeout()``` is not a global function, but a method of the `exchange` object.

See also: `exchange`

#### exchange.Encode

```
exchange.Encode(algo, inputFormat, outputFormat, data)
exchange.Encode(algo, inputFormat, outputFormat, data, keyFormat, key)
```

Performs signature and encryption computations.

Parameters:

- `algo` (string, required): The signing or hashing algorithm, for example ```sha256``` or ```ed25519```; see the remarks for all values.
- `inputFormat` (string, required): Used to specify the data format of the ```data``` parameter. The ```inputFormat``` parameter supports being set to one of: "raw", "hex", "base64", "string". "raw" represents raw data, "hex" represents ```hex```-encoded data, "base64" represents ```base64```-encoded data, and "string" represents string data.
- `outputFormat` (string, required): Used to specify the output data format. The ```outputFormat``` parameter supports being set to one of: "raw", "hex", "base64", "string". "raw" represents raw data, "hex" represents ```hex```-encoded data, "base64" represents ```base64```-encoded data, and "string" represents string data.
- `data` (string, required): Data to be processed.
- `keyFormat` (string, optional): Used to specify the data format of the ```key``` parameter. The ```keyFormat``` parameter supports being set to one of: "raw", "hex", "base64", "string". "raw" represents raw data, "hex" represents ```hex```-encoded data, "base64" represents ```base64```-encoded data, and "string" represents string data.
- `key` (string, optional): Key used in the signature computation. You can use a plaintext string, or you can use ```"{{accesskey}}"``` and ```"{{secretkey}}"``` to refer respectively to the ```accessKey``` and ```secretKey``` configured in the `exchange` object.

Returns (string): Computed hash value encoding.

Sign request parameters with HMAC-SHA256 using the secretKey configured on the exchange object.

```javascript
function main() {
    var query = "symbol=BTCUSDT&timestamp=" + Date.now()
    var signature = exchange.Encode("sha256", "raw", "hex", query, "raw", "{{secretkey}}")
    Log(signature)
    // Output: a 64-character hex signature
}
```

```python
import time
def main():
    query = "symbol=BTCUSDT&timestamp=" + str(int(time.time() * 1000))
    signature = exchange.Encode("sha256", "raw", "hex", query, "raw", "{{secretkey}}")
    Log(signature)
    # Output: a 64-character hex signature
```

```rust
fn main() {
    let query = format!("symbol=BTCUSDT&timestamp={}", Unix() * 1000);
    let signature = exchange.Encode("sha256", "raw", "hex", &query, "raw", "{{secretkey}}");
    Log!(signature);
    // Output: a 64-character hex signature
}
```

Example of Bybit v5 private WebSocket authentication and position push subscription (wss protocol): when ```key``` is passed the calculation is an HMAC, and the signature is the hex encoding of ```HMAC_SHA256(secretKey, "GET/realtime" + expires)```, where ```expires``` is a millisecond timestamp. ```"{{secretkey}}"``` refers to the ```secretKey``` configured in the exchange object (used as a string, so ```keyFormat``` is ```string```), so the secret key never appears in plain text in the strategy code.

```javascript
function main() {
    var APIKEY = "your Bybit API Key"
    // expires is a millisecond timestamp; signature = HMAC_SHA256(secretKey, "GET/realtime" +
    // expires), hex encoded
    var expires = Date.now() + 10000
    var signature = exchange.Encode("sha256", "string", "hex", "GET/realtime" + expires, "string",
        "{{secretkey}}")
    var client = Dial("wss://stream.bybit.com/v5/private", 60)
    if (!client) {
        Log("connection failed")
        return
    }
    client.write(JSON.stringify({op: "auth", args: [APIKEY, expires, signature]}))
    client.write(JSON.stringify({op: "subscribe", args: ["position"]}))
    var positions = {}
    var lastPing = Date.now()
    while (true) {
        // Bybit recommends sending a heartbeat every 20 seconds
        if (Date.now() - lastPing >= 20000) {
            client.write(JSON.stringify({op: "ping"}))
            lastPing = Date.now()
        }
        var buf = client.read(1000)
        if (buf === "") {
            break    // connection closed
        }
        if (!buf) {
            continue
        }
        var msg = JSON.parse(buf)
        if (msg.op == "auth" && !msg.success) {
            Log("auth failed", msg.ret_msg)
            break
        }
        if (msg.topic == "position") {
            msg.data.forEach(function(p) {
                var key = p.symbol + "/" + p.positionIdx
                var now = p.side + " " + p.size
                if (positions[key] !== now) {
                    Log("position change", key, positions[key], "->", now, "@")
                    positions[key] = now
                }
            })
        }
    }
}
```

```python
import time
import json
def main():
    APIKEY = "your Bybit API Key"
    # expires is a millisecond timestamp; signature = HMAC_SHA256(secretKey, "GET/realtime" +
    # expires), hex encoded
    expires = int(time.time() * 1000) + 10000
    signature = exchange.Encode("sha256", "string", "hex", "GET/realtime" + str(expires), "string",
        "{{secretkey}}")
    client = Dial("wss://stream.bybit.com/v5/private", 60)
    if not client:
        Log("connection failed")
        return
    client.write(json.dumps({"op": "auth", "args": [APIKEY, expires, signature]}))
    client.write(json.dumps({"op": "subscribe", "args": ["position"]}))
    positions = {}
    lastPing = time.time()
    while True:
        # Bybit recommends sending a heartbeat every 20 seconds
        if time.time() - lastPing >= 20:
            client.write(json.dumps({"op": "ping"}))
            lastPing = time.time()
        buf = client.read(1000)
        if buf == "":
            break    # connection closed
        if not buf:
            continue
        msg = json.loads(buf)
        if msg.get("op") == "auth" and not msg.get("success"):
            Log("auth failed", msg.get("ret_msg"))
            break
        if msg.get("topic") == "position":
            for p in msg["data"]:
                key = "%s/%s" % (p["symbol"], p["positionIdx"])
                now = p["side"] + " " + p["size"]
                if positions.get(key) != now:
                    Log("position change", key, positions.get(key), "->", now, "@")
                    positions[key] = now
```

```rust
use std::collections::HashMap;

fn main() {
    let apikey = "your Bybit API Key";
    // expires is a millisecond timestamp; signature = HMAC_SHA256(secretKey, "GET/realtime" +
    // expires), hex encoded
    let expires = Unix() * 1000 + 10000;
    let signature = exchange.Encode("sha256", "string", "hex", &format!("GET/realtime{}", expires), "string", "{{secretkey}}");
    let mut client = Dial::new("wss://stream.bybit.com/v5/private", 60);
    if !client.Valid() {
        Log!("connection failed");
        return;
    }
    // the Rust SDK has no JSON serializer, so build the requests with string formatting
    client.write(&format!(r#"{{"op":"auth","args":["{}",{},"{}"]}}"#, apikey, expires, signature), 0);
    client.write(r#"{"op":"subscribe","args":["position"]}"#, 0);
    let mut positions: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();
    let mut last_ping = Unix();
    while !client.IsClosed() {
        // Bybit recommends sending a heartbeat every 20 seconds
        if Unix() - last_ping >= 20 {
            client.write(r#"{"op":"ping"}"#, 0);
            last_ping = Unix();
        }
        let buf = client.read(1000);
        if buf == "" {
            continue;
        }
        let msg = match JSONParse(&buf) {
            Some(v) => v,
            None => continue,
        };
        if msg["op"].as_str() == Some("auth") && msg["success"].as_bool() != Some(true) {
            Log!("auth failed", msg["ret_msg"].as_str().unwrap_or(""));
            break;
        }
        if msg["topic"].as_str() == Some("position") {
            if let Some(arr) = msg["data"].as_array() {
                for p in arr {
                    let key = format!("{}/{}", p["symbol"].as_str().unwrap_or(""), p["positionIdx"].as_i64().unwrap_or(0));
                    let now = format!("{} {}", p["side"].as_str().unwrap_or(""), p["size"].as_str().unwrap_or("0"));
                    if positions.get(&key) != Some(&now) {
                        Log!("position change", &key, &now, "@");
                        positions.insert(key, now);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

Only live trading supports calling the ```exchange.Encode()``` function. The reference methods ```"{{accesskey}}"``` and ```"{{secretkey}}"``` are only valid when calling the ```exchange.Encode()``` function.

Values of ```algo```:

| Category | Values |
| - | - |
| No algorithm | ```raw``` |
| Signing | ```sign```, ```signTx``` |
| Hash (MD, SHA-1, SHA-2) | ```md4```, ```md5```, ```sha1```, ```sha256```, ```sha512```, ```sha512.384```, ```sha512.256```, ```sha512.224``` |
| Hash (SHA-3, Keccak) | ```keccak256```, ```sha3.224```, ```sha3.256```, ```sha3.384```, ```sha3.512```, ```sha3.keccak256```, ```sha3.keccak512``` |
| Hash (others) | ```ripemd160```, ```blake2b.256```, ```blake2b.512```, ```blake2s.128```, ```blake2s.256``` |
| String encoding and decoding | ```text.encoder.utf8```, ```text.decoder.utf8```, ```text.encoder.gbk```, ```text.decoder.gbk``` |
| Ed25519 | ```ed25519```, ```ed25519.seed```; a hash algorithm can be given, for example ```ed25519.md5```, ```ed25519.sha512``` |

See also: `exchange`, `Encode`

### IO

Calls the extended features of an exchange object; the first argument is the command name. Start with `exchange.IO` for the full list of commands and the commands specific to each exchange, then see the page of each command. Commands specific to exchange objects such as Web3, Uniswap and Jupiter are on their exchange pages, for example `Web3`, `Uniswap` and `Jupiter`.

#### exchange.IO

```
exchange.IO(k, ...args)
```

Calls other interfaces related to the exchange object.

Parameters:

- `k` (string, required): Call type identifier. Different values correspond to different functions; please refer to the descriptions in each section below for details.
- `args` (string / number / bool / object / array / any, optional): Extended parameters. Different parameters are passed according to the ```k``` value; their number and types are not fixed, and some commands take no parameters.

Returns (string / number / bool / object / array / any): The return value depends on the command, and some commands return a null value on success; a failed call returns a null value, and the error message can be obtained with `GetLastError`.

Switch the margin mode and call a raw exchange endpoint (Binance futures as an example).

```javascript
function main() {
    exchange.SetContractType("swap")
    // Switch the current contract to isolated margin
    exchange.IO("cross", false)
    // The third argument names the contract: switch the ETH_USDT perpetual to cross margin
    exchange.IO("cross", true, "ETH_USDT.swap")
    // Call an endpoint that has no wrapper function
    var ret = exchange.IO("api", "GET", "/fapi/v1/time")
    Log(ret)
}
```

```python
def main():
    exchange.SetContractType("swap")
    exchange.IO("cross", False)
    exchange.IO("cross", True, "ETH_USDT.swap")
    ret = exchange.IO("api", "GET", "/fapi/v1/time")
    Log(ret)
```

```rust
fn main() {
    let _ = exchange.SetContractType("swap");
    // Switch the current contract to isolated margin
    let _ = exchange.IO(("cross", false));
    // The third argument names the contract: switch the ETH_USDT perpetual to cross margin
    let _ = exchange.IO(("cross", true, "ETH_USDT.swap"));
    // Call an endpoint that has no wrapper function
    let ret = exchange.IO(("api", "GET", "/fapi/v1/time"));
    Log!(ret);
}
```

##### Commands at a glance

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| ```api``` | Call a raw exchange endpoint that has no wrapper function |
| ```currency``` | Switch the trading pair at runtime |
| ```base``` | Query or switch the API base address |
| ```simulate```, ```cross```, ```dual```, ```unified``` and more | Switch trading modes, see ```exchange.IO(mode, value)``` |
| ```rate``` / ```quota``` | Rate-limit API calls |

Each command has its own page in this category; commands specific to an exchange object are indexed below and documented on the exchange pages (see `Capability Matrix`).

##### Return values and error checking

The return value depends on the command. Some commands (for example ```cross```, ```dual``` or ```unified``` on some futures exchanges) return a null value on success, which is the same as the value returned on failure; to confirm success, read the error message with `GetLastError` after the call. A command the exchange does not support reports an error (```unsupported io method```) and returns a null value.

Commands that act on a specific contract, such as ```cross```, ```dual``` and ```unified```, accept a ```symbol``` argument after the value to name the contract, for example ```exchange.IO("cross", false, "ETH_USDT.swap")```; without it they act on the current trading pair and contract. Whether such a command applies per contract or to the whole account, and what each command returns, is given in the IO command table of the exchange page.

#### exchange.IO("api", ...)

```
exchange.IO(k, httpMethod, resource)
exchange.IO(k, httpMethod, resource, params)
exchange.IO(k, httpMethod, resource, params, raw)
```

Forms:

- `exchange.IO("api", ...)`

Calls a raw REST endpoint of the exchange that has no wrapper function; the platform signs the request. On a Web3 exchange object the command of the same name calls smart contracts, see `exchange.IO("api", ...)`.

Parameters:

- `k` (string, required): Selects the ```exchange.IO()``` feature; ```api``` calls a raw exchange endpoint.
- `httpMethod` (string, required): HTTP method, e.g. ```GET```, ```POST```, ```DELETE```.
- `resource` (string, required): Endpoint path; a full URL also works (its host replaces the current base address).
- `params` (string, optional): URL-encoded request parameters.
- `raw` (string, optional): Raw request body, e.g. a JSON string.

Returns (object / array / string / null value): Returns the full response of the endpoint; a response that is not JSON is returned as a string. Returns a null value on failure. Live trading only.

Use the ```api``` mode to call the ```Futures_OKCoin``` (OKX futures) batch order placement interface, and pass the JSON-formatted order data via the ```raw``` parameter.

```javascript
function main() {
    var arrOrders = [
        {"instId":"BTC-USDT-SWAP","tdMode":"cross","side":"buy","ordType":"limit","px":"16000","sz":"1","posSide":"long"},
        {"instId":"BTC-USDT-SWAP","tdMode":"cross","side":"buy","ordType":"limit","px":"16000","sz":"2","posSide":"long"}
    ]

    // Call exchange.IO to directly access the exchange's batch order placement interface
    var ret = exchange.IO("api", "POST", "/api/v5/trade/batch-orders", "", JSON.stringify(arrOrders))
    Log(ret)
}
```

```python
import json
def main():
    arrOrders = [
        {"instId":"BTC-USDT-SWAP","tdMode":"cross","side":"buy","ordType":"limit","px":"16000","sz":"1","posSide":"long"},
        {"instId":"BTC-USDT-SWAP","tdMode":"cross","side":"buy","ordType":"limit","px":"16000","sz":"2","posSide":"long"}
    ]
    ret = exchange.IO("api", "POST", "/api/v5/trade/batch-orders", "", json.dumps(arrOrders))
    Log(ret)
```

```rust
fn main() {
    // Rust has no JSON serialization; construct the order array directly using a raw string
    let arrOrders = r#"[
        {"instId":"BTC-USDT-SWAP","tdMode":"cross","side":"buy","ordType":"limit","px":"16000","sz":"1","posSide":"long"},
        {"instId":"BTC-USDT-SWAP","tdMode":"cross","side":"buy","ordType":"limit","px":"16000","sz":"2","posSide":"long"}
    ]"#;

    // Call exchange.IO to directly access the exchange's batch order placement interface; multiple parameters are passed in as a tuple
    let ret = exchange.IO(("api", "POST", "/api/v5/trade/batch-orders", "", arrOrders));
    Log!(ret);
}
```

When the value of a key in the ```params``` parameter is of string type, you need to wrap the parameter value with single quotes.

```javascript
var amount = 1
var price = 10
var basecurrency = "ltc"
function main () {
    // Note that there is a ' character on both the left and right sides of amount.toString() and price.toString()
    var message = "symbol=" + basecurrency + "&amount='" + amount.toString() + "'&price='" + price.toString() + "'&side=buy" + "&type=limit"
    var id = exchange.IO("api", "POST", "/v1/order/new", message)
}
```

```python
amount = 1
price = 10
basecurrency = "ltc"
def main():
    message = "symbol=" + basecurrency + "&amount='" + str(amount) + "'&price='" + str(price) + "'&side=buy" + "&type=limit"
    id = exchange.IO("api", "POST", "/v1/order/new", message)
```

```rust
fn main() {
    let amount = 1;
    let price = 10;
    let basecurrency = "ltc";
    // Note that there is a ' character on both the left and right sides of the amount and price parameter values
    let message = format!("symbol={}&amount='{}'&price='{}'&side=buy&type=limit", basecurrency, amount, price);
    let id = exchange.IO(("api", "POST", "/v1/order/new", message));
}
```

The ```resource``` parameter supports passing in a complete URL.

```javascript
function main() {
    var ret = exchange.IO("api", "GET", "https://www.okx.com/api/v5/account/max-withdrawal", "ccy=BTC")
    Log(ret)
}
```

```python
def main():
    ret = exchange.IO("api", "GET", "https://www.okx.com/api/v5/account/max-withdrawal", "ccy=BTC")
    Log(ret)
```

```rust
fn main() {
    let ret = exchange.IO(("api", "GET", "https://www.okx.com/api/v5/account/max-withdrawal", "ccy=BTC"));
    Log!(ret);
}
```

A GET request that does not use the ```raw``` parameter.

```javascript
function main(){
    var ret = exchange.IO("api", "GET", "/api/v5/trade/orders-pending", "instType=SPOT")
    Log(ret)
}
```

```python
def main():
    ret = exchange.IO("api", "GET", "/api/v5/trade/orders-pending", "instType=SPOT")
    Log(ret)
```

```rust
fn main() {
    let ret = exchange.IO(("api", "GET", "/api/v5/trade/orders-pending", "instType=SPOT"));
    Log!(ret);
}
```

##### Directly Calling Exchange APIs (```api``` mode)

```javascript

exchange.IO("api", httpMethod, resource, params, raw)

```

Used to call the exchange's native API endpoints that are not wrapped by FMZ. FMZ automatically handles signature verification; you only need to fill in the request parameters.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
| httpMethod | string | Yes | ```GET```, ```POST```, etc. |
| resource | string | Yes | Request path or full URL |
| params | string | No | Request parameters in URL-encoded format |
| raw | string | No | Raw request body (JSON, etc.) |

Returns a null value on failure, and this mode is only supported in live trading.

See also: `exchange.IO`

#### exchange.IO("currency", ...)

```
exchange.IO(k, symbol)
```

Forms:

- `exchange.IO("currency", ...)`

Switches the current trading pair of the exchange object at runtime.

Parameters:

- `k` (string, required): Selects the ```exchange.IO()``` feature; ```currency``` switches the trading pair.
- `symbol` (string, required): Trading pair, upper case and underscore-separated, e.g. ```ETH_USDT```.

Returns (bool / null value): Returns ```true``` on success; returns a null value if the trading pair format is invalid, and the current trading pair stays unchanged.

Switch trading pair at runtime.

```javascript
function main() {
    // For example, when the live bot starts, the exchange object's current trading pair is BTC_USDT; print the ticker of the current trading pair
    Log(exchange.GetTicker())
    // Switch the trading pair to LTC_BTC
    exchange.IO("currency", "LTC_BTC")
    Log(exchange.GetTicker())
}
```

```python
def main():
    Log(exchange.GetTicker())
    exchange.IO("currency", "LTC_BTC")
    Log(exchange.GetTicker())
```

```rust
fn main() {
    // For example, when the live bot starts, the exchange object's current trading pair is BTC_USDT; print the ticker of the current trading pair
    Log!(exchange.GetTicker(None));
    // Switch the trading pair to LTC_BTC
    let _ = exchange.IO(("currency", "LTC_BTC"));
    Log!(exchange.GetTicker(None));
}
```

##### Switching Trading Pairs at Runtime (```currency``` mode)

```javascript

exchange.IO("currency", "ETH_USDT")

```

Used to dynamically switch trading pairs at runtime. The trading pair format is uppercase letters separated by an underscore. This instruction is equivalent to `exchange.SetCurrency`.

> In backtesting mode, only spot is supported, and you can only switch to a trading pair with the same quote currency. For futures, the contract code is kept after switching the trading pair; call ```exchange.SetContractType()``` when you need a different contract.

See also: `exchange.IO`

#### exchange.IO("base", ...)

```
exchange.IO(k)
exchange.IO(k, address)
```

Forms:

- `exchange.IO("base", ...)`

Queries or switches the base address of the exchange API. On a Web3 exchange object it sets the RPC node address, see `exchange.IO("base", ...)`.

Parameters:

- `k` (string, required): Selects the ```exchange.IO()``` feature; ```base``` queries or switches the API base address.
- `address` (string, optional): New base address, e.g. ```https://api.example.com```. When omitted, the current base address is queried.

Returns (string / null value): Without ```address```, returns the current base address; with ```address```, switches the base address and returns the base address before the switch. Returns a null value on failure.

Switch the exchange API base address.

```javascript
function main () {
    // exchanges[0] is the first exchange object added when the live trading was created
    var old = exchanges[0].IO("base", "https://api.huobi.pro")
    Log("Base address before:", old, "current base address:", exchanges[0].IO("base"))
}
```

```python
def main():
    old = exchanges[0].IO("base", "https://api.huobi.pro")
    Log("Base address before:", old, "current base address:", exchanges[0].IO("base"))
```

```rust
fn main() {
    // exchanges[0] is the first exchange object added when the live trading was created
    let old = exchanges[0].IO(("base", "https://api.huobi.pro"));
    Log!("Base address before:", old, "current base address:", exchanges[0].IO("base"));
}
```

##### Querying and switching the base address (```base``` mode)

- ```exchange.IO("base", address)```: switches the exchange API base address, equivalent to `exchange.SetBase`.
- ```exchange.IO("base")```: queries the current base address; if it has never been switched, the exchange's default API address is returned. Equivalent to `exchange.GetBase`.

A few exchanges have separate base address commands (for example for coin-margined contracts, options or the market data API); see the IO command table of the exchange page (all exchanges are listed in `Capability Matrix`).

See also: `exchange.IO`, `exchange.SetBase`, `exchange.GetBase`

#### exchange.IO(mode, value)

```
exchange.IO(mode)
exchange.IO(mode, value)
```

Forms:

- `exchange.IO(mode, value)`

Switches the trading mode of an exchange, including demo/live trading, cross/isolated margin, hedge/one-way position mode, unified account, margin trading mode and self-trade prevention.

Parameters:

- `mode` (string, required): The command, e.g. ```simulate```, ```cross```, ```dual```. See the table below for the full list of commands.
- `value` (bool / string, optional): The value for the command. Its type and meaning are given in the table below. Some commands do not take this parameter.

Returns (string / number / bool / object / array / any): The return value depends on the command. Some commands (e.g. ```cross``` and ```dual``` on certain exchanges) return a null value even when the call succeeds. On failure, a null value is returned, and the error message can be retrieved with `GetLastError`.

Switch between demo and live trading environments (using ```Futures_OKCoin``` (OKX Futures) as an example).

```javascript
function main() {
    exchange.IO("simulate", true)    // Switch to demo trading environment
    // ... trading logic ...
    exchange.IO("simulate", false)   // Switch back to live trading environment
}
```

```python
def main():
    exchange.IO("simulate", True)
    # ... trading logic ...
    exchange.IO("simulate", False)
```

```rust
fn main() {
    let _ = exchange.IO(("simulate", true));    // Switch to demo trading environment
    // ... trading logic ...
    let _ = exchange.IO(("simulate", false));   // Switch back to live trading environment
}
```

Switch the margin mode and position mode of contracts (using Binance Futures as an example).

```javascript
function main() {
    exchange.IO("dual", true)    // Switch to hedge mode (dual position)
    exchange.IO("dual", false)   // Switch to one-way mode

    exchange.SetContractType("swap")
    exchange.IO("cross", true)    // Switch to cross margin
    exchange.IO("cross", false)   // Switch to isolated margin
}
```

```python
def main():
    exchange.IO("dual", True)
    exchange.IO("dual", False)

    exchange.SetContractType("swap")
    exchange.IO("cross", True)
    exchange.IO("cross", False)
```

```rust
fn main() {
    let _ = exchange.IO(("dual", true));    // Switch to hedge mode (dual position)
    let _ = exchange.IO(("dual", false));   // Switch to one-way mode

    let _ = exchange.SetContractType("swap");
    let _ = exchange.IO(("cross", true));    // Switch to cross margin
    let _ = exchange.IO(("cross", false));   // Switch to isolated margin
}
```

Switch unified account mode (using Binance Futures as an example).

```javascript
function main() {
    exchange.IO("unified", true)   // Switch to unified account mode
    exchange.IO("unified", false)  // Switch to normal mode
}
```

```python
def main():
    exchange.IO("unified", True)
    exchange.IO("unified", False)
```

```rust
fn main() {
    let _ = exchange.IO(("unified", true));   // Switch to unified account mode
    let _ = exchange.IO(("unified", false));  // Switch to normal mode
}
```

Set the self-trade prevention (STP) mode (using Binance as an example).

```javascript
function main() {
    // "NONE" means disable STP mode, other parameters: "EXPIRE_TAKER", "EXPIRE_MAKER", "EXPIRE_BOTH"
    exchange.IO("selfTradePreventionMode", "NONE")
}
```

```python
    exchange.IO("selfTradePreventionMode", "NONE")
```

```rust

    // "NONE" means disable STP mode, other parameters: "EXPIRE_TAKER", "EXPIRE_MAKER", "EXPIRE_BOTH"
    let _ = exchange.IO(("selfTradePreventionMode", "NONE"));
}
```

##### General Trading Mode Commands

The following commands are shared by multiple exchanges. For which commands each exchange supports, see the `capability matrix`. For differences in value meaning, whether a command applies per contract, and return values, see the page for each exchange.

| Command | Parameter | Function |
| - | - | - |
| ```simulate``` | bool | Demo trading (true) / live trading (false). It is recommended to tick "Demo trading" when adding the exchange; this command is kept only for compatibility with legacy strategies |
| ```cross``` | bool | Cross margin (true) / isolated margin (false) |
| ```dual``` | bool | Hedge mode (true) / one-way mode (false) |
| ```unified``` | bool | Unified account (true) / normal account (false) |
| ```trade_margin``` | None | Switch to isolated margin trading mode |
| ```trade_super_margin``` | None | Switch to cross margin trading mode |
| ```trade_normal``` | None | Switch back to normal spot mode |
| ```selfTradePreventionMode``` | string | Self-trade prevention (STP) mode |

##### Demo Trading

Exchanges that support demo trading offer a "Demo trading" checkbox in their configuration when added. Once ticked, the exchange object connects to the demo environment (testnet) from startup, and the strategy does not need to switch. Supported exchanges include: Binance Spot and Futures, Bybit Spot and Futures, OKX Spot and Futures, Bitget Spot and Futures, Gate.io Spot and Futures, Futures_DigiFinex, Hyperliquid Spot and Futures (testnet), Futures_Lighter, and Futu (paper trading account).

```exchange.IO("simulate", true/false)``` can still switch between demo and live trading at runtime for compatibility with legacy strategies (see the support tables for each command below for supported exchanges); new strategies should rely on the checkbox set when adding the exchange. The DigiFinex spot exchange itself does not provide a demo environment.

See also: `exchange.IO`

#### exchange.IO("rate", ...)

```
exchange.IO(k, functionNames, maxCalls, period)
exchange.IO(k, functionNames, maxCalls, period, behavior)
```

Forms:

- `exchange.IO("rate", ...)`

Limits how often each API function is called: ```rate``` for smoothed limiting, ```quota``` for quota limiting.

Parameters:

- `k` (string, required): Selects the function of ```exchange.IO()```: ```rate``` is smooth rate limiting (a token bucket that allows short bursts), ```quota``` is quota limiting (calls counted per time window, windows aligned to the clock).
- `functionNames` (string, required): API function name (such as ```GetTicker```, ```CreateOrder```, ```GetAccount```); several names separated by commas share one rule. ```*``` is the fallback rule and applies only to functions without a rule of their own; ```IO/api``` stands for ```exchange.IO("api", ...)```. An empty string clears all rules.
- `maxCalls` (number, required): Maximum number of calls per period; a value of 0 or less deletes the rule for ```functionNames```. In ```rate``` mode it can be the string ```"count/burst"```, for example ```"10/5"```: 10 calls per period with bursts of at most 5; without a burst the burst equals the count.
- `period` (string, required): Period, written like a Go duration: ```500ms```, ```1s```, ```1m```, ```1h30m``` (units ns, us, ms, s, m, h), or ```1d```; or a daily reset time ```@HHMM``` / ```@HHMMSS``` (Beijing time), for example ```@0815```.
- `behavior` (string, optional): Decides what happens over the limit: ```delay``` waits and then runs; by default the call returns a null value.

Returns (string / number / bool / object / array / any): Returns the result of the command on success, or a null value on failure.

rate mode rate limiting - Limit GetTicker to a maximum of 10 calls per second; returns null when the limit is exceeded.

```javascript
function main() {
    exchange.IO("rate", "GetTicker", 10, "1s")

    for (var i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
        var ticker = exchange.GetTicker("BTC_USDT")
        if (ticker) {
            Log("Ticker:", ticker.Last)
        } else {
            Log("Rate limit exceeded")
        }
    }
}
```

```python
def main():
    exchange.IO("rate", "GetTicker", 10, "1s")

    for i in range(20):
        ticker = exchange.GetTicker("BTC_USDT")
        if ticker:
            Log("Ticker:", ticker["Last"])
        else:
            Log("Rate limit exceeded")
```

```rust
fn main() {
    let _ = exchange.IO(("rate", "GetTicker", 10, "1s"));

    for _i in 0..20 {
        // GetTicker returns Err when the limit is exceeded
        match exchange.GetTicker("BTC_USDT") {
            Ok(ticker) => Log!("Ticker:", ticker.Last),
            Err(_) => Log!("Rate limit exceeded"),
        }
    }
}
```

```javascript
        Log("Call", i+1, "Ticker:", ticker.Last)

}
```

quota mode - strict rate limiting aligned to time windows.

```javascript

}
```

```rust
            Ok(ticker) => Log!(_D(None), "Ticker:", ticker.Last),
```

quota mode - intraday quota, resets daily at the specified time.

```javascript
function main() {
    exchange.IO("quota", "GetTicker", 1000, "@0815")

    var count = 0
    while (true) {
        var ticker = exchange.GetTicker("BTC_USDT")
        if (ticker) {
            count++
            Log("Call count:", count, "Ticker:", ticker.Last)
        } else {
            Log("Daily quota exceeded, waiting for reset at 08:15")
            Sleep(60000)  // Wait 1 minute
        }
        Sleep(1000)
    }
}
```

```python
def main():
    exchange.IO("quota", "GetTicker", 1000, "@0815")

    count = 0
    while True:
        ticker = exchange.GetTicker("BTC_USDT")
        if ticker:
            count += 1
            Log("Call count:", count, "Ticker:", ticker["Last"])
        else:
            Log("Daily quota exceeded, waiting for reset at 08:15")
            Sleep(60000)  # Wait 1 minute
        Sleep(1000)
```

```rust
fn main() {
    let _ = exchange.IO(("quota", "GetTicker", 1000, "@0815"));

    let mut count = 0;
    loop {
        match exchange.GetTicker("BTC_USDT") {
            Ok(ticker) => {
                count += 1;
                Log!("Call count:", count, "Ticker:", ticker.Last);
            }
            Err(_) => {
                Log!("Daily quota exceeded, waiting for reset at 08:15");
                Sleep(60000);  // Wait 1 minute
            }
        }
        Sleep(1000);
    }
}
```
