##### Exchange-specific IO Commands

###### ```WOO``` (Spot)

| Command | Arguments | Description |
| - | - | - |
| ```trade_margin``` | — | Switches the account to margin mode (MARGIN) by sending a settings request to the exchange (```POST /v1/client/account_mode```); returns ```true``` once the exchange confirms. This is an account-level setting. |
| ```trade_normal``` | — | Switches the account to pure spot mode (PURE_SPOT) by sending a settings request to the exchange; returns ```true``` once the exchange confirms. This is an account-level setting. |
| ```api``` | method, path[, params[, raw]] | Call a WOO X endpoint directly; ```path``` may be a full URL. (more below the table) |

The rest of the longer descriptions in the table:

- ```api```: The signing rule follows ```/v1/``` or ```/v3/``` in the path; ```GET``` parameters go into the query string, other methods send a form body for v1 and a JSON body for v3. Paths containing ```/public/``` are unsigned by default and all others signed; the sign argument can set it explicitly, and unsigned requests are also sent with the given HTTP method. ```raw``` is not a request body but a parameter table (a JSON object) that replaces ```params``` entirely when non-empty and is signed as usual; for v3 JSON bodies its object, array, number and boolean values are kept as they are. Spot and futures behave the same for this command. Returns: The whole exchange response (```data``` is not unwrapped for either v1 or v3 endpoints); an error is raised when the response ```success``` is not ```true```.

For the common commands ```base``` and ```currency``` see `exchange.IO`.

###### ```Futures_WOO``` (Futures)

| Command | Arguments | Description |
| - | - | - |
| ```cross``` | bool | Cross (true) / isolated (false) margin. Only changes the local setting without sending a request; subsequent orders, conditional orders and ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()``` carry it. Cross margin by default. |
| ```dual``` | bool | Hedge (true) / one-way (false) position mode, sent to the exchange (```POST /v1/client/position_mode```); after it succeeds the connector places orders for hedge mode (both regular and conditional orders carry the position side). |
| ```api``` | method, path[, params[, raw]] | Call a WOO X endpoint directly; ```path``` may be a full URL. (more below the table) |

The rest of the longer descriptions in the table:

- ```api```: The signing rule follows ```/v1/``` or ```/v3/``` in the path; ```GET``` parameters go into the query string, other methods send a form body for v1 and a JSON body for v3. Paths containing ```/public/``` are unsigned by default and all others signed; the sign argument can set it explicitly, and unsigned requests are also sent with the given HTTP method. ```raw``` is not a request body but a parameter table (a JSON object) that replaces ```params``` entirely when non-empty and is signed as usual; for v3 JSON bodies its object, array, number and boolean values are kept as they are. Spot and futures behave the same for this command. Returns: The whole exchange response (```data``` is not unwrapped for either v1 or v3 endpoints); an error is raised when the response ```success``` is not ```true```.

For the common commands ```base``` and ```currency``` see `exchange.IO`.

##### Function Support

###### All exchange objects

Not supported (the call fails with an error and returns null): `exchange.GetTickers`.

###### ```WOO``` (Spot)

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: Native periods are 1m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 4h, 12h, 1d, 1w, 1M; other periods are synthesized by the docker.

###### ```Futures_WOO``` (Futures)

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: Native periods are 1m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 4h, 12h, 1d, 1w, 1M, 1y; other periods are synthesized by the docker.

##### Margin, Account and Simulation

###### ```Futures_WOO``` (Futures)

Margin mode: Choose cross/isolated margin with ```exchange.IO("cross", bool)```; it is a local setting carried with every order (cross by default). ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()``` sets leverage per contract and carries the current cross/isolated setting.

Position mode: Switch hedge/one-way mode with ```exchange.IO("dual", bool)```. The connector does not detect the account's position mode: if the account is already in hedge mode, call ```exchange.IO("dual", true)``` at the start of every run, otherwise orders lack the position side and are rejected by the exchange. In hedge mode ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()``` sets the same leverage on both the long and the short side in one call (it fails if either side fails, and the error names the side that was already set), regardless of the direction set by ```exchange.SetDirection()```; in one-way mode it is set once.

##### Notes

###### All exchange objects

- ```exchange.ModifyOrder()``` modifies the price and amount in place, keeping the order ID.

###### ```WOO``` (Spot)

- The amount of a market buy order is the quote-currency amount to spend (WOO X's ```order_amount```); a market sell order is in the base currency. When queried, both ```Amount``` and ```DealAmount``` of a regular market buy order are the filled base-currency quantity.
- WOO X spot has no 24-hour ticker endpoint; ```exchange.GetTicker()``` is built from the latest 24 one-hour K-lines (open, high, low, volume) and the order book (best bid and ask), requesting two endpoints per call.
- Conditional orders support take-profit, stop-loss and OCO; ```exchange.ModifyConditionOrder()``` can modify take-profit and stop-loss orders only, not OCO conditional orders.
- ```exchange.GetConditionOrders()``` queries one trading pair only: when omitted or empty it queries the current trading pair.
- ```exchange.GetHistoryOrders()``` and ```exchange.GetHistoryConditionOrders()``` query one trading pair only: without ```symbol``` they query the current trading pair, and an empty string fails.
- WebSocket push is supported: market data (ticker, bbo, depth, trades, klines) and the private stream (order updates and balances) can be subscribed through the event stream. ```exchange.GetTicker()```, ```exchange.GetDepth()``` and the other functions still request the REST API directly, and ```EventLoop()``` does not subscribe to this exchange's push streams by itself. The market data connection URL carries the configured ApplicationId (without one, the URL without an ApplicationId is used). The ticker push takes its best bid/ask prices and sizes from the pair's best bid/ask stream (WOO X's 24h ticker stream has no bid/ask) and starts once both streams have arrived; its volume is the aggregated volume, the same as ```exchange.GetTicker()```. Trades carry no exchange trade IDs and use the same synthesized IDs as ```exchange.GetTrades()``` (when several trades share the same millisecond, side, price and amount, ```exchange.GetTrades()``` appends a sequence number to the ID; the push does not). Depth subscriptions go up to 100 levels (20 by default) and are synchronized from a snapshot of the same endpoint as ```exchange.GetDepth()``` plus updates chained by the previous update's timestamp; a broken chain fetches a new snapshot automatically. WOO X only pushes when the book changes, so a snapshot is pushed first once the subscription is active. Kline periods are 1 minute, 5, 15 and 30 minutes, 1 hour, 4 hours, 12 hours, 1 day, 1 week and 1 month, and a first kline subscription pushes 500 historical bars first; the exchange's kline push has no closed flag, so a bar counts as closed when it is pushed after its end time or when the next bar starts. The private stream is one ```private``` subscription for the whole account (no symbol); it needs the ApplicationId and connects and logs in only when subscribed: once the subscription is active (and again after every reconnect) it first pushes a snapshot of all balances from the same endpoint as ```exchange.GetAssets()```, then reports ready, and afterwards pushes spot order updates (all pairs; conditional orders themselves are not pushed, the orders they place when triggered are). Balance pushes only signal a change: each one triggers a re-query through ```exchange.GetAssets()``` and only the changed currencies are pushed. Spot has no positions, so the private stream pushes none. A rejected signature reports a degraded connection status and a failed private stream (market data push is unaffected). A market-wide ```tickers``` subscription (no symbol) uses WOO's all-market 24-hour ticker stream together with its all-market best bid/ask stream: once a second it pushes every spot pair with the last price, the 24-hour open/high/low, the volume (same as the ticker) and the best bid/ask.

###### ```Futures_WOO``` (Futures)

- Conditional orders support take-profit, stop-loss and OCO, with the trigger price type fixed to ```MARKET_PRICE```; ```exchange.ModifyConditionOrder()``` can modify take-profit and stop-loss orders only (trigger price, order price and amount, keeping the order ID), not OCO conditional orders.
- The ```Rate``` of ```exchange.GetFundings()``` is the exchange's estimated funding rate for the next settlement and ```Time``` is the next settlement time; batch queries are supported.
- In ```exchange.GetPositions()```, ```Profit``` is computed as (mark price − average open price) × position size and ```Margin``` is estimated as average open price × position size ÷ leverage; the position's margin mode is the ```marginMode``` in the exchange's position data (one account can hold both cross and isolated positions), independent of the local ```exchange.IO("cross", bool)``` order setting.
- Like the open-order queries, ```exchange.GetHistoryOrders()``` and ```exchange.GetHistoryConditionOrders()``` accept ranges such as ```USDT.swap```: the exchange is queried without a trading pair and the results are filtered by the range, with ```limit``` counting only orders inside the range.
- WebSocket push is supported: market data (ticker, bbo, depth, trades, klines) and the private stream (order updates, positions and balances) can be subscribed through the event stream. ```exchange.GetTicker()```, ```exchange.GetDepth()``` and the other functions still request the REST API directly, and ```EventLoop()``` does not subscribe to this exchange's push streams by itself. The market data connection URL carries the configured ApplicationId (without one, the URL without an ApplicationId is used). The ticker push takes its best bid/ask prices and sizes from the contract's best bid/ask stream (WOO X's 24h ticker stream has no bid/ask) and starts once both streams have arrived; its volume is the exchange's 24h volume, the same as ```exchange.GetTicker()```, and it carries no open interest. Trades carry no exchange trade IDs and use the same synthesized IDs as ```exchange.GetTrades()``` (when several trades share the same millisecond, side, price and amount, ```exchange.GetTrades()``` appends a sequence number to the ID; the push does not). Depth subscriptions go up to 100 levels (20 by default) and are synchronized from a snapshot of the same endpoint as ```exchange.GetDepth()``` plus updates chained by the previous update's timestamp; a broken chain fetches a new snapshot automatically. WOO X only pushes when the book changes, so a snapshot is pushed first once the subscription is active. Kline periods are 1 minute, 5, 15 and 30 minutes, 1 hour, 4 hours, 12 hours, 1 day, 1 week and 1 month (the 1-year period is not available for push), and a first kline subscription pushes 500 historical bars first; the exchange's kline push has no closed flag, so a bar counts as closed when it is pushed after its end time or when the next bar starts. The private stream is one ```private``` subscription for the whole account (no symbol); it needs the ApplicationId and connects and logs in only when subscribed: once the subscription is active (and again after every reconnect) it first pushes a snapshot of all balances and positions from the same endpoints as ```exchange.GetAssets()``` and ```exchange.GetPositions()```, then reports ready, and afterwards pushes perpetual order updates (all contracts; conditional orders themselves are not pushed, the orders they place when triggered are) and position changes (each one the full position of that contract, with profit and margin computed the same way as ```exchange.GetPositions()```; the push carries no liquidation price). Balance pushes only signal a change: each one triggers a re-query through ```exchange.GetAssets()``` and only the changed currencies are pushed. A rejected signature reports a degraded connection status and a failed private stream (market data push is unaffected). A market-wide ```tickers``` subscription (no symbol) uses WOO's all-market 24-hour ticker stream together with its all-market best bid/ask stream: once a second it pushes every perpetual with the last price, the 24-hour open/high/low, the volume (same as the ticker; no open interest) and the best bid/ask.

#### Zaif

Spot trading on the Japanese exchange Zaif (API address ```https://api.zaif.jp```). It uses REST only, with no market-data or order push. Private endpoints (```/tapi```) are signed with a Zaif API key (Access Key and Secret Key). The exchange has no K-line or all-market ticker endpoint, supports GTC limit orders only, and does not support conditional orders or order amendment.

##### Names and Configuration

```exchange.GetName()```: ```Zaif``` (Spot).

| Field | Required |
| - | - |
| Access Key | Yes |
| Secret Key | Yes |

##### Trading Pairs and Contract Codes

Pair examples: ```BTC_JPY```, ```ETH_JPY```

Trading pairs are written ```BASE_QUOTE```, matching the Zaif native code ```btc_jpy```. For pairs whose currency names contain ```.``` (such as the native ```polygon.mv_jpy```), write the ```.``` in the currency name as ```-```: ```POLYGON-MV_JPY```; ```exchange.GetMarkets()``` and the account assets return currency names in the same form.

##### Function Support

Not supported (the call fails with an error and returns null): `exchange.GetTickers`, `exchange.ModifyOrder`, `exchange.CreateConditionOrder`, `exchange.ModifyConditionOrder`, `exchange.CancelConditionOrder`, `exchange.GetConditionOrder`, `exchange.GetConditionOrders`, `exchange.GetHistoryConditionOrders`.

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: The exchange has no K-line endpoint; bars are synthesized by the docker from trades. The first call covers only the few bars spanned by recent trades, and more accumulate with later calls.
- `exchange.GetOrder`: The exchange has no single-order query interface, so the order is looked up among the current open orders and the historical orders. The historical orders are rebuilt from trade records whose ```Id``` is not guaranteed to equal the order ID, so a completed order may not be found.

##### Notes

- Market orders are not supported, only GTC limit orders: a ```tif``` of ```ioc``` or ```fok```, or ```postOnly```, fails.
- Without the ```symbol``` argument, ```exchange.GetOrders()``` queries the current trading pair only. The returned open orders carry no fill information, so ```DealAmount``` is 0.
- Zaif has no order history endpoint, so ```exchange.GetHistoryOrders()``` is rebuilt from the trade history (```trade_history```): each trade is returned as a filled order, with ```Price``` and ```AvgPrice``` set to that trade's price, ```Amount``` and ```DealAmount``` set to that trade's amount, and ```Type``` set to this account's side in the trade (the trade's aggressor side for self-trades). Trade records carry no order ID, so an order filled in several trades shows up as several rows that cannot be merged; ```Id``` is the trade record's number and is not guaranteed to equal the order ID returned when the order was placed; orders cancelled without any fill never appear, and an order cancelled after a partial fill shows only the filled part. Without ```limit```, at most 100 rows are returned; ```since``` is passed to the exchange with second precision, and with it the earliest records after that time are returned, without it the most recent ones. Without ```symbol```, regular pairs and token pairs (the exchange's ```is_token```) are queried once each and merged; the exchange allows at most 12 calls to this endpoint per 60 seconds.
- ```exchange.GetTicker()``` has no opening price (```Open``` is 0), and the exchange gives no ticker time, so ```Time``` is the local time.

### Decentralized Exchanges (DEX)

On-chain order-book exchanges and swap aggregators; transactions are signed with the configured wallet or key.

#### Order-book Perpetuals

Perpetual exchanges with an on-chain order book: `Hyperliquid`, `Lighter`, `edgeX`, `Aster`, `Aevo`, `Pendle`, `WOOFi Pro`.

#### Swaps and Aggregators

AMM pools and swap aggregators, mapping on-chain swaps onto the spot trading functions: `Uniswap / PancakeSwap`, `Aerodrome / Velodrome`, `KyberSwap`, `1inch`, `Jupiter`, `OKX DEX`.

IO command sub-pages shared by several exchanges: `EVM DEX Common Commands` (`Uniswap / PancakeSwap`, `Aerodrome / Velodrome`, `KyberSwap`, `1inch`).

See also: `DEX Strategy Examples`.

#### Hyperliquid

```Hyperliquid``` (Spot): The spot market of the Hyperliquid on-chain order book. Market data and account queries need only the wallet address; placing, canceling and amending orders are signed (EIP-712) with the API wallet (agent wallet) private key and need no on-chain gas. Perpetuals and HIP-3 / HIP-4 (Outcome) instruments are served by the Futures_Hyperliquid exchange object.

```Futures_Hyperliquid``` (Futures): USDC-margined perpetuals on the Hyperliquid on-chain order book: perpetuals of the main dex, HIP-3 perpetuals (on builder-deployed dexes, codes carry a ```dex:``` prefix) and HIP-4 Outcome (prediction) instruments. Market data and account queries need only the wallet address; orders, cancels, amendments and leverage changes are signed (EIP-712) with the API wallet (agent wallet) private key and need no on-chain gas. Spot is served by the Hyperliquid exchange object.

See the [Hyperliquid guide](https://www.fmz.com/digest-topic/10574).

##### Names and Configuration

| ```exchange.GetName()``` | Type | Aliases |
| - | - | - |
| ```Hyperliquid``` | Spot | — |
| ```Futures_Hyperliquid``` | Futures | HIP-3, HIP-4 |

✓ marks the exchange objects that have the field.

| Field | ```Hyperliquid``` | ```Futures_Hyperliquid``` | Required | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| Wallet Address | ✓ | ✓ | Yes | — | The main account wallet address (starting with ```0x```), used as the ```user``` of every query other than market data. |
| Wallet Private Key | ✓ | ✓ | No | — | The main account private key, optional. Used only to sign transfer actions (```usdSend```, ```withdraw3``` and so on sent with ```exchange.IO("api", "POST", "/exchange", ...)```); not needed for trading. |
| API Wallet Private Key | ✓ |  | Yes | — | The private key of an API wallet (agent wallet) created on the Hyperliquid "API" page, used to sign orders, cancels and amendments. Without it only market data and account queries work. |
| Simulate (testnet) | ✓ | ✓ | No | Unchecked | Use the Hyperliquid testnet when checked; the API address becomes ```https://api.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz``` and trading and transfer actions are signed for the testnet (```source``` is ```b```). A configured node address is still used; the signing network follows the checkbox. |
| API Wallet Private Key |  | ✓ | Yes | — | The private key of an API wallet (agent wallet) created on the Hyperliquid "API" page, used to sign orders, cancels, amendments and leverage changes. Without it only market data and account queries work. |

##### Trading Pairs and Contract Codes

###### ```Hyperliquid``` (Spot)

Pair examples: ```HYPE_USDC```, ```PURR_USDC```

Pairs are written as ```COIN_QUOTE```, using Hyperliquid spot token names (for example ```HYPE```, ```PURR```; bridged assets use the exchange's token name, such as ```UBTC```), case-insensitive. The exchange's internal pair names such as ```@1``` and ```@2``` are resolved by the connector from the spot metadata and need not be used directly.

###### ```Futures_Hyperliquid``` (Futures)

Pair examples: ```BTC_USD```, ```xyz:XYZ100_USD```, ```BTC-above-100k---Dec_USD```

Perpetual pairs are written as ```COIN_USD``` (```COIN_USDC``` is accepted too; returned symbols always use ```USD```), with USDC as margin, for example ```BTC_USD.swap```. The connector restores the coin's case from the exchange's instrument list (such as ```kPEPE```). HIP-3 pairs carry a dex prefix, kept lowercase, for example ```xyz:XYZ100_USD.swap```.

A HIP-4 Outcome pair is the market name (spaces and ```/``` replaced by ```-```) plus ```_USD```, and the contract code is the name of the outcome side, for example ```BTC-above-100k---Dec_USD.Yes```; when several markets share a name, ```-<market id>``` is appended to tell them apart (such as ```Recurring-1399_USD.Yes```), and the bare name fails as ambiguous. ```exchange.GetMarkets()``` lists the available Outcome codes.

| Contract code | Description |
| - | - |
| ```swap``` | Perpetual contract; the main dex and HIP-3 instruments are perpetual only. |

There are no delivery contracts. The contract code of an Outcome instrument is the outcome side name (such as ```Yes```, ```No```), not ```swap```.

##### Exchange-specific IO Commands

###### ```Hyperliquid``` (Spot)

| Command | Arguments | Description | Returns |
| - | - | - | - |
| ```walletAddress``` | address | Set the address used by read-only queries (assets, orders, order history), so another address's assets can be queried; the wallet that signs orders is unchanged. To query your own account again, pass the configured wallet address. | The address set. |
| ```vaultAddress``` | address | Place, cancel and amend orders on behalf of a vault or sub-account (the address goes into the signature and the request body); an empty string clears it. Queries still use the wallet address; to query the vault's assets and orders, also set ```walletAddress``` to the vault address. | The address set. |
| ```expiresAfter``` | timestamp | Set the ```expiresAfter``` carried by all subsequent signed actions (orders, cancels, amendments, ...), a Unix timestamp in milliseconds after which the exchange rejects the action; 0 clears it (the default). The value stays in effect, so every action after that time is rejected until it is set again or reset to 0. | The value set. |
| ```source``` | "a" \| "b" | The network used for signing: ```a``` is mainnet (the default; ```b``` when the Simulate (testnet) box is checked), ```b``` is testnet. (more below the table) | The value set. |
| ```api``` | method, path[, params[, body]] | Call a Hyperliquid endpoint directly. (more below the table) | The raw exchange response. |

The rest of the longer descriptions in the table:

- ```source```: It sets the ```source``` field of the Agent signature of trading actions and the chainId of the EIP-712 signature of transfer actions (```usdSend```, ```spotSend```, ```withdraw3```, ...): Arbitrum 42161 on mainnet, Arbitrum Sepolia 421614 on testnet. The API address is not changed; to connect to the testnet also switch it with ```exchange.IO("base", "https://api.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz")```.
- ```api```: A ```POST``` to ```/exchange``` takes an action object, and the connector adds the nonce and signs it; transfer actions (```usdSend```, ```spotSend```, ```withdraw3```, ```usdClassTransfer```, ```approveAgent```, ```approveBuilderFee```, ```userSetAbstraction```) are signed with the wallet private key ```WalletPrivateKey```, and fields such as ```hyperliquidChain``` must be filled in by the caller; other actions are signed with the API wallet private key. Other paths (such as ```POST /info```) are sent as they are, unsigned. ```body``` (a JSON object or a JSON string), when given, is the request body (the action for ```/exchange```); otherwise ```params``` is used as the body; a ```body``` of any other type is an error.

For the common commands ```base``` and ```currency``` see `exchange.IO`.

###### ```Futures_Hyperliquid``` (Futures)

| Command | Arguments | Description | Returns |
| - | - | - | - |
| ```cross``` | bool | Cross (true, the default) / isolated (false) margin. Only recorded by the connector, not per contract, and submitted together with the leverage on the next ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()``` call for any contract; the command itself sends no request. | ```cross``` or ```isolated```. |
| ```dex``` | name | Set the default HIP-3 dex name (without ```:```, such as ```xyz```; list the names with ```exchange.IO("api", "POST", "/info", {type: "perpDexs"})```). (more below the table) | The dex name set (an empty string when cleared). |
| ```walletAddress``` | address | Set the address used by read-only queries (account, positions, orders), so another address's positions can be queried; the wallet that signs orders is unchanged. To query your own account again, pass the configured wallet address. | The address set. |
| ```vaultAddress``` | address | Place, cancel and amend orders and set leverage on behalf of a vault or sub-account (the address goes into the signature and the request body); an empty string clears it. Queries still use the wallet address; to query the vault's account and positions, also set ```walletAddress``` to the vault address. | The address set. |
| ```expiresAfter``` | timestamp | Set the ```expiresAfter``` carried by all subsequent signed actions (orders, cancels, amendments, leverage changes, ...), a Unix timestamp in milliseconds after which the exchange rejects the action; 0 clears it (the default). The value stays in effect, so every action after that time is rejected until it is set again or reset to 0. | The value set. |
| ```source``` | "a" \| "b" | The network used for signing: ```a``` is mainnet (the default; ```b``` when the Simulate (testnet) box is checked), ```b``` is testnet. (more below the table) | The value set. |
| ```split``` | symbol, amount | HIP-4 Outcome split (the ```splitOutcome``` action) of ```amount``` for the Outcome that ```symbol``` belongs to, into positions on each outcome side. (more below the table) | The raw exchange response (```status``` is ```ok```). |
| ```merge``` | symbol[, amount] | HIP-4 Outcome merge (the ```mergeOutcome``` action) of the positions on each side of the Outcome that ```symbol``` belongs to; ```amount``` is optional, and when omitted or not above 0 the request carries no amount. | The raw exchange response (```status``` is ```ok```). |
| ```mergeQuestion``` | symbol[, amount] | HIP-4 merge by question (the ```mergeQuestion``` action) for the question that the Outcome of ```symbol``` belongs to; ```amount``` is optional (when omitted or not above 0 the request carries no amount). Fails if the Outcome belongs to no question. | The raw exchange response (```status``` is ```ok```). |
| ```negate``` | symbol, amount | HIP-4 negation (the ```negateOutcome``` action) of the Outcome of ```symbol``` within its question; ```amount``` must be greater than 0. Fails if the Outcome belongs to no question. | The raw exchange response (```status``` is ```ok```). |
| ```api``` | method, path[, params[, body]] | Call a Hyperliquid endpoint directly. (more below the table) | The raw exchange response. |

The rest of the longer descriptions in the table:

- ```dex```: Once set, range queries without a symbol (```GetPositions()```, ```GetOrders()```, ```GetConditionOrders()```, ```GetTickers()```, ```GetMarkets()```) cover only this dex, while ```GetTickers()``` and ```GetMarkets()``` still add all HIP-4 Outcome instruments. An empty string clears it and restores the default, where these queries gather the main dex and all HIP-3 dexes. Calls with a symbol always follow the symbol's own dex prefix. The name is not checked when set; an unknown name fails on the next range query.
- ```source```: It sets the ```source``` field of the Agent signature of trading actions and the chainId of the EIP-712 signature of transfer actions (```usdSend```, ```withdraw3```, ```usdClassTransfer```, ...): Arbitrum 42161 on mainnet, Arbitrum Sepolia 421614 on testnet. The API address is not changed; to connect to the testnet also switch it with ```exchange.IO("base", "https://api.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz")```. The testnet has no HIP-3, so range queries cover the main dex only.
- ```split```: ```symbol``` is an Outcome code (such as ```BTC-above-100k---Dec_USD.Yes```), written as for market data and orders (markets sharing a name take the code with ```-<market id>``` (such as ```Recurring-1399_USD.Yes```) and the bare name fails as ambiguous); the ```symbol``` of ```merge```, ```mergeQuestion``` and ```negate``` follows the same rule. ```amount``` must be greater than 0.
- ```api```: A ```POST``` to ```/exchange``` takes an action object, and the connector adds the nonce and signs it; transfer actions (```usdSend```, ```spotSend```, ```withdraw3```, ```usdClassTransfer```, ```approveAgent```, ```approveBuilderFee```, ```userSetAbstraction```) are signed with the wallet private key ```WalletPrivateKey```, and fields such as ```hyperliquidChain``` must be filled in by the caller; other actions are signed with the API wallet private key. Other paths (such as ```POST /info```) are sent as they are, unsigned. ```body``` (a JSON object or a JSON string), when given, is the request body (the action for ```/exchange```); otherwise ```params``` is used as the body; a ```body``` of any other type is an error.

For the common commands ```base``` and ```currency``` see `exchange.IO`.

##### Common Usage

###### Query the Info endpoint with api and read another address's account

```javascript
function main() {
    // POST /info is unsigned; the params object is the request body
    var mids = exchange.IO("api", "POST", "/info", {type: "allMids"})
    Log("BTC mid:", mids["BTC"], "HYPE mid:", mids["HYPE"])
    var meta = exchange.IO("api", "POST", "/info", {type: "spotMeta"})
    Log("Spot tokens:", meta.tokens.length, "spot pairs:", meta.universe.length)
    // Later account and order queries target this address (the HLP vault here); the wallet
    // that signs orders is unchanged. Pass the configured wallet address to query your own
    // account again
    exchange.IO("walletAddress", "0xdfc24b077bc1425ad1dea75bcb6f8158e10df303")
    Log("Account of that address:", exchange.GetAccount())
    Log("Open orders of that address:", exchange.GetOrders())
}
```

###### Trade on behalf of a vault or sub-account

```javascript
function main() {
    var vault = "0x..."    // replace with the vault or sub-account address
    // Later orders, cancels and amendments are signed and sent on behalf of the vault
    exchange.IO("vaultAddress", vault)
    // Queries still use the wallet address; set it as well to query the vault
    exchange.IO("walletAddress", vault)
    Log("Vault account:", exchange.GetAccount())
    var orders = exchange.GetOrders()
    for (var i = 0; i < orders.length; i++) {
        exchange.CancelOrder(orders[i].Id)
    }
    // An empty string clears it; later actions are the wallet's own again
    exchange.IO("vaultAddress", "")
}
```

###### Give signed actions an expiry time

```javascript
function main() {
    // Later signed actions (orders, cancels, amendments, ...) expire in 10 seconds; the
    // exchange rejects actions that arrive after that time
    exchange.IO("expiresAfter", Date.now() + 10 * 1000)
    var orders = exchange.GetOrders()
    for (var i = 0; i < orders.length; i++) {
        if (!exchange.CancelOrder(orders[i].Id)) {
            Log("Cancel failed:", GetLastError())
        }
    }
    // The value stays in effect; reset it to 0, or every later action is rejected
    exchange.IO("expiresAfter", 0)
}
```

###### Send a transfer action with api, moving USDC between the spot and perpetual accounts

```javascript
function main() {
    // Transfer actions are signed with the "Wallet Private Key" option; the caller fills in
    // hyperliquidChain, signatureChainId and the other fields
    var r = exchange.IO("api", "POST", "/exchange", {
        type: "usdClassTransfer",
        hyperliquidChain: "Mainnet",     // Testnet on the testnet
        signatureChainId: "0xa4b1",      // signing chain ID 42161; 0x66eee (421614) on testnet
        amount: "10",                    // a string
        toPerp: true,                    // true: spot to perp; false: perp to spot
        nonce: Date.now()
    })
    Log(r)
}
```

###### List the HIP-3 dexes and query the instruments and positions of one of them (Futures_Hyperliquid only)

```javascript
function main() {
    // perpDexs: the first item is the main dex (null), followed by the HIP-3 dexes
    var dexs = exchange.IO("api", "POST", "/info", {type: "perpDexs"})
    var names = []
    for (var i = 0; i < dexs.length; i++) {
        if (dexs[i]) {
            names.push(dexs[i].name)
        }
    }
    Log("HIP-3 dexes:", names.join(", "))
    // Later range queries without a symbol cover only xyz (GetMarkets and GetTickers
    // always add the HIP-4 Outcome instruments)
    exchange.IO("dex", "xyz")
    var markets = exchange.GetMarkets()
    var n = 0
    for (var k in markets) {
        if (k.indexOf("xyz:") == 0) {
            n++
        }
    }
    Log("Perpetuals on xyz:", n)
    Log("Positions on xyz:", exchange.GetPositions())
    // Calls with a symbol follow the symbol's own dex prefix, whatever IO("dex") says
    Log(exchange.GetTicker("xyz:XYZ100_USD.swap"))
    // An empty string clears it; range queries gather the main dex and all HIP-3 dexes again
    exchange.IO("dex", "")
}
```

###### Find HIP-4 Outcome instruments and the questions they belong to (Futures_Hyperliquid only)

```javascript
function main() {
    // Rows of GetMarkets() with Info.isOutcome true are Outcome instruments, and
    // Info.outcomeId is the Outcome number
    var markets = exchange.GetMarkets()
    var byId = {}
    for (var k in markets) {
        var info = markets[k].Info
        if (info.isOutcome) {
            byId[info.outcomeId] = byId[info.outcomeId] || []
            byId[info.outcomeId].push(k)
        }
    }
    // A question consists of several Outcomes (namedOutcomes) plus a fallback Outcome
    var meta = exchange.IO("api", "POST", "/info", {type: "outcomeMeta"})
    Log("Outcomes:", meta.outcomes.length, "questions:", meta.questions.length)
    var q = meta.questions[0]
    Log("Question", q.question, q.description)
    for (var i = 0; i < q.namedOutcomes.length; i++) {
        Log("Outcome", q.namedOutcomes[i], byId[q.namedOutcomes[i]])
    }
    Log("Fallback Outcome", q.fallbackOutcome, byId[q.fallbackOutcome])
    var symbol = byId[q.namedOutcomes[0]][0]
    Log(symbol, exchange.GetDepth(symbol))
}
```

###### Split, merge and negate HIP-4 Outcome positions (Futures_Hyperliquid only)

```javascript
function main() {
    var symbol = "BTC-above-100k---Dec_USD.Yes"    // replace with an Outcome code of GetMarkets()
    // Split: an amount of 10 into positions on each side of the Outcome; must be above 0
    var r = exchange.IO("split", symbol, 10)
    Log("split:", r ? r.status : GetLastError())
    // Merge the positions on each side back; the amount may be omitted
    r = exchange.IO("merge", symbol, 10)
    Log("merge:", r ? r.status : GetLastError())
    // negate and mergeQuestion only work for an Outcome that belongs to a question
    r = exchange.IO("negate", symbol, 10)
    Log("negate:", r ? r.status : GetLastError())
    r = exchange.IO("mergeQuestion", symbol)
    Log("mergeQuestion:", r ? r.status : GetLastError())
}
```

##### Function Support

###### ```Hyperliquid``` (Spot)

Not supported (the call fails with an error and returns null): `exchange.CreateConditionOrder`, `exchange.ModifyConditionOrder`, `exchange.CancelConditionOrder`, `exchange.GetConditionOrder`, `exchange.GetConditionOrders`, `exchange.GetHistoryConditionOrders`.

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: Native periods are 1m, 3m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h, 8h, 12h, 1d, 3d, 1w, 1M; other periods are synthesized by the docker.

###### ```Futures_Hyperliquid``` (Futures)

No unsupported standard functions.

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: Native periods are 1m, 3m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h, 8h, 12h, 1d, 3d, 1w; other periods are synthesized by the docker. Outcome instruments have no bars.

##### Margin, Account and Simulation

###### ```Futures_Hyperliquid``` (Futures)

Margin mode: Choose cross/isolated margin with ```exchange.IO("cross", bool)```; it is submitted together with the leverage on the next ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()``` (the exchange's ```updateLeverage``` action). The leverage is truncated to an integer. HIP-3 margin is kept per dex.

Position mode: One-way positions only. Closing orders (```closebuy```, ```closesell```) are sent as reduce-only.

Account: For a unified account or portfolio margin account, the balance and equity of ```exchange.GetAccount()``` come from the spot USDC balance and the unrealized PnL from the perpetual account; a standard account reads the perpetual account (for HIP-3, the dex of the current symbol). The balance currency is USDC.

##### Notes

###### ```Hyperliquid``` (Spot)

- Market orders are sent as IOC orders priced at the mid price ±0.5%; the amount of a market buy is the number of coins to buy, not a quote-currency amount. An explicit ```{type: "limit"}``` with a price of 0 or below is an error; it is never sent as a market order.
- Order options go in the last object argument: ```{tif: "ioc"}``` for IOC and ```{postOnly: true}``` for post-only (the exchange's ```Alo```, not allowed on market orders); ```fok``` is not supported on limit orders and fails. ```builder``` (builder fee, ```{b: builder address, f: integer fee}```) and ```grouping``` are merged into the order action and signed with it; other keys are ignored.
- Prices allow at most 5 significant figures and at most 8 minus the coin's size decimals (szDecimals) decimal places; integer prices are always valid. ```TickSize``` and ```PricePrecision``` of ```exchange.GetMarkets()``` are computed at the magnitude of the current price, so the tick changes when the price crosses a power of 10: for example ```HYPE_USDC``` (szDecimals 2) has a tick of 0.001 below 100 and 0.01 from 100 up. An order or amendment whose price breaks the rule fails with an error that gives the tick at that price and the nearest valid prices on both sides; the price is not rounded automatically. The protective price of a market order is rounded by the connector according to the rule.
- ```AvgPrice``` of an order is the actual average fill price aggregated per order from the exchange's fill records (```userFillsByTime```), and 0 when nothing is filled. For a few seconds after a fill the exchange's fill records may not be updated yet; ```AvgPrice``` is then 0 (or the average of the fills already recorded) and is accurate when queried again shortly afterwards. The exchange keeps only the latest 10000 fills, so orders filled earlier report 0. Fill records are queried only for filled orders, and the results are cached.
- After a successful ```exchange.ModifyOrder()``` the order ID changes; the return value is the new order ID.
- ```Buy``` and ```Sell``` of ```exchange.GetTicker()``` are the best bid and ask (the mid price when one side is empty); ```Last```, ```High``` and ```Low``` are all the mid price, as the exchange has no 24h high/low. ```Buy``` and ```Sell``` of ```exchange.GetTickers()``` are the mid price too.
- ```exchange.GetHistoryOrders()``` returns only the recent orders the exchange provides; the ```since``` parameter is not supported and a ```since``` greater than 0 fails.
- WebSocket push is supported: market data (ticker, bbo, depth, trades, klines) and the private stream (order updates and balances) can be subscribed through the event stream. ```exchange.GetTicker()```, ```exchange.GetDepth()``` and the other functions still request the REST API directly, and ```EventLoop()``` does not subscribe to this exchange's push streams by itself. The ticker's last price, volume and open come from the same source as ```exchange.GetTicker()``` (mid price, 24h volume, previous day price), the best bid and ask come from the best bid/offer stream, and there is no 24h high or low. Depth subscriptions take at most 20 levels: 1 to 5 levels use the exchange's fast 5-level book (about every 0.5 seconds) and 6 to 20 levels (20 by default) use its 20-level book (about every 5 seconds); the two are separate streams. Trades carry the same trade IDs as ```exchange.GetTrades()```; the recent trades the exchange replays when a subscription becomes active are not pushed. Kline periods are the same as ```exchange.GetRecords()```, a first kline subscription pushes 500 historical bars first, and since the exchange's kline push has no closed flag a bar is pushed as closed when the next bar starts (on thinly traded pairs that waits for the next trade). The private stream is one ```private``` subscription for the whole wallet address (no symbol), subscribed read-only by ```WalletAddress``` (or the address set with ```exchange.IO("walletAddress", ...)```) without signing: once the subscription is active (and again after every reconnect) it first pushes a snapshot of all balances from the same endpoint as ```exchange.GetAccount()```, then reports ready, and afterwards pushes spot order updates (without the average fill price; use ```exchange.GetOrder()``` for it) and the balances of coins that changed. A market-wide ```tickers``` subscription is not supported (Hyperliquid's all-market ```allMids``` push carries mid prices only, not tickers) and fails at subscribe; subscribe ticker per symbol.

###### ```Futures_Hyperliquid``` (Futures)

- Market orders are sent as IOC orders priced at the mid price ±0.5%; for Outcome instruments ±1% (bounded to 0.001–0.999). A conditional order that executes at market after triggering is priced at the mid price ±0.5% as well. An explicit ```{type: "limit"}``` with a price of 0 or below is an error; it is never sent as a market order.
- Order options go in the last object argument: ```{tif: "ioc"}``` for IOC and ```{postOnly: true}``` for post-only (the exchange's ```Alo```; an error on conditional orders and on market orders of Outcome instruments; other market orders are always IOC); ```fok``` is not supported on limit orders and fails. ```builder``` (builder fee, ```{b: builder address, f: integer fee}```) and ```grouping``` are merged into the order action and signed with it; ```orders``` (a non-empty array) replaces the order legs built by the connector entirely, with the legs written by the caller in the exchange's format; other keys are ignored.
- Prices allow at most 5 significant figures and at most 6 minus the contract's size decimals (szDecimals) decimal places; integer prices are always valid. ```TickSize``` and ```PricePrecision``` of ```exchange.GetMarkets()``` are computed at the magnitude of the current price, so the tick changes when the price crosses a power of 10. An order or amendment (including the order price of a conditional order) whose price breaks the rule fails with an error that gives the tick at that price and the nearest valid prices on both sides; the price is not rounded automatically. The protective price of a market order is rounded by the connector according to the rule. HIP-4 Outcome instruments are not checked locally.
- ```AvgPrice``` of orders and conditional orders is the actual average fill price aggregated per order from the exchange's fill records (```userFillsByTime```), and 0 when nothing is filled. For a few seconds after a fill the exchange's fill records may not be updated yet; ```AvgPrice``` is then 0 (or the average of the fills already recorded) and is accurate when queried again shortly afterwards. The exchange keeps only the latest 10000 fills, so orders filled earlier report 0. Fill records are queried only for filled orders, and the results are cached.
- Conditional orders support take-profit and stop-loss, not OCO; take-profit and stop-loss are separate trigger orders. After a successful ```exchange.ModifyOrder()``` or ```exchange.ModifyConditionOrder()``` the order ID changes; the return value is the new order ID.
- ```Last``` of ```exchange.GetTicker()``` and ```exchange.GetTickers()``` is the mid price; ```Buy``` and ```Sell``` are the exchange's bid/ask impact prices (not the best bid and ask; use ```exchange.GetDepth()``` for those), and ```High```/```Low``` take the same impact prices, as the exchange has no 24h high/low.
- ```exchange.GetFundings()```: the main dex returns predicted funding rates (settled hourly); HIP-3 instruments need an explicit symbol and return the funding records of the last 24 hours.
- ```exchange.GetHistoryOrders()``` and ```exchange.GetHistoryConditionOrders()``` return only the recent orders the exchange provides; the ```since``` parameter is not supported and a ```since``` greater than 0 fails.
- HIP-4 Outcome instruments are spot-like holdings: trade them by buying and selling (integer amounts); reduce-only is not supported, so closing orders (```closebuy```, ```closesell```) fail; holdings come from the Outcome tokens in the spot account. Outcome instruments have no bars or funding rates, and ```Last``` of ```GetTicker()``` is the mid price while ```Buy``` and ```Sell``` are 0. An Outcome instrument the exchange has no mid price for yet (newly listed, not traded yet, and so on) is still listed by ```GetMarkets()``` (```PricePrecision``` is 4 and ```Info.assetCtx.midPx``` is ```null```), is left out of ```GetTickers()```, and fails ```GetTicker()``` and market orders; a holding of it is valued at a mid price of 0 (```Margin``` is 0 and ```Profit``` is minus the entry cost).
- WebSocket push is supported: market data (ticker, bbo, depth, trades, klines) and the private stream (order updates, positions and balances) can be subscribed through the event stream. ```exchange.GetTicker()```, ```exchange.GetDepth()``` and the other functions still request the REST API directly, and ```EventLoop()``` does not subscribe to this exchange's push streams by itself. The ticker's last price, volume, open and open interest come from the same source as ```exchange.GetTicker()``` (mid price, 24h volume, previous day price, open interest), the best bid and ask come from the best bid/offer stream (not the impact prices), and there is no 24h high or low. Depth subscriptions take at most 20 levels: 1 to 5 levels use the exchange's fast 5-level book (about every 0.5 seconds) and 6 to 20 levels (20 by default) use its 20-level book (about every 5 seconds); the two are separate streams. Trades carry the same trade IDs as ```exchange.GetTrades()```; the recent trades the exchange replays when a subscription becomes active are not pushed. Kline periods are the same as ```exchange.GetRecords()```, a first kline subscription pushes 500 historical bars first, and since the exchange's kline push has no closed flag a bar is pushed as closed when the next bar starts. HIP-4 Outcome instruments have no push (subscribing reports an error). The private stream is one ```private``` subscription for the whole wallet address (no symbol), subscribed read-only by ```WalletAddress``` (or the address set with ```exchange.IO("walletAddress", ...)```) without signing: once the subscription is active (and again after every reconnect) it first pushes a snapshot of all balances and positions from the same endpoints as ```exchange.GetAccount()``` and ```exchange.GetPositions()```, then reports ready, and afterwards pushes perpetual order updates (without the average fill price; use ```exchange.GetOrder()``` for it), positions that changed (one-way net positions; a closed position is pushed with quantity 0) and balances (re-queried from the same endpoint as ```exchange.GetAccount()``` when the pushed account state changes, so the figures are the same). Live positions cover one dex (the dex set with ```exchange.IO("dex", ...)```, the main dex by default); positions on other HIP-3 dexes appear only in the snapshots. A market-wide ```tickers``` subscription is not supported (Hyperliquid's all-market ```allMids``` push carries mid prices only, not tickers) and fails at subscribe; subscribe ticker per symbol.

#### Lighter

A perpetual-futures DEX on a zk rollup, quoted and settled in USDC. The exchange object connects to Lighter perpetuals: placing, modifying and canceling orders and setting leverage are L2 transactions signed with the API key private key, and open/historical order queries use an auth token generated with the same key. Create an API key on Lighter first and note its API key index and the account index.

##### Names and Configuration

```exchange.GetName()```: ```Futures_Lighter``` (Futures); aliases: zkLighter.

| Field | Required | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
| API Key Private Key | Yes | — | The API key private key created on Lighter (40-byte hex, ```0x``` prefix optional), used to sign L2 transactions and generate auth tokens. |
| API Key Index | Yes | — | API key index number, range 3-254 (0-2 reserved for system) |
| Account Index | Yes | — | Lighter account index for identifying master or sub-account |
| Simulate | No | Unchecked | Connect to the Lighter testnet when checked. |

##### Trading Pairs and Contract Codes

Pair examples: ```BTC_USDC```, ```ETH_USDC```

Only USDC-quoted perpetuals are listed; write the trading pair as ```BTC_USDC```, and the full symbol looks like ```BTC_USDC.swap```; other quote currencies are rejected. Pairs are case-insensitive and returned in upper case.

| Contract code | Description |
| - | - |
| ```swap``` | USDC perpetual contract (the only contract type). |

Lighter lists perpetuals only; contract codes other than ```swap``` are rejected.

##### Exchange-specific IO Commands

| Command | Arguments | Description | Returns |
| - | - | - | - |
| ```cross``` | bool[, symbol] | Cross (true) / isolated (false) margin, for the current contract when ```symbol``` is omitted. (more below the table) | ```{symbol, leverage, marginMode, initialMarginFraction, txHash, ok}```; ```txHash``` is the hash of the on-chain transaction. |
| ```expiry``` | number | Lifetime of subsequent limit orders and conditional orders (milliseconds, must be greater than 0), 29 days by default (the exchange's maximum); an order expires at the time of placing plus 10 minutes plus this duration. Market orders are not affected. | ```true``` |
| ```api``` | method, path[, params[, raw[, sign]]] | Call a Lighter endpoint directly; only ```GET``` and ```POST``` are supported. (more below the table) | The raw exchange response; an error is raised when the response ```code``` is not 200. |

The rest of the longer descriptions in the table:

- ```cross```: Lighter sets margin mode and leverage in the same on-chain transaction, which also writes the instrument's current leverage (read from the instrument's setting in the exchange account data; a value set in this run within the last 60 seconds takes precedence; the market's default leverage when neither exists).
- ```api```: By default the auth token generated with the API key private key is attached (the private key and account index must be filled in); with ```sign``` set to ```false``` (it may also be given directly as the 4th argument) no token is sent, which only works for public ```GET``` endpoints. ```raw``` is not a request body but a parameter table (a JSON object or ```a=1&b=2```) that replaces ```params``` entirely when non-empty; it goes into the query string for ```GET``` and a form body for ```POST```. L2 transactions are not signed for the caller.

For the common commands ```base``` and ```currency``` see `exchange.IO`.

##### Common Usage

###### Set the lifetime of limit orders

```javascript
function main() {
    // Later limit and conditional orders expire 10 minutes plus 1 hour after they are placed
    // (29 days by default); market orders are not affected
    exchange.IO("expiry", 60 * 60 * 1000)
    var id = exchange.CreateOrder("ETH_USDC.swap", "buy", 2000, 0.01)
    Log("Order ID:", id)
}
```

###### Call public endpoints and account endpoints that need the auth token with api

```javascript
function main() {
    // Public endpoints: false as the 4th argument sends no auth token
    var books = exchange.IO("api", "GET", "/api/v1/orderBooks", {}, false)
    Log("Markets:", books.order_books.length)
    var d = exchange.IO("api", "GET", "/api/v1/orderBookDetails", {market_id: 0}, false)
    Log(d.order_book_details[0].symbol, "last:", d.order_book_details[0].last_trade_price)
    // Account endpoints carry the auth token by default; the account index is in the Info
    // of GetAccount()
    var idx = exchange.GetAccount().Info.account_index
    var params = {account_index: idx, market_id: 0}
    var r = exchange.IO("api", "GET", "/api/v1/accountActiveOrders", params)
    Log("Open orders on market_id 0:", r.orders.length)
}
```

##### Function Support

No unsupported standard functions.

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: Native periods are 1m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 4h, 12h, 1d, 1w; other periods are synthesized by the docker.

##### Margin, Account and Simulation

Margin mode: Switch cross/isolated margin per contract with ```exchange.IO("cross", bool)``` and set leverage with ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()```. On Lighter both are the same on-chain transaction (UpdateLeverage); every call sends one and always writes both leverage and margin mode, keeping the other one at the instrument's current value: ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()``` keeps the current margin mode and ```exchange.IO("cross", ...)``` keeps the current leverage. The current values are read from the instrument's setting in the exchange account data (present even without a position); a value set in this run within the last 60 seconds takes precedence (the exchange data lags); without either, the market's default leverage and cross. ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()``` also accepts ```{marginMode: "isolated"}``` (or ```cross```) in the extra parameters to set the margin mode at the same time. A position's ```MarginLevel``` is derived from the initial margin fraction in the exchange's position data.

Position mode: One-way (net) positions only; hedge mode is not supported.

Account: The account index selects the master account or a sub-account; the account and positions are queried by account index, and USDC is the only asset.

Simulation: The Simulate box connects to the Lighter testnet (```https://testnet.zklighter.elliot.ai```). The API address can also be switched with ```exchange.SetBase()``` (or ```exchange.IO("base", url)```): transactions are signed for the testnet when the address contains ```testnet```, otherwise for the mainnet.

##### Notes

| Function | Behavior on Futures_Lighter |
| - | - |
| exchange.GetTicker() | Bid and ask come from the order book; the exchange's market data has no timestamp, so ```Time``` is the local time |
| exchange.GetTickers() | ```Buy``` and ```Sell``` are each instrument's last trade price (the exchange has no batch order book endpoint); use ```exchange.GetTicker()``` or ```exchange.GetDepth()``` when you need the best bid and ask. Placeholder instruments whose last price, 24h high/low and volume are all zero are omitted |
| exchange.GetDepth() | The exchange returns individual resting orders; each order is its own level and orders at the same price are not merged, so a price may appear more than once |
| exchange.GetFundings() | ```Rate``` is the exchange's rate divided by 8 (an hourly rate), ```Interval``` is 1 hour and ```Time``` is the next full hour |
| exchange.CreateOrder() | Limit orders support GTC (resting for the ```exchange.IO("expiry", ...)``` lifetime), IOC and post-only; FOK is not supported. A market order is an IOC order whose worst fill price is the best opposite price at the time of placing plus or minus a slippage (a buy no higher than the best ask × (1 + slippage), a sell no lower than the best bid × (1 − slippage)); the slippage defaults to 0.5% and can be set with the order extra parameter ```slippage``` (such as ```0.01```, greater than 0 and less than 1, the same parameter as for market conditional orders); whatever the book cannot fill within that price is canceled. An order that fills nothing is canceled with a ```DealAmount``` of 0, and ```status``` in ```Info``` gives the reason (such as ```canceled-too-much-slippage```) |
| exchange.CreateConditionOrder() | Take-profit and stop-loss only, no OCO. With an order price it is a limit conditional order; with an order price of -1 (market) it executes at market once triggered (IOC) with a worst fill price of the trigger price ±5% (up for buys, down for sells), adjustable with ```{slippage: 0.1}``` in the extra parameters |
| exchange.ModifyOrder() | Modifies in place, the order ID stays the same; a price or amount that is not passed keeps its current value |
| exchange.GetOrders(), exchange.GetConditionOrders() | The exchange API requires an instrument: without a symbol, or with an empty string, only the current instrument is queried. ```GetOrders``` returns limit and market orders only and ```GetConditionOrders``` take-profit/stop-loss orders only (other types such as TWAP appear in neither); range arguments such as ```USDC.swap``` are not supported |
| exchange.GetOrder() | Searches only the open orders and the latest 100 historical orders of the instrument; older orders return null |
| exchange.ModifyConditionOrder() | Modifies the amount, trigger price and order price in place; the order ID stays the same. The limit/market variant cannot change: an order price of -1 on a limit conditional order, or a positive one on a market conditional order, fails (cancel and recreate instead); a market conditional order's worst fill price is recomputed from the new trigger price |
| exchange.GetHistoryOrders(), exchange.GetHistoryConditionOrders() | The exchange API requires an instrument: the current one is queried when omitted, and an empty string or a range raises an error; the ```since``` parameter is not supported and raises an error; without ```limit``` the latest 100 and 500 orders are returned respectively |

- WebSocket push is supported: market data (ticker, bbo, depth, trades, klines) and the private stream (order updates, positions and balances) can be subscribed through the event stream. ```exchange.GetTicker()```, ```exchange.GetDepth()``` and the other functions still request the REST API directly, and ```EventLoop()``` does not subscribe to this exchange's push streams by itself. The ticker's last price, 24h high/low, volume, open interest and open price (derived from the 24h change) match ```exchange.GetTickers()```, while the best bid/ask prices and sizes come from the exchange's best bid/offer channel (the same push as a bbo subscription). Depth subscriptions (20 levels by default, at most 255) are synchronized from the exchange's full-book snapshot plus deltas, checking the matching engine's sequence numbers for continuity and resubscribing on a gap; the exchange has a single order book stream per instrument, so subscriptions of different depths share it and each is cut to its own depth. Pushed depth is aggregated by price (unlike the individual resting orders of ```exchange.GetDepth()```). Trades carry the same trade IDs as ```exchange.GetTrades()```; liquidation trades are not pushed. Klines support the 1m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 4h, 12h and 1d periods (the push has no weekly period), and a first kline subscription pushes 500 historical bars first. The private stream is one ```private``` subscription for the whole account (no symbol); it needs the API key private key and the account index and connects only when subscribed: the order channel carries the same auth token as the private REST endpoints, while the position and account statistics channels are subscribed by account index. Once the subscription is active (and again after every reconnect) it first pushes a snapshot of the USDC balance and all positions from the same endpoints as ```exchange.GetAccount()``` and ```exchange.GetPositions()```, then reports ready, and afterwards pushes order updates on every instrument (the order ID is the one ```exchange.CreateOrder()``` returns), positions that changed (one-way net positions, a closed position is pushed with quantity 0) and the USDC balance after a change (free is the available margin and frozen is the total account value minus it, the same as ```exchange.GetAccount()```). The auth token is valid for 7 hours; the private connection reconnects with a fresh token before it expires and pushes a new snapshot. An authentication failure reports a degraded connection status and a failed private stream (market data push is unaffected). Simulated trading uses the testnet push endpoint. A market-wide ```tickers``` subscription (no symbol) uses the exchange's all-market statistics channel: about once a second it pushes the instruments that changed, with the last price, 24h high/low, volume, open interest and open price as in the ticker, and the best bid/ask prices without sizes (the exchange has no all-market best bid/offer channel); instruments that have not traded yet (last price, 24h high/low and volume all zero) are not pushed, as in ```exchange.GetTickers()```.

#### edgeX

A perpetual-futures DEX (V2 API), with contracts quoted in USDC. Private endpoints are authenticated by HMAC with the edgeX Perps V2 API Key, API Secret and API Passphrase, and orders are additionally EIP-712-signed with the trading private key (SDK Signer); create both sets of credentials on edgeX and note the account ID before configuring the exchange object. Configurations from the old V1 scheme (only AccountID and the StarkEx private key Secret Key) no longer work: private endpoints report missing V2 credentials, so create V2 API credentials on edgeX and fill in all five fields.

##### Names and Configuration

```exchange.GetName()```: ```Futures_EdgeX``` (Futures); aliases: EdgeX.

| Field | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
| AccountID | Yes | The edgeX account ID (numeric). |
| API Key | Yes | The edgeX Perps V2 API Key, used with the API Secret and API Passphrase for HMAC authentication of private endpoints. |
| API Secret | Yes | The edgeX Perps V2 API Secret (HMAC key). |
| API Passphrase | Yes | The edgeX Perps V2 API Passphrase. |
| Trading Private Key | Yes | The private key (hex) of the edgeX Perps V2 SDK Signer, used for the EIP-712 signature of orders; the IO command ```calcOrderHashAndSign``` also uses it for Stark signatures. |

##### Trading Pairs and Contract Codes

Pair examples: ```BTC_USDC```, ```ETH_USDC```

All edgeX perpetuals are quoted in USDC: write the trading pair as ```BTC_USDC``` and so on, with full symbols such as ```BTC_USDC.swap```; ```BTC_USDT``` or ```BTC_USD``` fails with the error ```symbol not found: BTCUSDT``` (or ```BTCUSD```). ```exchange.SetCurrency()``` keeps the case as given (```exchange.GetCurrency()``` returns it unchanged), contracts are looked up case-insensitively; symbols in data returned by the exchange (orders, positions, etc.) are upper case, while the ```Symbol``` of ```exchange.GetTicker()``` keeps the case passed in or currently set, so upper case is recommended.

| Contract code | Description |
| - | - |
| ```swap``` | USDC perpetual contract (the only contract type). |

edgeX lists perpetuals only; contract codes other than ```swap``` are rejected.

##### Exchange-specific IO Commands

| Command | Arguments | Description | Returns |
| - | - | - | - |
| ```calcOrderHashAndSign``` | json | Legacy (StarkEx) limit-order signature, kept only so that old strategies keep working; computes the Pedersen hash of a LIMIT_ORDER_WITH_FEES order and signs it with Stark ECDSA using the configured TradingPrivateKey. (more below the table) | A 128-character lowercase hex string (r and s, 64 characters each, without ```0x```). |
| ```api``` | method, path[, params[, raw[, sign]]] | Call an edgeX endpoint directly. (more below the table) | The ```data``` of the response; an error is raised when the response ```code``` is not ```SUCCESS```. |

The rest of the longer descriptions in the table:

- ```calcOrderHashAndSign```: The argument is a JSON string or object with 10 keys, see the notes. edgeX V2 orders use EIP-712 signatures and do not accept this signature, and this exchange object does not use it when placing orders.
- ```api```: By default the request is HMAC-signed with the API Key, API Secret and API Passphrase (these three V2 credentials must be filled in); with ```sign``` set to ```false``` (it may also be given directly as the 4th argument) it is sent unsigned, which only works for ```GET```. ```GET``` parameters go into the query string, other methods send a JSON body. ```raw``` is not a request body but a parameter table (a JSON object, a JSON string or ```a=1&b=2```) that replaces ```params``` entirely when non-empty. Orders are not EIP-712-signed for the caller.

For the common commands ```base``` and ```currency``` see `exchange.IO`.

##### Common Usage

###### Call public endpoints and signed account endpoints with api

```javascript
function main() {
    // Public endpoints: false as the 4th argument sends the request unsigned (GET only);
    // the data of the response is returned
    var meta = exchange.IO("api", "GET", "/api/v2/public/meta/getMetaData", {}, false)
    var c = null
    for (var i = 0; i < meta.contractList.length; i++) {
        if (meta.contractList[i].contractName == "BTCUSDC") {
            c = meta.contractList[i]
        }
    }
    var p = {contractId: c.contractId}
    var t = exchange.IO("api", "GET", "/api/v2/public/quote/getTicker", p, false)
    Log(c.contractName, "contract ID:", c.contractId, "last:", t[0].lastPrice)
    // Account endpoints are HMAC-signed by default; accountId is in the Info of GetAccount()
    var accountId = exchange.GetAccount().Info.account.id
    var params = {accountId: accountId, size: "50"}
    var orders = exchange.IO("api", "GET", "/api/v2/private/order/getActiveOrderPage", params)
    Log("Open orders:", orders.dataList.length)
}
```

###### Compute a legacy (StarkEx) limit-order signature for an old strategy

```javascript
function main() {
    // Exactly 10 keys; an accountID beyond JavaScript integer precision is a decimal string
    var sig = exchange.IO("calcOrderHashAndSign", JSON.stringify({
        assetIdSynthetic: "0x4554482d3900000000000000000000",
        assetIdCollateral: "0x2ce625e94458d39dd0bf3b45a843544dd4a14b8169045a3a3d15aa564b936c5",
        assetIdFee: "0x2ce625e94458d39dd0bf3b45a843544dd4a14b8169045a3a3d15aa564b936c5",
        isBuyingSynthetic: true,
        amountSynthetic: 10000000,
        amountCollateral: 13020000,
        amountFee: 6250,
        nonce: 676432751,
        accountID: "601416704693633632",
        expirationTimestamp: 484831
    }))
    // 128 hex characters: the first 64 are r, the last 64 are s
    Log("r:", sig.slice(0, 64), "s:", sig.slice(64))
}
```

##### Function Support

Not supported (the call fails with an error and returns null): `exchange.GetTickers`, `exchange.GetTrades`, `exchange.ModifyOrder`, `exchange.ModifyConditionOrder`, `exchange.SetMarginLevel`.

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: Native periods are 1m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h, 6h, 8h, 12h, 1d, 1w, 1M; other periods that are a multiple of 60 seconds are synthesized by the docker from native bars, and the rest (such as second-level periods) are not available (the exchange has no trades endpoint).

##### Margin, Account and Simulation

Margin mode: edgeX uses cross margin; a position's ```MarginLevel``` is the current leverage reported by the exchange. ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()``` is not supported; set leverage on edgeX yourself.

Position mode: One-way (net) positions.

Account: The account, positions and orders are queried by the configured AccountID. ```exchange.GetAssets()``` lists collateral assets per coin, and ```exchange.GetAccount()``` takes the row of the current pair's quote currency (USDC).

##### Notes

| Function | Behavior on Futures_EdgeX |
| - | - |
| exchange.GetTicker() | The ticker endpoint has no bid/ask, so each call makes an extra order book request to fill them in (two requests in all); if the order book request fails, the whole call fails. ```Time``` is the server time of the order book response (as is the ```Time``` of ```exchange.GetDepth()```), not the ticker's ```endTime``` (the end of the 24-hour statistics window, which advances in 15-minute steps); ```endTime``` is still available in ```Info``` |
| exchange.GetTickers() | Not supported: edgeX has no endpoint that returns the tickers of all contracts at once (its ticker endpoint returns an empty list without a contract ID), so the call reports an error and returns null. To get several contracts' tickers, call ```exchange.GetTicker(symbol)``` for each one (such as ```exchange.GetTicker("BTC_USDC.swap")```) |
| exchange.GetFundings() | With a symbol (such as ```BTC_USDC.swap```) it returns that contract's entry; without arguments it queries every tradable perpetual of the current quote currency (such as ```USDC.swap```, which can also be passed directly). edgeX has no batch funding endpoint, so a range query sends one request per contract and takes over ten seconds for the hundred-plus contracts; pass a specific symbol when calling it often. ```Rate``` is the exchange's forecast (next) rate and ```Time``` the next settlement time |
| exchange.CreateOrder() | Order amounts are in coins (1 contract = 1 coin). Limit orders support GTC, IOC, FOK and post-only; market orders are IOC by default, cannot be post-only, and are bounded by the oracle price: buys at no more than 1.2 times it, sells at no less than 0.8 times it |
| exchange.CreateConditionOrder() | Take-profit and stop-loss only, no OCO (place the two legs separately), triggered by the last trade price; with an order price of -1 (market) the order executes at market once triggered, with the price bound computed from the oracle price at creation. To modify a conditional order, cancel it and create a new one |
| exchange.GetOrders(), exchange.GetConditionOrders() | Without a symbol, open orders of all contracts are returned. Conditional and regular orders share one order table, so untriggered conditional orders also appear in the result of ```exchange.GetOrders()``` |
| exchange.GetHistoryOrders() | At most 100 orders are returned when ```limit``` is omitted; finished conditional orders are included |
| exchange.GetHistoryConditionOrders() | The third parameter keeps its legacy meaning and is not a count: a value above 1e12 is taken as the end time (millisecond timestamp) and smaller values are ignored; the number of results is not limited. Without ```since``` the call pages through the contract's whole order history and fails beyond about 10,000 orders, so passing ```since``` is recommended |

The argument of ```exchange.IO("calcOrderHashAndSign", json)``` must have exactly 10 keys: ```assetIdSynthetic```, ```assetIdCollateral```, ```assetIdFee``` (hex), ```isBuyingSynthetic``` (bool), ```amountSynthetic```, ```amountCollateral```, ```amountFee```, ```nonce```, ```accountID``` and ```expirationTimestamp``` (integers, or decimal strings; an ```accountID``` beyond JavaScript integer precision must be a string). A missing or malformed key reports ```argument X error```, and extra keys report ```argument error```. The signing key is the configured TradingPrivateKey (used as a Stark private key), not the Stark key of an old account; the signing nonce is deterministic (RFC 6979), so the same input always gives the same signature, which differs from the old docker's but is equally valid.

WebSocket push is supported: market data (ticker, bbo, depth, trades, klines) and the private stream (order updates, positions and balances) can be subscribed through the event stream. ```exchange.GetTicker()```, ```exchange.GetDepth()``` and the other functions still request the REST API directly, and ```EventLoop()``` does not subscribe to this exchange's push streams by itself. Depth subscriptions of up to 15 levels (15 by default) use edgeX's 15-level book stream and 16 to 200 levels the 200-level stream, both synchronized from a snapshot plus version-linked deltas, at most 200 levels. edgeX has no usable top-of-book stream, so bbo and the ticker's bid/ask prices and sizes come from the 15-level book on a separate connection. Trades carry the exchange's ```ticketId``` (a UUID string) as the trade ID; edgeX has no trades query (```exchange.GetTrades()``` is not supported), so they cannot be compared with REST, and the 30 recent trades the exchange sends on subscription are not pushed as live trades. Kline periods are the native periods of ```exchange.GetRecords()```, and a first kline subscription pushes 500 historical bars first; the exchange's push has no closed flag, so when the next bar starts the previous one is marked closed with its last pushed values. The private stream is one ```private``` subscription for the whole account (no symbol); it needs the AccountID and the V2 API Key, API Secret and API Passphrase, connects only when subscribed and authenticates with the same HMAC scheme as the private endpoints: once the subscription is active (and again after every reconnect) it first pushes a snapshot of all balances and positions from the same endpoints as ```exchange.GetAccount()``` and ```exchange.GetPositions()```, then reports ready, and afterwards pushes order updates and positions that changed (one-way net positions with the average price taken as position value divided by size; a closed position is pushed with quantity 0; the push carries no unrealized profit, margin or leverage). The collateral amount in the exchange's push is not the free/frozen balance, so every account event triggers one balance query and only coins that changed are pushed. An authentication failure reports a degraded connection status and a failed private stream (market data push is unaffected). A market-wide ```tickers``` subscription (no symbol) uses edgeX's all-market ticker channel: once a second it pushes every tradable contract with the same fields as the ticker, the best bid/ask carrying prices without sizes; contracts whose last price, 24h high/low and volume are all zero are not pushed.

#### Aster

```Aster``` (Spot): Aster spot (API address ```https://sapi.asterdex.com```). Private endpoints use wallet signatures (EIP-712): configure the main account's wallet address plus the private key of the API signer wallet authorized for that account on Aster (the signer wallet address is optional and is derived from the private key); no API Key is needed. Perpetual contracts use the Futures_Aster exchange object.

```Futures_ApolloX``` (Futures): ApolloX has merged into and been renamed Aster. Futures_ApolloX connects to the same exchange's legacy futures API (```https://fapi.apollox.finance```, the v1/v2 API that mirrors Binance USDⓈ-M) with an API Key (HMAC signature); perpetual contracts only. The Futures_Aster exchange object connects to the v3 API with wallet signatures.

```Futures_Aster``` (Futures): Aster perpetual contracts (API address ```https://fapi.asterdex.com```, the v3 API that mirrors Binance USDⓈ-M). Private endpoints use wallet signatures (EIP-712): configure the main account's wallet address plus the private key of the API signer wallet authorized for that account on Aster (the signer wallet address is optional and is derived from the private key); no API Key is needed. The Futures_ApolloX exchange object connects to the same exchange's legacy API with an API Key (HMAC); spot uses the Aster exchange object.

##### Names and Configuration

| ```exchange.GetName()``` | Type | Aliases |
| - | - | - |
| ```Aster``` | Spot | AsterDEX |
| ```Futures_ApolloX``` | Futures | ApolloX, ApolloX DEX |
| ```Futures_Aster``` | Futures | — |

✓ marks the exchange objects that have the field.

| Field | ```Aster``` | ```Futures_ApolloX``` | ```Futures_Aster``` | Required | Description |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| User | ✓ |  | ✓ | Yes | Wallet address of the main account (the account holding the assets). |
| Signer | ✓ |  | ✓ | No | Address of the API signer wallet (agent wallet) authorized for the main account on Aster. It is optional; when blank it is derived from the signer private key below (the address of that key is the signer wallet address); when filled it is used as is and must match the private key. |
| Private Key | ✓ |  | ✓ | Yes | Private key of the signer wallet above, used to sign private requests. |
| Access Key |  | ✓ |  | Yes | The API Key created in the exchange's API management. |
| Secret Key |  | ✓ |  | Yes | The Secret Key paired with the API Key, used for HMAC signing. |

If the contract is already in the requested mode, the first call may get an exchange error (Binance-style ```-4046```). |

##### Function Support

###### All exchange objects

Not supported (the call fails with an error and returns null): `exchange.ModifyOrder`, `exchange.ModifyConditionOrder`.

###### ```Futures_ApolloX``` (Futures), ```Futures_Aster``` (Futures)

Served through a fallback:

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: Native periods are 1s, 1m, 3m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h, 6h, 8h, 12h, 1d, 3d, 1w, 1M; other periods are synthesized by the docker.

##### Margin, Account and Simulation

###### ```Futures_ApolloX``` (Futures), ```Futures_Aster``` (Futures)

Position mode: Switch hedge/one-way mode with ```exchange.IO("dual", bool)```. The account's position mode is queried once before the first order and cached; in hedge mode orders carry ```positionSide``` automatically (closing orders without ```reduceOnly```), or an explicit ```positionSide``` can be passed in the order's extra parameters. After a failed order the mode is queried again for the next order.

###### ```Futures_ApolloX``` (Futures)

Margin mode: Switch cross/isolated margin per contract with ```exchange.IO("cross", bool)```; set leverage per contract with ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()```.

###### ```Futures_Aster``` (Futures)

Margin mode: Switch cross/isolated margin per contract with ```exchange.IO("cross", bool)```; set leverage per contract with ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()```. When the account has Multi-Assets mode enabled, the exchange rejects switching to isolated margin (```-4168```).

Account: In single-asset mode ```exchange.GetAccount()``` reads the row of the current quote currency (such as USDT): ```Balance``` is that currency's withdrawable balance and ```Equity``` its margin balance. In Multi-Assets mode all margin currencies share one USD-valued margin pool: ```Balance``` is the account's available margin (```availableBalance```), ```FrozenBalance``` the initial margin held by open orders, ```Equity``` the account margin balance (```totalMarginBalance```) and ```UPnL``` the account's unrealized PnL, all whole-account USD values computed by the exchange regardless of the quote currency; the account mode is queried at most once a minute and cached. ```exchange.GetAssets()``` lists each currency's own wallet balance.

##### Notes

###### ```Aster``` (Spot), ```Futures_Aster``` (Futures)

- After ```exchange.IO("base", url)``` switches to a testnet address containing ```testnet```, signatures automatically use the testnet chain ID.

###### ```Futures_ApolloX``` (Futures), ```Futures_Aster``` (Futures)

- Order amounts are base-currency quantities (one contract is one unit of the base currency); market buy orders also use the base-currency quantity.
