- Conditional orders support take-profit and stop-loss only, not OCO; create a take-profit order and a stop-loss order separately when needed. Modifying a conditional order (```exchange.ModifyConditionOrder()```) is not supported; cancel and recreate it instead.
- ```exchange.GetHistoryOrders()``` and ```exchange.GetHistoryConditionOrders()``` require a contract.

###### ```Aster``` (Spot)

- The amount of a market buy order is the quote-currency amount (sent as Aster's ```quoteOrderQty```); a market sell order uses the base-currency quantity. Conditional orders always use the base-currency quantity, for both buys and sells.
- A market buy by quote amount is rounded down to the quantity step by the exchange; the leftover amount below one step is not used and the order ends as ```EXPIRED```. As long as anything was filled, the queried order status is filled (```ORDER_STATE_CLOSED```), and both ```Amount``` and ```DealAmount``` are the base-currency quantity actually bought. A market order placed by quantity that is not fully filled for lack of liquidity is still canceled (```DealAmount``` less than ```Amount```).
- Conditional orders support take-profit and stop-loss only, not OCO; create a take-profit order and a stop-loss order separately when needed. Modifying a conditional order (```exchange.ModifyConditionOrder()```) is not supported; cancel and recreate it instead. ```exchange.GetConditionOrder()``` with the ID of a regular order fails (that order is not conditional).
- ```exchange.GetHistoryOrders()``` and ```exchange.GetHistoryConditionOrders()``` require a trading pair.
- WebSocket push is supported: market data (ticker, bbo, depth, trades, klines) and the private stream (order updates and balances) can be subscribed through the event stream. ```exchange.GetTicker()```, ```exchange.GetDepth()``` and the other functions still request the REST API directly, and ```EventLoop()``` does not subscribe to this exchange's push streams by itself. The ticker merges Aster's 24-hour ticker stream with the best bid/ask stream; the 24-hour stream only pushes when trades happen, so a pair that has not traded since the subscription has no ticker yet (bbo is pushed as usual). Depth subscriptions of 5, 10 and 20 levels use Aster's snapshot streams; other depths (20 by default, at most 255) are synchronized from the diff stream and a REST snapshot. Trades are aggregate trades (the same trade IDs as ```exchange.GetTrades()```). Klines from 1 minute to 1 month are pushed (there is no 1-second kline stream); a first kline subscription pushes 500 historical bars first. The private stream is one ```private``` subscription for the whole spot account (no symbol); it requests a listenKey with the wallet signature and connects only when subscribed, and renews the key every 30 minutes. Once the subscription is active (and again after every reconnect) it first pushes a snapshot of all balances from the same endpoint as ```exchange.GetAssets()```, then reports ready, and afterwards pushes order updates (market buys by amount match ```exchange.GetOrder()```) and the balances of coins that changed (free and frozen match ```exchange.GetAssets()```). Spot has no positions, so the private stream pushes none. A rejected signature reports a degraded connection status and a failed private stream (market data push is unaffected); when the REST address points to the testnet, push connects to the testnet too. A market-wide ```tickers``` subscription (no symbol) uses Aster's all-market 24-hour ticker stream (once a second, the pairs that changed, with the last price, the 24-hour open/high/low and the volume) together with the best bid/ask from the all-market book ticker stream; a pair is pushed once its best bid/ask has arrived.

###### ```Futures_ApolloX``` (Futures)

- WebSocket push is supported: market data (ticker, bbo, depth, trades, klines) and the private stream (order updates, positions and balances) can be subscribed through the event stream. ```exchange.GetTicker()```, ```exchange.GetDepth()``` and the other functions still request the REST API directly, and ```EventLoop()``` does not subscribe to this exchange's push streams by itself. The ticker merges the 24-hour ticker stream with the best bid/ask stream. Depth subscriptions of 5, 10 or 20 levels use the exchange's partial-depth snapshot streams; other depths (20 by default, at most 255 levels) use the diff stream synchronized with a REST depth snapshot. Trades carry the same trade IDs as ```exchange.GetTrades()```. Kline periods are the same as ```exchange.GetRecords()``` (no second-level periods), and a first kline subscription pushes 500 historical bars first. The private stream is one ```private``` subscription for the whole account (no symbol); it requests a listenKey and connects only when subscribed. Once the subscription is active (and again after every reconnect) it first pushes a snapshot of all balances and positions from the same endpoints as ```exchange.GetAccount()``` and ```exchange.GetPositions()```, then reports ready, and afterwards pushes order updates, positions that changed (one net position in one-way mode, one long and one short leg in hedge mode, a closed position is pushed with quantity 0; pushed positions carry no margin, leverage or liquidation price) and the balances re-queried after a balance change (same figures as ```exchange.GetAccount()```; placing or canceling orders and mark price moves do not trigger a balance push). An authentication failure reports a degraded connection status and a failed private stream (market data push is unaffected). A market-wide ```tickers``` subscription (no symbol) uses ApolloX's all-market 24-hour ticker stream (once a second, the contracts that changed, with the last price, the 24-hour open/high/low and the volume) together with the best bid/ask from the all-market book ticker stream; a contract is pushed once its best bid/ask has arrived.

###### ```Futures_Aster``` (Futures)

- WebSocket push is supported: market data (ticker, bbo, depth, trades, klines) and the private stream (order updates, positions and balances) can be subscribed through the event stream. ```exchange.GetTicker()```, ```exchange.GetDepth()``` and the other functions still request the REST API directly, and ```EventLoop()``` does not subscribe to this exchange's push streams by itself. The ticker merges Aster's 24-hour ticker stream with the best bid/ask stream; the 24-hour stream only pushes when trades happen, so a contract that has not traded since the subscription has no ticker yet (bbo is pushed as usual). Depth subscriptions of 5, 10 and 20 levels use Aster's snapshot streams; other depths (20 by default, at most 255) are synchronized from the diff stream and a REST snapshot. Trades carry the same trade IDs as ```exchange.GetTrades()```; liquidation and auto-deleveraging fills are not pushed. A first kline subscription pushes 500 historical bars first. The private stream is one ```private``` subscription for the whole futures account (no symbol); it requests a listenKey with the wallet signature and connects only when subscribed, and renews the key every 30 minutes. Once the subscription is active (and again after every reconnect) it first pushes a snapshot of all balances and positions from the same endpoints as ```exchange.GetAssets()``` and ```exchange.GetPositions()```, then reports ready, and afterwards pushes order updates, positions that changed (one net position in one-way mode, one long and one short leg in hedge mode, a closed position is pushed with quantity 0; the push carries no margin, leverage, liquidation price or mark price) and balances: after a balance change or an order update the balances are queried once more like ```exchange.GetAssets()``` and only the coins that changed are pushed. Floating profit and equity changes caused by the mark price are not pushed. A rejected signature reports a degraded connection status and a failed private stream (market data push is unaffected); when the REST address points to the testnet, push connects to the testnet too. A market-wide ```tickers``` subscription (no symbol) uses Aster's all-market 24-hour ticker stream (once a second, the contracts that changed, with the last price, the 24-hour open/high/low and the volume) together with the best bid/ask from the all-market book ticker stream; a contract is pushed once its best bid/ask has arrived.

#### Aevo

USDC perpetual contracts and USDC options. Queries, cancellations and leverage changes are signed with the API key; orders, order amendments and conditional orders are additionally signed (EIP-712) with a signing key registered on the Aevo account (the "Signing Key" option).

##### Names and Configuration

```exchange.GetName()```: ```Futures_Aevo``` (Futures).

| Field | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
| Access Key | Yes | The Aevo API key, sent as the ```AEVO-KEY``` header of private endpoints. |
| Secret Key | Yes | The Aevo API secret, used for the HMAC-SHA256 signature of private endpoints. |
| Signing Key | Yes | The EIP-712 signing private key registered on the Aevo account (```0x``` plus 64 hex digits), used for orders, order amendments and conditional orders. (more below the table) |

The rest of the longer descriptions in the table:

- Signing Key: Generate it on Aevo's settings page (```https://app.aevo.xyz/settings```, not the API Keys page); it expires automatically one week after generation, after which a new one must be generated and entered here. Without it, placing or amending orders and creating conditional orders fail, while queries, cancellations and leverage settings still work; it can also be set at run time with ```exchange.IO("signingKey", key)```.

##### Trading Pairs and Contract Codes

Pair examples: ```BTC_USDC```, ```ETH_USDC```

Aevo quotes and settles in USDC; trading pairs are written as ```ETH_USDC```, and any quote currency other than USDC is rejected.

| Contract code | Description |
| - | - |
| ```swap``` | Perpetual contract (exchange code ```ETH-PERP```); the full symbol looks like ```ETH_USDC.swap```. |

Aevo has no delivery contracts; any contract code other than ```swap``` and option codes is rejected.

##### Exchange-specific IO Commands

| Command | Arguments | Description | Returns |
| - | - | - | - |
| ```signingKey``` | string | Set the EIP-712 signing private key (```0x``` plus 64 hex digits) used for orders by this exchange object, overriding the "Signing Key" option for the current run only. The signing key is generated and registered on the account when an API key is created on the Aevo website; it has an expiry and must be regenerated after it expires. | The wallet address of the key, to check against the signing key list on the Aevo website; an error if the key is malformed. Registration is not checked here; an unregistered key fails when an order is placed. |
| ```api``` | method, path[, params[, raw[, sign]]] | Call an Aevo endpoint directly. (more below the table) | The raw exchange response; an error is raised when the response carries ```error```. |

The rest of the longer descriptions in the table:

- ```api```: Public paths (```/markets```, ```/statistics```, ```/orderbook```, ```/instrument/...```, ```/funding```, ```/coingecko-statistics```; for a full URL ```path```, its path part decides) are unsigned by default and other paths are signed with the API key (```AEVO-KEY```, ```AEVO-SIGNATURE``` and related headers); ```sign``` set to ```true```/```false``` (it may also be given directly as the 4th argument) forces signing on or off. ```GET``` parameters go into the query string, other methods send a JSON body (numbers and booleans keep their types). ```raw``` is not a request body but a parameter table (a JSON object, a JSON string or ```a=1&b=2```) that replaces ```params``` entirely when non-empty. Orders are not EIP-712-signed for the caller.

For the common commands ```base``` and ```currency``` see `exchange.IO`.

##### Common Usage

###### Query markets and the account with api, and switch to another signing key

```javascript
function main() {
    // Public paths are unsigned by default
    var q = {asset: "ETH", instrument_type: "PERPETUAL"}
    var markets = exchange.IO("api", "GET", "/markets", q)
    Log(markets[0].instrument_name, "mark price:", markets[0].mark_price)
    // Other paths are signed with the API key by default
    var account = exchange.IO("api", "GET", "/account")
    Log("Available balance:", account.available_balance, "positions:", account.positions.length)
    // Switch to another registered signing key for this run only; the key's wallet address
    // is returned, to check against the signing key list on the Aevo website
    var addr = exchange.IO("signingKey", "0x...")    // replace with the signing private key
    Log("Signing key address:", addr)
}
```

##### Function Support

Not supported (the call fails with an error and returns null): `exchange.GetTickers`.

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: The exchange has no K-line endpoint; bars are synthesized by the docker from trades. The first call covers only the few bars spanned by recent trades, and more accumulate with later calls. The result is empty while the contract has no trades.

##### Margin, Account and Simulation

Margin mode: Aevo uses a unified margin account with no cross/isolated switch; the margin mode in ```exchange.GetPositions()``` follows the exchange (the position's ```margin_type```, falling back to the account's setting for that contract), and option positions without a per-contract setting are cross. ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()``` sets leverage per perpetual contract; options are not supported. A position's ```MarginLevel``` is the contract's leverage (the position's ```leverage```, falling back to the account's setting for that contract; 0 for options), and ```Margin``` is the initial margin held by the position (```initial_margin```).

Position mode: One-way (net) positions only, no hedge mode. Closing orders (```closebuy```, ```closesell```) are placed as reduce-only.

Account: In ```exchange.GetAccount()```, ```Balance``` is the available USDC balance, ```FrozenBalance``` the initial margin in use and ```Equity``` the account equity; collateral other than USDC is listed per currency in ```exchange.GetAssets()```.

##### Options

Aevo USDC options are supported; orders, cancellations and queries use the same interfaces as perpetuals. Limitations:

- The result of ```exchange.GetMarkets()``` includes option contracts (active ones only), and ```exchange.SetContractType()``` validates option codes against it.
- ```Last``` in ```exchange.GetTicker()``` is the mark price; ```Buy``` and ```Sell``` are 0 when nobody is quoting; ```Open```, ```High``` and ```Low``` are 0.
- ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()``` and ```exchange.GetFundings()``` are not supported.
- Prices and amounts are signed as 6-decimal fixed point; a non-zero price or amount below 0.000001 is rejected.

Option code examples: ```ETH-30JUN23-1600-C```, ```ETH-24SEP27-2800-P```

Option codes are Aevo native codes: underlying-expiry (DDMMMYY)-strike-C/P, C for a call and P for a put. Options settle in USDC; set the trading pair to the underlying plus ```_USDC``` (the underlying must match the pair's base currency), the full symbol looks like ```ETH_USDC.ETH-30JUN23-1600-C```.

##### Notes

- Limit orders only; market orders are rejected. Conditional orders (take-profit, stop-loss) need a limit order price; market take-profit/stop-loss and OCO are not supported.
- Order options go in the last object argument: ```{tif: "ioc"}```, ```{tif: "fok"}``` and ```{postOnly: true}``` map to the exchange's IOC, FOK and post-only; other keys are merged into the order request body as they are (overriding fields of the same name built by the connector).
- ```exchange.ModifyOrder()``` and ```exchange.ModifyConditionOrder()``` have the exchange re-issue the order and return a new order ID, which should be used from then on; ```exchange.ModifyOrder()``` keeps the original order's reduce-only flag. The exchange keeps reporting a conditional order replaced by ```exchange.ModifyConditionOrder()``` as open (it is no longer in the open order list, and cancelling it fails with ```ORDER_DOES_NOT_EXIST```); for conditional orders modified within the same docker process, ```exchange.GetConditionOrder(original ID)``` checks the open order list and returns canceled, while orders modified after a restart or by another process are returned as the exchange reports them.
- When the order query has no average fill price, ```exchange.GetOrder()``` and ```exchange.GetConditionOrder()``` compute ```AvgPrice``` for orders with fills from the exchange's trade history (volume-weighted, one or a few extra requests), and cache the result for finished orders; ```AvgPrice``` is 0 while the fills have not been recorded yet.
- For perpetuals, ```Last``` in ```exchange.GetTicker()``` is the mark price and ```Open``` the mark price 24 hours ago; there is no high or low (```High``` and ```Low``` are 0), and ```Volume``` is the 24-hour volume in contracts.
- Funding is settled every hour; ```exchange.GetFundings()``` returns perpetuals only.
- ```exchange.GetHistoryOrders()``` and ```exchange.GetHistoryConditionOrders()``` query one symbol at a time; an empty string (all symbols) is rejected.
- WebSocket push is supported: market data (ticker, bbo, depth, trades) and the private account stream (order updates, positions, balances) can be subscribed through the event stream, for perpetuals and options. ```exchange.GetTicker()```, ```exchange.GetDepth()``` and the other functions still request the REST API directly, and ```EventLoop()``` does not subscribe to this exchange's push streams by itself. The exchange has no kline stream (and no kline endpoint), so kline subscriptions fail. The ticker is the exchange's 500 ms ticker push with the best bid/ask, their sizes and open interest; ```Last``` is the mark price as in ```exchange.GetTicker()```, and there is no 24-hour volume, open, high or low. bbo is pushed in real time whenever the best bid/ask changes. Aevo has a single depth stream (the whole book on subscription, then deltas every 100 ms): depth subscriptions of any size (20 levels by default, at most 255) share it and each publishes its own number of levels; the full book is verified against the exchange's checksum, and a delta whose timestamp goes backwards or a checksum mismatch resubscribes for a fresh book. Trades carry the same trade IDs as ```exchange.GetTrades()```. The private stream is one ```private``` subscription for the whole account (no symbol). It connects only when subscribed, logs in with a signature made from the API key and secret key, and subscribes to the order, fill and position channels: once active (and again after every reconnect) it first pushes a balance and position snapshot from the same endpoints as ```exchange.GetAssets()``` and ```exchange.GetPositions()```, then reports ready, and afterwards pushes order updates (orders already open when subscribing are not reported again) and positions that changed (one-way net positions; a closed position is pushed with quantity 0; the push carries no leverage, so the leverage of the latest snapshot is kept). The exchange has no balance push: after an order, fill or position push the connector re-reads the balances from the same endpoint as ```exchange.GetAssets()``` and pushes the coins that changed. A rejected signature reports a degraded connection status and a failed private stream (market data push is unaffected). A market-wide ```tickers``` subscription is not supported (Aevo ticker push is per instrument only) and fails at subscribe; subscribe ticker per symbol.

#### Pendle

```Pendle``` (Spot): Trades Pendle PT (principal tokens) and YT (yield tokens). One exchange object corresponds to one wallet on one chain: market orders are swaps built by Pendle's convert API, limit orders rest on Pendle's limit order book, and the docker signs transactions and orders with the configured private key. Supported chains: Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, BNB Chain, HyperEVM, Plasma, Robinhood, Monad, X Layer.

```Futures_Boros``` (Futures): Trades Pendle Boros funding-rate swaps (Yield Units, YU): on an on-chain order book on Arbitrum, buy or sell the funding rate of perpetual exchanges (Hyperliquid, Binance, OKX, Gate, KuCoin, Bybit, Lighter and more) at a fixed annualized rate, settled hourly until maturity. One exchange object corresponds to one Boros sub-account (cross margin) of one wallet. Orders cost no ETH from the wallet: the docker derives an agent key from the wallet private key, the wallet approves it by signature before the first order, and every order is then signed by the agent and put on chain by Pendle's relayer, with the relay fee taken from the Boros account's gas balance.

##### Names and Configuration

| ```exchange.GetName()``` | Type | Aliases |
| - | - | - |
| ```Pendle``` | Spot | Pendle Finance, PT, YT |
| ```Futures_Boros``` | Futures | Boros, Pendle Boros, Futures_Boros |

✓ marks the exchange objects that have the field.

| Field | ```Pendle``` | ```Futures_Boros``` | Required | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| Chain | ✓ |  | Yes | ```Ethereum``` | The chain of the wallet and the trades; it also determines the default nodes and the native coin's name. Options: ```Ethereum```, ```Arbitrum```, ```Base```, ```BNB Chain```, ```HyperEVM```, ```Plasma```, ```Robinhood```, ```Monad```, ```X Layer``` |
| Wallet Private Key | ✓ |  | Yes | — | The EVM wallet private key (hex). |
| RPC Address | ✓ |  | No | ```https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com,https://eth.drpc.org``` | RPC nodes; separate several with commas, and the next one is used automatically when a node fails. Choosing a chain fills in its default nodes. |
| RPC Auth | ✓ |  | No | — | Optional. For RPC nodes that need authentication: a header in the form ```Header-Name: value```, or a Basic auth value. |
| Wallet Private Key |  | ✓ | Yes | — | The EVM wallet private key (hex). The docker derives the trading agent from it and signs the approval once; deposits and withdrawals are signed with it too. |
| Sub-account |  | ✓ | No | ```0``` | The Boros sub-account id; 0 is the main account (only it can deposit and withdraw), range 0 to 254. |
| API Address |  | ✓ | No | ```https://api-boros.pendle.finance/apis``` | The Boros API address; normally left as is. |
| RPC Address |  | ✓ | No | ```https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc,https://arbitrum-one-rpc.publicnode.com``` | Arbitrum RPC nodes (for deposits, withdrawals and on-chain nonce reads); separate several with commas, and the next one is used when a node fails. |

##### Trading Pairs and Contract Codes

###### ```Pendle``` (Spot)

Pair examples: ```PT-apyUSD-5NOV2026_apyUSD```, ```YT-apyUSD-5NOV2026_USDC```

The first part is the PT or YT name (with its expiry, taken from Pendle's asset list; see ```exchange.GetMarkets()```) and the second part is the quote token. The price is how many quote tokens one PT/YT is worth. The quote can be the market's underlying asset, its accounting asset, or any other token Pendle can swap on the chain (market orders route through an aggregator), or a token contract address. Pairs are not upper-cased; write them as they are.

###### ```Futures_Boros``` (Futures)

Pair examples: ```BTC_USDT```, ```ETH_ETH```, ```BTC_BTC```

Pairs are ```underlying_collateral```: the underlying is the asset whose funding rate is traded, the collateral is the market's margin token (WBTC is written ```BTC```, WETH ```ETH```, USD₮0 ```USDT```, plus ```BNB``` and ```HYPE```). The same market name can exist with two collaterals (for example Hyperliquid BTC with USDT and with BTC margin); the collateral tells them apart. The price is the annualized rate as a decimal (```0.065``` means 6.5%) and can be negative; the amount is YU in the collateral token (in a USDT-margined market 1 YU is the funding on 1 USDT of notional).

Contract codes are Boros market names with underscores, ```funding source_asset_maturity```, such as ```HYPERLIQUID_BTC_30OCT2026``` or ```BINANCE_ETHUSDT_25DEC2026```; a full symbol looks like ```BTC_USDT.HYPERLIQUID_BTC_30OCT2026```. The Boros name itself (```HYPERLIQUID-BTC-30OCT2026```) also works. ```exchange.GetMarkets()``` lists the available markets (unmatured only). Boros's numeric market id (such as ```206```) also works.

##### Exchange-specific IO Commands

###### ```Pendle``` (Spot)

| Command | Arguments | Description | Returns |
| - | - | - | - |
| ```market``` | symbol | The market of a pair: expiry, years to expiry, current implied APY, the PT/YT/SY, underlying and accounting asset addresses, and how much accounting asset one quote token is worth (used by the limit-order conversion). | ```{symbol, market, name, kind, expiry, yearsToExpiry, impliedApy, pt, yt, sy, underlying, accounting, accountingPerQuote, chainId}```: ```kind``` is ```PT``` or ```YT```, ```expiry``` is a timestamp in milliseconds and the addresses are contract addresses; ```accountingPerQuote``` is null when the quote token cannot be converted through the SY (such as ```USDC``` swapped through an aggregator). |
| ```apy``` | symbol, price | Convert a PT/YT price to an implied APY (the same conversion limit orders use): the quote is converted to the accounting asset at the SY rate, PT price = (1 + APY)^(−years to expiry), YT price = 1 − PT price. The quote token must be one the SY can convert (as for limit orders); otherwise it fails. | The implied APY (0.16 means 16%); an error and null when the price has no implied APY (a PT at or above one accounting asset, a YT outside 0 to 1) or the market has expired. |
| ```price``` | symbol, apy | The reverse of ```apy```, converting an implied APY to a price in the quote token; the quote token must meet the same condition as for ```apy```. | The price. |
| ```slippage``` | [ratio] | Slippage protection of market orders, range ```[0, 0.5)```, default ```0.005``` (0.5%), written into the swap transaction. The order option ```slippage``` overrides it for one order. Queries when called without an argument. | The current slippage ratio. |
| ```orderExpiry``` | [seconds] | Default lifetime of limit orders in seconds, 60 to 31536000 (one year), 604800 (7 days) by default, never beyond the market's expiry. (more below the table) | The current lifetime (seconds). |
| ```cancelWait``` | [seconds] | How long a cancel waits for the cancel transaction to be mined, default 30, range 0 to 600. On timeout ```exchange.CancelOrder()``` still returns ```true```, meaning the cancel was submitted. Queries when called without an argument. | The current wait (seconds). |
| ```approve``` | [mode] | Approval amount: ```max``` for unlimited, ```exact``` for just what the order needs (the default). Swaps approve the Pendle Router, limit orders the Pendle limit order contract. Queries when called without an argument. | The current mode. |
| ```gasMultiplier``` | [x] | gasLimit = estimated gas × x, range 1 to 5, default 1.2. Queries when called without an argument. | The current multiplier. |
| ```receipt``` | txHash[, waitMs] | Query a transaction receipt: status, block, gas and fee, optionally waiting until it is mined (up to 10 minutes). For a swap order, pass the transaction hash after the comma in the order ID. | ```{txHash, status, blockNumber, gasUsed, fee}```, where ```status``` is ```success```, ```reverted``` or ```pending```; while not mined (```pending```) only ```txHash``` and ```status``` are present. |
| ```base``` | [url] | Without an argument, returns the current RPC node address; with an address, switches the node (separate several with commas), and the first request afterwards checks that the node is on the configured chain. | The previous address. |
| ```address``` | — | The wallet address. | — |
| ```abi``` | address, abiContent | Register the ABI of a contract address (a JSON string, or one of the built-in templates ```weth```, ```uniswapV3Pool```, ```uniswapV3Factory```, ```uniswapV3QuoterV2```, ```uniswapV3SwapRouter02```, ```uniswapV3PositionManager```, ```permit2```, with matching ```pancakeV3*``` aliases for PancakeSwap V3), for this exchange object only. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("abi", ...)`. | — |
| ```api``` | address \| "eth", method, ...args[, options] | With a contract address as the first argument, calls a contract method; read-only methods (```view```, ```pure```) return the decoded value, and write methods are signed with the configured wallet key and broadcast and return the transaction hash (a payable method takes the native amount as its first argument; ```options``` may set ```gasLimit```, ```gasPrice```, ```nonce```, ```dryRun```). See the sub-page `exchange.IO("api", ...)`. | — |
| ```call``` | address, method \| calldata, ...args[, options] | Simulate any contract method (including write methods) with ```eth_call```, without signing, broadcasting or spending gas, for quotes and dry runs; the arguments are as for ```api```, ```options``` is ```{from, value, block, gasLimit}```, and the caller defaults to this wallet. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("call", ...)`. | The decoded value when called by method name (```true``` for a method without return values); the raw return data (a hex string) when called with calldata. |
| ```multicall``` | calls[, options] | Read several contract calls in one request on the same block state through the Multicall3 contract; each item of ```calls``` is ```[address, method, ...args]```, and ```options``` is ```{allowFailure, block, multicall}```. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("multicall", ...)`. | An array of results in the order of ```calls```. By default any failing item fails the whole call (with its index and reason); with ```allowFailure``` ```true```, failed items are null. |
| ```logs``` | query | Query a contract's event logs (```eth_getLogs```) and decode them by ABI; ```query``` is ```{address, event, filter, fromBlock, toBlock, topics, blockHash}```, and block numbers may be negative (relative to the latest block). See the sub-page `exchange.IO("logs", ...)`. | An array of logs, each with ```event``` and ```args``` when it can be decoded. |
| ```waitReceipt``` | txHash[, options] | Wait until a transaction is mined and has the required confirmations; ```options``` is ```{timeout, confirmations, interval}```: ```timeout``` and ```interval``` are in milliseconds, 120000 (1000 to 600000) and 1500 by default, and ```confirmations``` defaults to 1. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("waitReceipt", ...)`. | The transaction receipt (```status``` as a number, ```events``` decoded); an error and null on timeout. |
| ```nonce``` | ["sync" \| number] | Show the nonce counter this exchange object sends with (shared by ```api``` writes and swaps, limit-order cancels and the like); ```sync``` resyncs it from the node's pending count, and a number sets the next local nonce. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("nonce", ...)`. | ```{address, latest, pending, local}``` (all values are strings; ```local``` is null before any transaction has been sent). |
| ```speedUp``` | txHash[, options] | Resend a pending transaction with a higher fee (same nonce, recipient, amount, call data and gas limit); ```options``` is ```{multiplier, dryRun}```, ```multiplier``` 1.1 to 10, default 1.125. The transaction must come from this wallet and be visible to the node. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("speedUp", ...)`. | The replacement transaction's hash; its content with ```dryRun```. |
| ```cancelTx``` | txHash[, options] | Cancel a pending transaction by sending a zero-amount transaction to yourself with the same nonce and a higher fee; ```options``` as for ```speedUp```. Success is not guaranteed. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("cancelTx", ...)`. | The cancel transaction's hash; its content with ```dryRun```. |
| ```encode``` | [address, ]dataFormat, ...args | Standard ABI encoding by a type list (like Solidity's ```abi.encode```); with a contract address as the first argument, encodes a method call of that contract (calldata). ```pack``` is an older name of the same command. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("encode", ...)`. | A hex string without ```0x```. |
| ```encodePacked``` | dataFormat, ...args | Packed encoding by a type list (like Solidity's ```abi.encodePacked```). See the sub-page `exchange.IO("encodePacked", ...)`. | A hex string without ```0x```. |
| ```decode``` | dataFormat, data | Decode hex data by a type list. ```unpack``` is an older name of the same command. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("decode", ...)`. | The value itself for a single type, an array for several. |
| ```sign``` | hash[, key] | Sign a 32-byte hash with a secp256k1 private key (no further hashing), for off-chain signatures such as EIP-712; the configured wallet key is used when ```key``` is omitted. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("sign", ...)`. | ```{r, s, v, signature, vs}``` (```v``` is 27 or 28, ```vs``` the EIP-2098 compact signature). |
| ```signTypedData``` | typedData[, key] \| domain, types, message[, key] | Sign structured data per EIP-712 (Permit2 permits, limit orders and the like), computing the type hash, domain separator, struct hash and digest in one call. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("signTypedData", ...)`. | As for ```sign```, plus ```digest``` (the EIP-712 digest). |
| ```signMessage``` | message[, key] | Sign a message per EIP-191 (```personal_sign```); a string is signed as UTF-8, raw bytes are passed as ```{hex: "0x..."}```. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("signMessage", ...)`. | As for ```sign```, plus ```digest``` (the EIP-191 message hash). |
| ```toUnits``` | amount, decimals | Convert a readable amount into an on-chain integer with exact string arithmetic; ```decimals``` may be a number or a token contract address (its ```decimals()``` is read). More fractional digits than the precision fail. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("toUnits", ...)`. | A decimal string. |
| ```fromUnits``` | amount, decimals | Convert an on-chain integer into a readable amount with exact string arithmetic; ```decimals``` as for ```toUnits```. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("fromUnits", ...)`. | A decimal string (trailing zeros removed). |
| ```uniswapV3``` | fn, ...args | Concentrated-liquidity math: ```tickToPrice```, ```priceToTick```, ```sqrtPriceToPrice```, ```tickToSqrtPrice```, ```sqrtPriceToTick```, ```nearestUsableTick```, ```amountsForLiquidity```, ```liquidityForAmounts```; precision arguments may be numbers or token addresses. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("uniswapV3", ...)`. | — |

The rest of the longer descriptions in the table:

- ```orderExpiry```: The order option ```expiry``` sets the expiry of one order as a timestamp in seconds or milliseconds (a point in time, not a duration); a time already past fails, and a time after the market's expiry becomes one minute before it. Queries when called without an argument.

For the common command ```currency``` see `exchange.IO`.

###### ```Futures_Boros``` (Futures)

| Command | Arguments | Description | Returns |
| - | - | - | - |
| ```address``` | — | The wallet address (the root address of the Boros account). | — |
| ```agent``` | — | The trading agent: its address, the sub-account, and the approval expiry (Unix seconds, 0 when not approved). Read-only; the agent is approved automatically before the first order and renewed when less than a day is left. | ```{agent, accountId, expiry, approved}``` |
| ```approveAgent``` | — | Have the wallet sign a (re)approval of the trading agent right away, valid for 30 days. The approval goes on chain through Pendle's relayer and costs no ETH from the wallet. The agent can only place and cancel orders and pay gas; it cannot withdraw. | ```{agent, expiry}``` |
| ```gasBalance``` | — | The Boros relayer gas balance in USD. Each order or cancel costs about $0.02 to $0.04; the relayer refuses submissions below a floor. | The balance in USD; negative means debt. |
| ```topUpGas``` | usd[, currency] | Pay the gas balance from the cross account's cash; ```usd``` is the USD amount (at most 100) and ```currency``` the collateral to pay with, ```USDT``` by default. | ```{txHash, usd, paid, currency}``` |
| ```autoTopUp``` | [enabled[, usd]] | Automatic gas top-up: when on (the default) and the gas balance is below $0.3, an order first pays ```usd``` dollars (default 1, above 0 and at most 20, plus any debt) from the cross cash of the market's collateral, in the same batch. ```enabled``` must be a boolean (```true```/```false```); any other value leaves the switch unchanged. Queries when called without arguments. | ```{enabled, usd}``` |
| ```slippage``` | [rate] | The maximum distance of a market order from the mark rate (a decimal rate, default ```0.01```, one percentage point), range 0 to 0.5. The order option ```slippage``` overrides it for one order. Queries when called without an argument. | The current value. |
| ```base``` | [url] | Query or switch the Boros API base URL (default ```https://api-boros.pendle.finance/apis```). | The address before the switch. |
| ```rpc``` | [url] | Query or switch the Arbitrum RPC nodes (used for deposits, withdrawals and on-chain nonce reads); separate several with commas. | The address before the switch. |
| ```market``` | symbol | The raw market data: fees, margin parameters, mark rate, underlying funding rate, maturity and more. ```symbol``` must be a full symbol (such as ```BTC_USDT.HYPERLIQUID_BTC_27NOV2026```); the same holds for ```tick``` and ```isolatedTransfer```. | The Boros ```/v1/markets/by-ids``` response ```{results, ...}```: ```results[0]``` is the market, with ```marketId```, ```imData``` (```symbol```, ```maturity```, ```tickStep```, ```isIsolatedOnly``` and more) and ```data``` (```markApr```, ```floatingApr```, ```bestBid```, ```bestAsk```, ```nextSettlementTime``` and more; times in Unix seconds). |
| ```tick``` | symbol, rate[, side] | Convert a rate to a limit tick: a long (```buy```, the default) takes the nearest step not above the rate, a short (```sell```) the nearest step not below it, the same rounding orders use. | ```{market, marketId, tick, rate, tickStep}```, where ```rate``` is the actual rate of the tick. |
| ```deposit``` | currency, amount | A wallet transaction: deposit a collateral token from the wallet into the Boros cross account (approving the Boros Router first); pays ETH gas from the wallet and returns once mined. | ```{txHash, currency, amount, accountId}``` |
| ```withdraw``` | currency, amount | A wallet transaction: request a withdrawal from the cross account to the wallet, from the main account (sub-account 0) only. Boros completes it automatically after the cooldown (about 15 minutes at present); another request during the cooldown adds to the amount and restarts the timer. | ```{txHash, currency, amount, note}``` |
| ```cancelWithdraw``` | currency | A wallet transaction: cancel a pending withdrawal request. | ```{txHash, currency}``` |
| ```isolatedTransfer``` | symbol, amount | Move cash between the cross account and the isolated account of an isolated-only market: a positive ```amount``` (in the collateral) moves it from cross into isolated, a negative one moves it back. Goes through the relayer and uses the gas balance. Withdrawals come from the cross account only, so move isolated cash back first. | ```{txHash, symbol, amount, account}``` |
| ```wallet``` | — | The wallet's (not the Boros account's) ETH and collateral token balances on Arbitrum, for checking before a deposit. | ```[{currency, amount, token}]```; the first item is the wallet's ETH (```currency``` is ```ETH (gas)```, without ```token```). |
| ```abi``` | address, abiContent | Register the ABI of a contract address (a JSON string, or one of the built-in templates ```weth```, ```uniswapV3Pool```, ```uniswapV3Factory```, ```uniswapV3QuoterV2```, ```uniswapV3SwapRouter02```, ```uniswapV3PositionManager```, ```permit2```, with matching ```pancakeV3*``` aliases for PancakeSwap V3), for this exchange object only. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("abi", ...)`. | — |
| ```api``` | address \| "eth", method, ...args[, options] | With a contract address as the first argument, calls a contract method; read-only methods (```view```, ```pure```) return the decoded value, and write methods are signed with the configured wallet key and broadcast and return the transaction hash (a payable method takes the native amount as its first argument; ```options``` may set ```gasLimit```, ```gasPrice```, ```nonce```, ```dryRun```). See the sub-page `exchange.IO("api", ...)`. | — |
| ```call``` | address, method \| calldata, ...args[, options] | Simulate any contract method (including write methods) with ```eth_call```, without signing, broadcasting or spending gas, for quotes and dry runs; the arguments are as for ```api```, ```options``` is ```{from, value, block, gasLimit}```, and the caller defaults to this wallet. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("call", ...)`. | The decoded value when called by method name (```true``` for a method without return values); the raw return data (a hex string) when called with calldata. |
| ```multicall``` | calls[, options] | Read several contract calls in one request on the same block state through the Multicall3 contract; each item of ```calls``` is ```[address, method, ...args]```, and ```options``` is ```{allowFailure, block, multicall}```. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("multicall", ...)`. | An array of results in the order of ```calls```. By default any failing item fails the whole call (with its index and reason); with ```allowFailure``` ```true```, failed items are null. |
| ```logs``` | query | Query a contract's event logs (```eth_getLogs```) and decode them by ABI; ```query``` is ```{address, event, filter, fromBlock, toBlock, topics, blockHash}```, and block numbers may be negative (relative to the latest block). See the sub-page `exchange.IO("logs", ...)`. | An array of logs, each with ```event``` and ```args``` when it can be decoded. |
| ```waitReceipt``` | txHash[, options] | Wait until a transaction is mined and has the required confirmations; ```options``` is ```{timeout, confirmations, interval}```: ```timeout``` and ```interval``` are in milliseconds, 120000 (1000 to 600000) and 1500 by default, and ```confirmations``` defaults to 1. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("waitReceipt", ...)`. | The transaction receipt (```status``` as a number, ```events``` decoded); an error and null on timeout. |
| ```nonce``` | ["sync" \| number] | Show the nonce counter this exchange object sends with (shared by ```api``` writes and wallet transactions such as deposits and withdrawals); ```sync``` resyncs it from the node's pending count, and a number sets the next local nonce. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("nonce", ...)`. | ```{address, latest, pending, local}``` (all values are strings; ```local``` is null before any transaction has been sent). |
| ```speedUp``` | txHash[, options] | Resend a pending transaction with a higher fee (same nonce, recipient, amount, call data and gas limit); ```options``` is ```{multiplier, dryRun}```, ```multiplier``` 1.1 to 10, default 1.125. The transaction must come from this wallet and be visible to the node. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("speedUp", ...)`. | The replacement transaction's hash; its content with ```dryRun```. |
| ```cancelTx``` | txHash[, options] | Cancel a pending transaction by sending a zero-amount transaction to yourself with the same nonce and a higher fee; ```options``` as for ```speedUp```. Success is not guaranteed. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("cancelTx", ...)`. | The cancel transaction's hash; its content with ```dryRun```. |
| ```encode``` | [address, ]dataFormat, ...args | Standard ABI encoding by a type list (like Solidity's ```abi.encode```); with a contract address as the first argument, encodes a method call of that contract (calldata). ```pack``` is an older name of the same command. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("encode", ...)`. | A hex string without ```0x```. |
| ```encodePacked``` | dataFormat, ...args | Packed encoding by a type list (like Solidity's ```abi.encodePacked```). See the sub-page `exchange.IO("encodePacked", ...)`. | A hex string without ```0x```. |
| ```decode``` | dataFormat, data | Decode hex data by a type list. ```unpack``` is an older name of the same command. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("decode", ...)`. | The value itself for a single type, an array for several. |
| ```sign``` | hash[, key] | Sign a 32-byte hash with a secp256k1 private key (no further hashing), for off-chain signatures such as EIP-712; the configured wallet key is used when ```key``` is omitted. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("sign", ...)`. | ```{r, s, v, signature, vs}``` (```v``` is 27 or 28, ```vs``` the EIP-2098 compact signature). |
| ```signTypedData``` | typedData[, key] \| domain, types, message[, key] | Sign structured data per EIP-712 (Permit2 permits, limit orders and the like), computing the type hash, domain separator, struct hash and digest in one call. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("signTypedData", ...)`. | As for ```sign```, plus ```digest``` (the EIP-712 digest). |
| ```signMessage``` | message[, key] | Sign a message per EIP-191 (```personal_sign```); a string is signed as UTF-8, raw bytes are passed as ```{hex: "0x..."}```. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("signMessage", ...)`. | As for ```sign```, plus ```digest``` (the EIP-191 message hash). |
| ```toUnits``` | amount, decimals | Convert a readable amount into an on-chain integer with exact string arithmetic; ```decimals``` may be a number or a token contract address (its ```decimals()``` is read). More fractional digits than the precision fail. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("toUnits", ...)`. | A decimal string. |
| ```fromUnits``` | amount, decimals | Convert an on-chain integer into a readable amount with exact string arithmetic; ```decimals``` as for ```toUnits```. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("fromUnits", ...)`. | A decimal string (trailing zeros removed). |
| ```uniswapV3``` | fn, ...args | Concentrated-liquidity math: ```tickToPrice```, ```priceToTick```, ```sqrtPriceToPrice```, ```tickToSqrtPrice```, ```sqrtPriceToTick```, ```nearestUsableTick```, ```amountsForLiquidity```, ```liquidityForAmounts```; precision arguments may be numbers or token addresses. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("uniswapV3", ...)`. | — |

For the common command ```currency``` see `exchange.IO`.

##### Common Usage

###### Read a PT market and convert between price and implied APY (Pendle only)

```javascript
function main() {
    var symbol = "PT-apyUSD-11FEB2027_apyUSD"
    var m = exchange.IO("market", symbol)
    if (!m) {
        Log("Market query failed:", GetLastError())
        return
    }
    Log(m.kind, m.name, "expiry:", _D(m.expiry), "years to expiry:", m.yearsToExpiry)
    Log("implied APY now:", m.impliedApy, "accounting asset per quote:", m.accountingPerQuote)
    var t = exchange.GetTicker(symbol)
    if (t) {
        // The APY locked in by buying at the best ask
        Log("ask:", t.Sell, "implied APY:", exchange.IO("apy", symbol, t.Sell))
    }
    // The buy price for an APY one point above the current one (a lower PT price)
    var price = exchange.IO("price", symbol, m.impliedApy + 0.01)
    Log("price for the target APY:", price)
}
```

###### Place a PT limit buy at a target APY and cancel it if it has not filled after a while (Pendle only)

```javascript
function main() {
    var symbol = "PT-apyUSD-11FEB2027_apyUSD"
    exchange.IO("orderExpiry", 86400)    // limit orders placed from now on expire after 1 day
    exchange.IO("approve", "max")        // approve the paying token in full (default: per order)
    exchange.IO("cancelWait", 60)        // wait up to 60 seconds for a cancel to be mined
    var m = exchange.IO("market", symbol)
    var apy = m.impliedApy + 0.01
    var price = exchange.IO("price", symbol, apy)
    var id = exchange.CreateOrder(symbol, "buy", price, 10)    // the amount is in PT
    if (!id) {
        Log("Order failed:", GetLastError())
        return
    }
    Log("limit order:", id, "price:", price, "APY:", apy)
    Sleep(10 * 60 * 1000)
    var o = exchange.GetOrder(id)
    if (o && o.Status == ORDER_STATE_PENDING) {
        // Canceling is an on-chain transaction and costs gas
        Log("cancel:", exchange.CancelOrder(id), "filled:", o.DealAmount)
    }
}
```

###### Buy PT at market, then read the transaction receipt (Pendle only)

```javascript
function main() {
    var symbol = "PT-apyUSD-11FEB2027_USDC"    // quoted in USDC, swapped through an aggregator
    exchange.IO("slippage", 0.003)              // 0.3% slippage protection
    var id = exchange.CreateOrder(symbol, "buy", -1, 20)    // market buy: spend 20 USDC
    if (!id) {
        Log("Swap failed:", GetLastError())
        return
    }
    // A swap order ID is "pair,txHash"; wait up to 2 minutes for it to be mined
    var r = exchange.IO("receipt", id.split(",")[1], 120000)
    Log("status:", r.status, "block:", r.blockNumber, "gas:", r.gasUsed, "fee:", r.fee)
    if (r.status == "success") {
        var o = exchange.GetOrder(id)
        Log("PT bought:", o.DealAmount, "average price:", o.AvgPrice)
    }
}
```

###### Check the trading agent and the gas balance, and top up gas by hand when it runs low (Futures_Boros only)

```javascript
function main() {
    Log("wallet:", exchange.IO("address"))
    var a = exchange.IO("agent")
    if (!a) {
        Log("Agent query failed:", GetLastError())
        return
    }
    Log("agent:", a.agent, "sub-account:", a.accountId, "approved:", a.approved)
    // Renew early when less than 3 days are left (wallet signature, relayed, no ETH spent)
    if (!a.approved || a.expiry - Date.now() / 1000 < 3 * 86400) {
        var r = exchange.IO("approveAgent")
        Log("agent approved until:", _D(r.expiry * 1000))
    }
    var gas = exchange.IO("gasBalance")
    Log("gas balance (USD):", gas)
    if (gas < 0.5) {
        var t = exchange.IO("topUpGas", 2, "USDT")    // pay $2 from the USDT cross cash
        Log("gas topped up:", t.paid, t.currency, t.txHash)
    }
    // Automatic top-up before orders: keep it on, paying $3 each time
    Log(exchange.IO("autoTopUp", true, 3))
}
```

###### Deposit from the wallet, move margin into an isolated-only market, then request a withdrawal (Futures_Boros only)

```javascript
function main() {
    // The wallet's (not the Boros account's) balances on Arbitrum
    var w = exchange.IO("wallet")
    for (var i = 0; i < w.length; i++) {
        Log(w[i].currency, w[i].amount)
    }
    // A wallet transaction: pays ETH gas from the wallet and returns once mined
    var d = exchange.IO("deposit", "USDT", 50)
    if (!d) {
        Log("Deposit failed:", GetLastError())
        return
    }
    Log("deposited", d.amount, d.currency, "into sub-account", d.accountId, d.txHash)
    // Isolated-only market: positive moves cash from cross into it, negative moves it back
    var iso = "BRENTOIL_USDT.HYPERLIQUID_XYZBRENTOIL_18NOV2026"
    Log(exchange.IO("isolatedTransfer", iso, 20))
    Log(exchange.IO("isolatedTransfer", iso, -20))
    // Request a withdrawal (from the cross account of sub-account 0 only), paid after cooldown
    var r = exchange.IO("withdraw", "USDT", 30)
    Log(r ? r.note : GetLastError())
    // Cancel during the cooldown with exchange.IO("cancelWithdraw", "USDT")
}
```

###### Read a market's mark rate and underlying funding rate, and see which tick a target rate rounds to (Futures_Boros only)

```javascript
function main() {
    var symbol = "BTC_USDT.HYPERLIQUID_BTC_27NOV2026"
    var r = exchange.IO("market", symbol)
    if (!r) {
        Log("Query failed:", GetLastError())
        return
    }
    var m = r.results[0]
    Log(m.imData.symbol, "market id:", m.marketId, "isolated only:", m.imData.isIsolatedOnly)
    Log("mark rate:", m.data.markApr, "underlying funding rate:", m.data.floatingApr,
        "next settlement:", _D(m.data.nextSettlementTime * 1000))
    // A long half a point below the mark rate: see which tick it rounds to first
    var t = exchange.IO("tick", symbol, m.data.markApr - 0.005, "buy")
    Log("tick:", t.tick, "actual rate:", t.rate, "tickStep:", t.tickStep)
}
```

##### Function Support

###### ```Pendle``` (Spot)

Not supported (the call fails with an error and returns null): `exchange.GetTickers`, `exchange.GetRecords`, `exchange.GetTrades`, `exchange.ModifyOrder`, `exchange.CreateConditionOrder`, `exchange.ModifyConditionOrder`, `exchange.CancelConditionOrder`, `exchange.GetConditionOrder`, `exchange.GetConditionOrders`, `exchange.GetHistoryConditionOrders`.

###### ```Futures_Boros``` (Futures)

Not supported (the call fails with an error and returns null): `exchange.GetTickers`, `exchange.SetMarginLevel`, `exchange.ModifyConditionOrder`.

##### Margin, Account and Simulation

###### ```Futures_Boros``` (Futures)

Margin mode: Ordinary markets use the cross account (one per collateral token, shared by every market of that collateral); isolated-only markets (some commodity funding-rate markets) use their own isolated account automatically, funded first with ```exchange.IO("isolatedTransfer", ...)``` or along with an order through the option ```cashIn```. Boros has no leverage setting: the initial margin follows the position size, the rate and the time to maturity.

Position mode: One-way positions. Boros has no reduce-only flag: closing orders (```closebuy```, ```closesell```) are opposite orders capped at the current position (the exact position size when within one part per billion of it), and fail without an order when there is no position in that direction.

Account: ```exchange.GetAccount()``` reads the cross account of the current pair's collateral (the isolated account for an isolated-only market): ```Balance``` is the available initial margin, ```FrozenBalance``` the initial margin in use, ```Equity``` the account's net value (cash plus position value). In ```exchange.GetPositions()```, ```Price``` is the fixed annualized entry rate, ```Profit``` the unrealized PnL, and ```Margin``` the initial margin the position uses in the account that holds it (cross or isolated), all in the collateral; a matured position awaiting settlement has a ```Margin``` of 0.

##### Notes

###### ```Pendle``` (Spot)

| Function | Pendle behavior |
| - | - |
| exchange.GetTicker() | Buy/Sell are Pendle's live executable swap rates (AMM and limit orders matched, fees included); when the live rates are missing, or the market's SY cannot convert the quote token (a token swapped through an aggregator, such as USDC on some markets), a quote for about $1000 is used instead (shrinking to $100 and $10 when that cannot be filled) and ```Info.source``` is ```convert```; ```Info``` carries ```impliedApy``` and ```expiry``` (milliseconds). No 24h statistics: ```High```, ```Low```, ```Open``` are the current price and ```Volume``` is 0 |
| exchange.GetDepth() | Pendle's order book (limit orders and the AMM combined), grouped by 0.01% implied APY and converted to prices. When the market's SY cannot convert the quote token, the whole book is scaled by executable quotes for about $1000 (the mid matches ```exchange.GetTicker()``` and the relative structure of the levels is kept; without a quote, the USD prices of the two tokens are used as an approximation), and ```Info.approximate``` says how |
| exchange.GetMarkets() | For each active market, PT and YT against the underlying asset and the accounting asset; ```Info``` carries the market address, expiry, implied APY and PT/YT/SY addresses |
| exchange.GetAssets() | The native coin and every PT, YT, underlying asset etc. with a non-zero balance |
| exchange.CreateOrder() | Price -1 swaps immediately: for a market buy ```amount``` is the quote to spend, for a sell the PT/YT amount, with slippage protection. A price above 0 places a resting limit order on Pendle's book, with ```amount``` in PT/YT (a buy pays ```amount``` × price of the quote token): the price is converted to an implied APY via the accounting-asset rate and years to expiry (see ```exchange.IO("apy", ...)```). Order options go in the last object argument, e.g. ```exchange.CreateOrder(symbol, "buy", price, amount, {expiry: 1793836800})```: ```impliedApy``` places a limit order at an APY directly (a buy still pays ```amount``` × price of the quote token), ```expiry``` is the limit order's expiry (a timestamp in seconds or milliseconds, see ```exchange.IO("orderExpiry", ...)```), and ```slippage``` is the slippage of one market order; a value that is not a number fails |
| exchange.GetOrder() | Swap order IDs are ```pair,txHash``` with the state from the receipt, and a swap sent by this process that the node still cannot find after 5 minutes is canceled; limit order IDs are ```pair,lo-orderHash``` with state, filled amount and average price from Pendle (still pending while partially filled). Pendle takes 15 to 40 seconds to index on-chain cancels and fills; until then the state follows the chain: once this process's cancel transaction is mined successfully the order shows as canceled right away, and an order that is fully filled or canceled on chain shows that state right away when the filled amount can be reconciled (from the on-chain fill events for orders placed by this process). ```Info.onChain``` holds the remaining and filled amounts on chain, and ```Info.indexed``` is ```false``` while Pendle has not caught up. For limit orders not placed by this process (after a restart, for example), the price is converted back from the order's implied APY at the current rate and is approximate |
| exchange.GetOrders() | The wallet's resting limit orders (orders already canceled or filled on chain are left out), plus swaps sent by this process that are not mined yet |
| exchange.CancelOrder() | Limit orders: sends an on-chain cancel transaction and waits for it (see ```exchange.IO("cancelWait", ...)```). An order already canceled or fully filled on chain fails right away with an error saying which, without sending a transaction; it also fails while an earlier cancel transaction is still waiting to be mined (within 5 minutes), which can be checked with ```exchange.IO("receipt", ...)```. Swaps cannot be canceled |
| exchange.GetHistoryOrders() | The wallet's finished (filled, canceled, expired) limit orders, including ones finished on chain that Pendle has not indexed yet; swaps are not included |

Limit orders can only pay with or pay out tokens the market's SY accepts (usually the underlying and accounting assets); another quote token fails with the list of usable tokens. The token given is approved to the Pendle limit order contract automatically before placing; placing itself is off-chain and costs no gas, while canceling is an on-chain transaction.

Pendle's API is rate-limited by computing units (200 per minute: a swap quote costs at least 5, the order book 5, live prices 1). Keep market-data polling reasonable; when rate-limited the connector waits for the next minute and retries once.

###### ```Futures_Boros``` (Futures)

| Function | Boros behavior |
| - | - |
| exchange.GetTicker() | ```Last``` is the last traded rate, ```Buy``` and ```Sell``` the best bid and ask rates, ```High```, ```Low``` and ```Open``` come from the last 24 one-hour candles, and ```Volume``` is the 24h volume (YU); ```Info``` carries the mark rate ```markApr```, the underlying funding rate ```floatingApr```, the next settlement time and more |
| exchange.GetDepth() | The Boros order book (AMM included), grouped by 0.0001 of rate |
| exchange.GetTrades() | Recent trades of the market; Boros has no trade IDs, so ```Id``` is synthesized from the transaction hash, size and rate |
| exchange.GetRecords() | Native periods are 5 minutes, 1 hour, 1 day and 1 week; other periods are synthesized by the docker. Candle values are rates; periods without trades repeat the previous close |
| exchange.GetFundings() | The current funding rate of the underlying perpetual exchange: ```Rate``` is the annualized ```floatingApr``` scaled to one settlement period (1 hour), and ```Interval``` is the settlement period. Without a pair it returns every unmatured market, from the market list cached for up to 10 minutes |
| exchange.CreateOrder() | Limit orders are GTC by default (the option ```tif``` can be ```ioc```, ```fok``` or ```postOnly```); the rate is rounded to a tick in the trader's favor (a long never above, a short never below the given rate), and the given rate also guards the average fill rate. Price -1 is a market order: IOC within the mark rate ± slippage (see ```exchange.IO("slippage", ...)```), failing when nothing fills. Orders must be worth more than $10 (except closing a whole position). A paused market takes no orders and a close-only market takes closing orders only. The first order in a market enters it automatically (Boros charges a one-time entrance fee). For an isolated-only market the option ```cashIn``` (in the collateral) moves cash into the isolated account before the order |
| exchange.GetOrder() | Order IDs are ```market id,order id```; market orders that filled at once and never rested are returned from the fill recorded when this process placed them. ```AvgPrice``` is the order's tick rate (Boros order records carry no average fill rate), and for a market order the protective rate it was placed with |
| exchange.CancelOrder() | Cancels through the relayer; fails when the order is no longer open (filled or already canceled) |
| exchange.ModifyOrder() | Atomically cancels the old order and places a new one (Boros's ```idToStrictCancel```), returning the new order ID; the whole call fails when the old order is gone. The new order is a GTC limit order; without a price it keeps the old order's rate, and without an amount it takes the old order's unfilled amount |
| exchange.CreateConditionOrder() | Boros take-profit / stop-loss orders: once the rate crosses the trigger (```TpTriggerPrice``` or ```SlTriggerPrice```, which must be above 0) the position is closed at market, reduce-only. The side is the closing side (```closebuy``` closes a long, ```closesell``` a short); an amount not below the position closes the whole position; the order price can only be -1 (market) and OCO is not supported. Main account (sub-account 0) only. The stop-order API needs an API signing key: the connector mints one the first time, signed by the trading agent (named ```fmz-…```, valid 7 days, renewed before it expires; when the key slots are full it revokes the least recently used key this agent minted). A new key takes a while to reach all of Boros's gateways, so within a minute of minting, stop-order requests rejected with 401 are retried automatically after a short wait; the first call may take a few seconds longer |
| exchange.GetConditionOrders() | Take-profit / stop-loss orders waiting to trigger or executing; ```Price``` is -1 and the trigger is in ```Condition```; an order that closes the whole position has an ```Amount``` of 0 (the size is the position at trigger time) |

Every order and cancel goes on chain through Pendle's relayer and is paid from the Boros account's gas balance (about $0.02 to $0.04, see ```exchange.IO("gasBalance")```); by default a low balance is topped up from the cross cash automatically (see ```exchange.IO("autoTopUp", ...)```). Submissions of one exchange object run one at a time.

The Boros API is rate-limited by computing units: 200 per minute per IP (orders and cancels cost 5 each, the market list and order book 2 each, most others 1). When rate-limited the connector waits for the next window and retries once; keep market-data polling reasonable.

Risks: a funding-rate swap gains or loses with the difference between the underlying funding rate and the traded rate, and with position value changes as the implied rate moves; an account short of margin is liquidated. Funding settles hourly until maturity.

#### WOOFi Pro

Perpetual contracts (the WOO ecosystem's perpetual DEX built on Orderly Network, a different product and account from the WOO X exchange). Only USDC-settled perpetual contracts; the account is cross margin with one-way positions. Requires the Orderly account ID and an Orderly API key (ed25519 key pair).

##### Names and Configuration

```exchange.GetName()```: ```Futures_WOOFi``` (Futures); aliases: WOOFi, Orderly.

| Field | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
| AccountID | Yes | The Orderly account ID. |
| Access Key | Yes | The public key of the Orderly API key (ed25519), with or without the ```ed25519:``` prefix. |
| Secret Key | Yes | The private key of the Orderly API key (base58-encoded), with or without the ```ed25519:``` prefix. |

##### Trading Pairs and Contract Codes

Pair examples: ```BTC_USDC```, ```ETH_USDC```

Only USDC-settled contracts exist; the quote currency must be ```USDC```, for example ```ETH_USDC``` maps to the native code ```PERP_ETH_USDC```; other quote currencies are rejected.

| Contract code | Description |
| - | - |
| ```swap``` | Perpetual contract. |

Perpetual contracts only; other contract codes are rejected. Order amounts are in the base currency (```CtVal``` is 1 in ```exchange.GetMarkets()```).

##### Exchange-specific IO Commands

| Command | Arguments | Description | Returns |
| - | - | - | - |
| ```api``` | method, path[, params[, raw[, sign]]] | Call an Orderly endpoint directly. (more below the table) | The whole response (with ```success```, ```data``` and ```timestamp```; ```data``` is not unwrapped); an error is raised when ```success``` is ```false```. |

The rest of the longer descriptions in the table:

- ```api```: Paths starting with ```/v1/public/``` or ```/v1/tv/``` are unsigned by default and other paths are signed with the ed25519 key (```orderly-key```, ```orderly-signature``` and related headers; the account ID and API key must be configured); ```sign``` set to ```true```/```false``` (it may also be given directly as the 4th argument) forces signing on or off. ```GET``` parameters go into the query string, ```DELETE``` sends a form body and other methods a JSON body. ```raw``` is not a request body but a parameter table (a JSON object or ```a=1&b=2```) that replaces ```params``` entirely when non-empty.

For the common commands ```base``` and ```currency``` see `exchange.IO`.

##### Common Usage

###### Call public and signed endpoints with api

```javascript
function main() {
    // Paths starting with /v1/public/ are unsigned by default; the whole response is
    // returned, with the payload in data
    var info = exchange.IO("api", "GET", "/v1/public/info/PERP_ETH_USDC")
    Log("Tick:", info.data.quote_tick, "min size:", info.data.base_min)
    var fr = exchange.IO("api", "GET", "/v1/public/funding_rate/PERP_ETH_USDC")
    Log("Estimated funding rate:", fr.data.est_funding_rate)
    // Other paths are signed with the ed25519 key by default
    var orders = exchange.IO("api", "GET", "/v1/orders", {status: "INCOMPLETE"})
    Log("Open orders:", orders.data.rows.length)
    var pos = exchange.IO("api", "GET", "/v1/positions")
    Log("Positions:", pos.data.rows.length, "success:", pos.success)
}
```

##### Function Support

No unsupported standard functions.

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: Native periods are 1m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 4h, 12h, 1d, 1w, 1M, 1y; other periods are synthesized by the docker. At most 1000 bars per call.

##### Margin, Account and Simulation

Margin mode: The account is always cross margin, with no isolated margin; ```exchange.IO("cross", ...)``` is not supported. ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()``` sets leverage, which must be an integer; the exchange applies it to the whole account, so setting one contract's leverage also changes the other contracts.

Position mode: One-way (net) positions only; ```exchange.IO("dual", ...)``` is not supported, and ```exchange.SetDirection()``` only distinguishes opening from closing.

Account: The equity of ```exchange.GetAccount()``` is the USDC holding, and the unrealized PnL is the sum of the positions' unsettled PnL (```unsettled_pnl```). ```exchange.GetAssets()``` lists holdings per currency: frozen = ```frozen``` + ```pending_short```, available = holding − frozen.

##### Notes

- Conditional orders support take-profit and stop-loss only, not OCO (place the take-profit and stop-loss legs as two conditional orders); they trigger on the mark price, and with an order price of -1 (market) they execute at market once triggered.
- Limit orders accept ```{tif: "ioc"}```, ```{tif: "fok"}``` or ```{postOnly: true}``` in the last object argument, mapped to the exchange's ```IOC```, ```FOK``` and ```POST_ONLY``` order types; other keys are merged into the order request body as they are (overriding fields of the same name built by the connector).
- ```exchange.ModifyOrder()``` modifies in place and the order ID stays the same; a price or amount that is not passed keeps its current value. ```exchange.ModifyConditionOrder()``` modifies the trigger price, order price and amount in place, and the order ID stays the same as well.
- For market orders ```Price``` is 0; the average fill price is in ```AvgPrice``` (the exchange's ```average_executed_price```).
- ```MarginLevel``` in ```exchange.GetPositions()``` is the position's leverage (the exchange's ```leverage``` on the position row, or the reciprocal of the initial margin ratio ```imr``` when it is absent), and ```Margin``` is the initial margin in use (position value ÷ leverage).
- The order book and K-line endpoints also require a signature: ```exchange.GetDepth()```, ```exchange.GetRecords()``` and ```exchange.GetTicker()``` (best bid and ask come from the order book) all need a configured API key; ```exchange.GetTickers()```, ```exchange.GetTrades()```, ```exchange.GetFundings()``` and ```exchange.GetMarkets()``` need no signature.
- WebSocket push is supported: market data (ticker, bbo, depth, trades, klines) and the private stream (order updates, positions and balances) can be subscribed through the event stream. ```exchange.GetTicker()```, ```exchange.GetDepth()``` and the other functions still request the REST API directly, and ```EventLoop()``` does not subscribe to this exchange's push streams by itself. The stream addresses contain the account ID, so every subscription needs ```AccountID``` configured. The ticker push takes its best bid/ask prices and sizes from the contract's best bid/ask stream (Orderly's 24h ticker stream has no bid/ask) and starts once both streams have arrived. Trades carry no exchange trade ID; the trade IDs are synthesized by the same rule as ```exchange.GetTrades()``` (several trades with identical fields in the same millisecond are only unique within the push and may not match the REST numbering). Depth (at most 255 levels, 20 by default) takes its snapshot from the same signed order book endpoint as ```exchange.GetDepth()``` and then applies the 200 ms incremental pushes, linking each update to the previous version's timestamp; a broken chain refetches the snapshot automatically, so depth subscriptions need the API key. Kline periods are 1 minute, 5, 15 and 30 minutes, 1 hour, 4 hours, 12 hours, 1 day, 1 week and 1 month (1 year is not supported), and a first kline subscription pushes 500 historical bars from ```exchange.GetRecords()``` first; the exchange's kline push has no closed flag, so a bar counts as closed when the next bar appears or the push time reaches the bar's end time. The private stream is one ```private``` subscription for the whole account (no symbol). It connects only when subscribed and logs in with an API key signature: once the subscription is active (and again after every reconnect) it first pushes a snapshot of all balances and positions from the same endpoints as ```exchange.GetAssets()``` and ```exchange.GetPositions()```, then reports ready, and afterwards pushes order updates (all contracts), position changes (one-way positions) and balance changes with the same meaning as those two functions. Conditional orders are not pushed on the private stream; the regular order placed when one triggers is pushed as usual. A rejected login reports a degraded connection status and a failed private stream (market data push is unaffected); when ```RestBase``` points to the Orderly testnet the push connects to the testnet as well. A market-wide ```tickers``` subscription (no symbol) uses Orderly's all-market 24-hour ticker stream together with its all-market best bid/ask stream: once a second it pushes every perpetual with the last price, the 24-hour open/high/low, the volume and the best bid/ask (it also needs the AccountID).

#### Uniswap / PancakeSwap

The Uniswap and PancakeSwap exchange objects each connect to that exchange's pools on one chain and map on-chain swaps onto the spot trading functions. Their pools are built the same way: V2 pools, V3 pools, and V4 pools inside a singleton contract (called Infinity CL on PancakeSwap, together V4/Infinity CL below; only pools without hooks are used, and the native coin takes part in swaps directly without its wrapped token). The token table, swaps, orders, cancels, LP and the bridge work the same way too, so they share this page. The differences:

| Aspect | Uniswap | PancakeSwap |
| - | - | - |
| Chains | Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, BNB Chain, Unichain, Polygon, OP Mainnet, Robinhood, Arc (Ethereum by default) | Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, BNB Chain (BNB Chain by default) |
| V2 pools | Used on Ethereum, Unichain, Robinhood and Arc; 0.3% fee | Used on all four chains; 0.25% fee |
| V3 fee tiers | 0.01%, 0.05%, 0.3%, 1% | 0.01%, 0.05%, 0.25%, 1% |
| V4/Infinity CL | Uniswap V4, available on all nine chains (Arc uses only the ERC-20 form of USDC; pools of native USDC are not visible); pools come from the common fee combinations and GeckoTerminal (see below), with no fee cap | Infinity CL, available on BNB Chain and Base only, using only pools with a fee of at most 1%; Infinity Bin pools are not supported |
| V4/Infinity CL position IDs | ```v4:number``` | ```inf:number``` |
| Swap and approval contracts | Uniswap's Universal Router and Permit2 | PancakeSwap's own Universal Router and Permit2 |

Uniswap V4 has no fixed fee tiers either. The connector first looks for pools at Uniswap's common fee/tick-spacing combinations (0.01%/1, 0.02%/4, 0.03%/6, 0.04%/8, 0.05%/10, 0.3%/60, 1%/200), then takes the PoolIds of Uniswap V4 pools from the token's pool list on GeckoTerminal (the first two pages, the top 40 by volume and liquidity), resolves each PoolKey on chain with the PositionManager's ```poolKeys```, checks it against the PoolId and keeps only hookless pools, adding pools with custom fees and spacings (such as the CASHCAT/USDG 0.269% pool with tick spacing 54 on Robinhood). ```lp.pools```, ```lp.select```, ```lp.plan```, swap routing and the kline pool choice all use these pools. Only tokens that are not hubs (the wrapped native and stablecoins such as USDC and USDT) are looked up, so a pair of two hubs (such as ```ETH_USDC```) uses the common combinations only; results are cached in the process for an hour. The list can still miss pools: pools GeckoTerminal does not index or ranks below the top 40, and pools that never had a position on the PositionManager (```poolKeys``` returns no PoolKey), are not found; while GeckoTerminal is unavailable (for example rate-limited) only the common combinations are used and the lookup is retried after 5 minutes, and ```exchange.IO("route", ...)``` carries a ```warning``` with the reason. A hookless pool missing from the list can be passed by its PoolId to ```lp.pool``` and ```lp.plan``` (```pool```), provided the PositionManager can likewise resolve its PoolKey. Uniswap V4 pools have no fee cap (V4 allows static fees up to 100%, such as the 2% CASHCAT/ETH pool on Robinhood), and swap quotes come from the on-chain V4Quoter at the pool's actual fee; the cap of 1% applies only to PancakeSwap's Infinity CL.

PancakeSwap's Infinity CL has no fixed fee tiers, so the connector collects pools from recent on-chain trades with ```eth_getLogs```, and pools without trades for a long time are not used; when the configured nodes cannot serve logs (the official BSC bsc-dataseed nodes refuse ```eth_getLogs``` outright, and free nodes such as drpc rate-limit it), these public trades are read through the chain's default public nodes, and if that also fails ```exchange.IO("route", ...)``` carries a ```warning``` with the reason.

Each swap takes the best-quoted route among the direct routes through all available pools and the two-hop routes through hub tokens. V4/Infinity CL routes swap through the Universal Router, with token approvals going through the Permit2 contract (see ```exchange.IO("approve", ...)```).

The same implementation also serves `Aerodrome / Velodrome` (Slipstream and basic pools, gauge staking) and the swap aggregators `KyberSwap` and `1inch`. PancakeSwap, Aerodrome and Velodrome used to be options of the Uniswap exchange's "DEX" setting and are separate exchanges since October 2026; the setting has been removed, and older configurations that chose them there fail at startup (for example ```Velodrome is now its own exchange: add a Velodrome exchange instead of Uniswap with Dex=Velodrome```), so add the dedicated exchange instead.

##### Names and Configuration

| ```exchange.GetName()``` | Type | Aliases |
| - | - | - |
| ```Uniswap``` | Spot | — |
| ```PancakeSwap``` | Spot | Pancake |

| Field | Required | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
| Chain | Yes | Uniswap: ```Ethereum```; PancakeSwap: ```BNB``` | Options: ```Ethereum```, ```Arbitrum```, ```Base```, ```BNB Chain``` (Uniswap only: ```Unichain```, ```Polygon```, ```OP Mainnet```, ```Robinhood```, ```Arc```) |
| Private Key | Yes | — | Wallet private key (hex). |
| Rpc Address | No | Uniswap: ```https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com,https://eth.drpc.org```; PancakeSwap: ```https://bsc-dataseed.binance.org,https://bsc-rpc.publicnode.com``` | RPC node URL; several nodes separated by commas fail over to each other when one errors or lacks data; when empty, each chain's built-in default (a primary node plus a backup, comma-separated) is used. (more below the table) |
| Rpc Api Key | No | — | RPC authentication: a ```Header-Name: value``` header or a Basic auth value. |

The rest of the longer descriptions in the table:

- Rpc Address: Order states need a node that returns receipts of mined transactions; the publicnode public nodes for Base, BNB Chain and Arbitrum cannot (archive access is required), so do not use them alone.

##### Trading Pairs and Contract Codes

Pair examples: ```ETH_USDC```, ```WETH_USDC```

Pairs are written as ```ETH_USDC```; the native coin (ETH, BNB, POL) and its wrapped token (WETH, WBNB, WPOL) are different assets, such as ```BNB_USDT``` and ```WBNB_USDT``` on BNB Chain. On the chains only Uniswap supports, the native coin of Polygon is POL; the Arc chain pays gas in USDC, and the native balance and the USDC token (```0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000```) are the same funds, so pairs are written as ```WETH_USDC``` or ```EURC_USDC```; the Robinhood chain has no USDC or USDT and its main stablecoin is USDG, so pairs are written as ```ETH_USDG```; USDT on Unichain and Polygon is written as ```USDT0```.

Tokens outside the token table can be used in pairs after registering them with ```exchange.IO("token", name, address)```.

##### Exchange-specific IO Commands

| Command | Arguments | Description | Returns |
| - | - | - | - |
