pump.fun launches (```exchange.IO("pump.*", ...)```, see "Pump.fun launches" below): newly created coins are discovered on chain and quoted, bought and sold directly on the pump.fun bonding curve (the connector builds, simulates and signs the transactions itself); once a coin graduates to PumpSwap, trades go through Jupiter swaps automatically. New coins are extremely risky; see the risks in that section.

##### Names and Configuration

```exchange.GetName()```: ```Jupiter``` (Spot).

| Field | Required | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
| Private Key | Yes | — | The Solana wallet private key: the base58 string exported by Phantom or Solflare, or the JSON byte array generated by solana-keygen. |
| Rpc Address | No | ```https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com,https://solana-rpc.publicnode.com``` | Solana RPC nodes; separate several with commas, and the next one is used automatically when a node fails. The default is the official public node plus publicnode. |
| Jupiter Api Key | No | — | Optional. (more below the table) |
| Liquidity Sources | No | — | Optional. (more below the table) |

The rest of the longer descriptions in the table:

- Jupiter Api Key: Without it the free ```lite-api.jup.ag``` is used; with it ```api.jup.ag``` is used, the request rate can be raised according to your plan (see ```exchange.IO("rps", ...)```), and native limit orders and DCA with a USDC or USDT quote switch by default to Jupiter Trigger V2 (funds deposited into a vault in Jupiter's custody, see "Limit orders" and "DCA"; to keep the non-custodial v1, call ```exchange.IO("trigger.api", "v1")```). Get the key on the Jupiter developer platform; a key restricted by endpoint permissions must include Trigger.
- Liquidity Sources: Swap only through these liquidity sources, for example ```pump``` (the pump.fun bonding curve and PumpSwap), ```meteora```, ```raydium```, ```orca```, or Jupiter source names; empty means all sources. It can be changed at run time with ```exchange.IO("dexes", ...)```.

##### Trading Pairs and Contract Codes

Pair examples: ```SOL_USDC```, ```JUP_USDC```, ```BONK_SOL```

SOL is the native coin and is wrapped and unwrapped automatically during swaps. Built-in tokens: SOL, USDC, USDT, JUP, BONK, WIF, JTO, PYTH, RAY, JitoSOL, mSOL, JupSOL, TRUMP, PENGU, POPCAT. Other tokens can be written in three ways: by token name, resolved to the verified token with exactly that name in the Jupiter token list (an error is raised when several verified tokens share the name); by mint address; or after registering them with ```exchange.IO("token", ...)```. Pairs are not upper-cased (mint addresses and token names such as ```mSOL``` are case-sensitive), so write them as they are, for example ```DB5QKorV9KHY54y73h5xWQqYyuD8P3jC1p5Ea8DBpump_SOL```.

##### Exchange-specific IO Commands

| Command | Arguments | Description | Returns |
| - | - | - | - |
| ```route``` | symbol, side, qty | Quote only, no order, on the same basis as orders: ```sell``` quotes selling ```qty``` base tokens as exact input; ```buy``` quotes buying ```qty``` base tokens as exact output, and when there is no exact-output route (sources such as Meteora and PumpSwap do not support exact output) it estimates with exact input instead, the same fallback as a limit buy (a market buy is exact input itself). See the sub-page `exchange.IO("route", ...)`. | ```{symbol, side, qty, route, quote, price, priceImpactPct, swapMode, baseQty}```: ```swapMode``` is ```ExactIn``` or ```ExactOut```; ```baseQty``` is the base amount this quote actually buys or sells (with the exact-input estimate for a buy it may differ slightly from ```qty```), and ```price``` is ```quote``` divided by ```baseQty```. (more below the table) |
| ```token``` | [name, mint] | Register a token (for this run only) so its name can be used in pairs; without arguments, list the token table. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("token", ...)`. | ```{symbol, mint, decimals}``` when registering, an array of ```{symbol, mint, decimals, native}``` when listing. |
| ```transfer``` | to, amount | Transfer SOL out of the wallet; ```amount``` may be ```all``` (the whole balance minus the fee). Only SOL is supported; a third argument naming another token fails. Waits for the broadcast only, not for confirmation. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("transfer", ...)`. | ```{signature, amount, lastValidBlockHeight}``` |
| ```receipt``` | signature[, waitMs] | Query the status of a Solana transaction, optionally waiting until it is confirmed or fails (up to 10 minutes). For an order, pass the transaction signature after the comma in the order ID. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("receipt", ...)`. | ```{signature, state, slot, confirmationStatus, err, fee, blockTime}```, where ```state``` is ```success```, ```failed``` or ```pending```; ```fee``` and ```blockTime``` appear only once it is confirmed or failed. (more below the table) |
| ```dca.create``` | params | Creates a DCA order. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("dca.*", ...)`. | ```{id, version, signature, symbol, side, total, perOrder, numberOfOrders, interval, minPrice, maxPrice, startAt, priorityFeeLamports}```: ```version``` is ```v1``` or ```v2```; a v1 ```id``` is the DCA order account address and a V2 ```id``` is Jupiter's order UUID, ```signature``` being the deposit transaction, plus ```vault```. |
| ```dca.list``` | [params] | Lists the wallet's DCA orders (v1 first, then V2 when an API key is set or ```trigger.api``` is ```v2```): ```params.status``` is ```active``` (default, running) or ```history``` (ended), and ```params.symbol``` limits the list to that pair. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("dca.*", ...)`. | ```[{id, version, symbol, side, state, total, perOrder, numberOfOrders, ordersFilled, interval, minPrice, maxPrice, spent, received, filledQty, avgPrice, fee, createdAt, updatedAt, openTx, closeTx, info}]```, where ```state``` is ```active```, ```completed``` or ```canceled```, and for V2 also ```pending``` (depositing), ```canceling``` (canceled, funds not yet withdrawn) or ```failed``` (deposit failed); V2 rows also carry ```nextFillAt```, and their ```fee``` is ```null``` (the fee is already taken from the tokens received); ```spent``` is the input token spent so far and ```received``` the output token received (```fee```, in the output token, is the fee deducted from it); ```filledQty``` and ```avgPrice``` are the filled amount and average price in base-token terms; ```info``` is Jupiter's raw row. (more below the table) |
| ```dca.cancel``` | id | Cancels a running DCA order and returns the remaining input token to the wallet; v1 and V2 are told apart by the shape of ```id``` (a V2 ID is a UUID and needs the API key). See the sub-page `exchange.IO("dca.*", ...)`. | v1: ```{id, version, signature, priorityFeeLamports[, indexed]}```; V2: ```{id, version, signature, refund, refundCurrency, roundsRemaining, info}```, where ```signature``` is the withdrawal transaction and ```refund``` the amount of input token returned. |
| ```dca.simulate``` | params[, wallet] | Builds the transaction of ```dca.create``` from the same parameters and runs it with the node's ```simulateTransaction``` (not signed, nothing broadcast), to check balances, minimums and so on before ordering; with ```params``` written ```{cancel: id}``` it simulates canceling that DCA order. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("dca.*", ...)`. | ```{ok, err, reason, logs, unitsConsumed, version, wallet, id, plan, priorityFeeLamports}``` (```version``` is ```v1``` or ```v2```; V2 adds ```vault``` and has no ```id```): ```ok``` tells whether the simulation succeeded and ```reason``` explains a failure (when the paying wallet has no SOL at all the node only returns ```err``` ```AccountNotFound```, and ```reason``` adds "the paying wallet has no SOL"); ```id``` is the address of the DCA account that would be created; ```plan``` holds the normalized DCA parameters. |
| ```trigger.simulate``` | params[, wallet] | Builds the transaction of a Jupiter limit order and runs it with the node's ```simulateTransaction``` (not signed, nothing broadcast). See the sub-page `exchange.IO("trigger.*", ...)`. | v1: ```{ok, err, reason, logs, unitsConsumed, wallet, order, makingAmount, takingAmount, priorityFeeLamports}```, where ```order``` is the order account address and ```makingAmount``` and ```takingAmount``` are the amounts given and received in smallest units; V2: ```{ok, err, reason, logs, unitsConsumed, version, wallet, vault, inputMint, inputAmount, triggerPriceUsd, triggerCondition, expiresAt, priorityFeeLamports}```. (more below the table) |
| ```trigger.api``` | [mode] | Which API new native limit orders (```tif``` ```gtc```) and new DCA orders use: ```auto``` (default) uses Trigger V2 (custodial vault) when an API key is set and the quote is USDC or USDT, and v1 otherwise; ```v1``` always uses v1 (non-custodial, funds in an on-chain order account), even with an API key; ```v2``` always uses V2, fails orders whose quote is not USDC or USDT, and works without an API key too (Jupiter currently accepts V2 calls without a key, but its documentation says a key is required and this may be enforced at any time). See the sub-page `exchange.IO("trigger.*", ...)`. | The current mode: ```auto```, ```v1``` or ```v2```. |
| ```trigger.vault``` | [action] | Queries this wallet's custodial vault in Jupiter Trigger V2 and its balances (needs the API key, or ```exchange.IO("trigger.api", "v2")```). See the sub-page `exchange.IO("trigger.*", ...)`. | ```{wallet, registered: false}``` while there is no vault; otherwise ```{wallet, registered: true, vault, sol, tokens, info}```, where ```tokens``` is ```[{mint, symbol, amount, raw}]``` (```symbol``` only for tokens in the token table) and ```info``` is Jupiter's vault record. |
| ```slippage``` | [ratio] | Slippage protection of market orders, range ```[0, 0.5)```, default ```0.005``` (0.5%), enforced on chain. Limit orders do not use it. Queries when called without an argument. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("slippage", ...)`. | The current slippage ratio. |
| ```priorityFee``` | [sol] | Cap on the priority fee of each swap transaction, in SOL, 0 to 0.1, default 0.001; Jupiter estimates the actual priority fee from network congestion, up to the cap. Queries when called without an argument. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("priorityFee", ...)`. | The current cap (SOL). |
| ```dexes``` | [sources] | Restrict the liquidity sources swaps go through (comma-separated) to the group shorthands ```pump```, ```meteora```, ```raydium```, ```orca``` or Jupiter source names (case-sensitive); ```""``` removes the restriction. Market data, quotes and orders all use only these sources. Queries when called without an argument. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("dexes", ...)`. | The array of restricted source names (groups expanded; an empty array means no restriction). |
| ```rps``` | [n] | Maximum requests per second to the Jupiter API, 0.1 to 500, default 1. Requests are queued with at least ```1/n``` seconds between two of them. Queries when called without an argument. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("rps", ...)`. | The current maximum requests per second. |
| ```base``` | [url] | Without an argument, returns the current Solana node address; with an address, switches the node (separate several with commas). | The previous address. |
| ```address``` | — | The wallet address (base58). | — |
| ```pump.new``` | [options] | Coins recently created on pump.fun, discovered on chain: the recent signatures of the pump.fun mint authority (```TSLvdd1pWpHVjahSpsvCXUbgwsL3JAcvokwaKt1eokM```, which appears only in creation transactions) are listed and each transaction's ```CreateEvent``` is parsed, newest first. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("pump.*", ...)`. | ```[{signature, slot, time, mint, name, symbol, uri, creator, user, bondingCurve, tokenProgram, quote, quoteMint, mayhem, cashback, holderReward, devBuy}]```: ```time``` is the block time (milliseconds); ```user``` is the wallet that sent the creation (usually the ```creator```); ```tokenProgram``` is ```spl-token``` or ```token-2022```; ```quote``` is ```SOL```, ```USDC``` or the quote token's mint (only ```SOL``` coins can be traded with ```pump.buy``` and ```pump.sell```); ```devBuy``` is the first buy in the same transaction, ```{tokens, quoteAmount}``` (```quoteAmount``` includes fees and is ```null``` when the quote is neither SOL nor USDC), or ```null``` when there is none. (more below the table) |
| ```pump.info``` | mint | The coin's bonding-curve state, read with one ```getMultipleAccounts``` (curve, mint, global config and fee table). Fails for a coin that is not a pump.fun coin. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("pump.*", ...)`. | ```{mint, bondingCurve, creator, tokenProgram, decimals, quote, quoteMint, complete, migrated, virtualTokenReserves, virtualQuoteReserves, realTokenReserves, realQuoteReserves, tokenTotalSupply, price, marketCap, progress, fees, mayhem, cashback, holderReward}```: reserves and supply are in readable units; ```price``` is the quote (SOL) value of one coin and ```marketCap``` is ```price``` times the total supply; ```progress``` is the share of the curve sold (%), and at 100 the curve is complete (```complete```) and then migrates to PumpSwap (```migrated```, reserves zeroed, ```price```, ```marketCap``` and ```fees``` ```null```); ```fees``` is the current rate ```{protocolBps, creatorBps}``` in basis points. |
| ```pump.quote``` | mint, side, amount | Quotes locally on the bonding curve (no transaction), with the on-chain program's formula and fees: for ```buy``` ```amount``` is the SOL to spend (fees included), for ```sell``` the number of coins to sell. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("pump.*", ...)`. | ```{venue, mint, side, quote, amountIn, amountOut, price, spotPrice, priceAfter, priceImpactPct, fees, protocolFeeBps, creatorFeeBps, crossesCurve}```: ```venue``` is ```pump``` (bonding curve) or ```jupiter``` (graduated, which adds ```route```, the liquidity sources used); ```price``` is the average fill price including fees (SOL per coin), ```priceImpactPct``` is how far the average price before fees is from the current price ```spotPrice``` (%), and ```fees``` is the protocol plus creator fee (SOL); ```crossesCurve``` ```true``` means the buy goes past the end of the curve (see "Pump.fun launches" below). (more below the table) |
| ```pump.buy``` | mint, solAmount[, options] | Buys on the bonding curve for ```solAmount``` SOL (protocol and creator fees included): the wallet's token account is created idempotently, then ```buy_exact_quote_in_v3``` is sent with a minimum output of the local quote × (1 − ```slippage```), enforced on chain. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("pump.*", ...)`. | ```{txHash, venue, mint, side, solAmount, tokenAmount, price, fee, slot}```: ```venue``` is ```pump``` or ```jupiter``` (which adds ```route```); ```solAmount``` is the SOL paid (protocol and creator fees included, network fee and account deposits excluded), ```tokenAmount``` the coins bought and ```fee``` the network fee (SOL). (more below the table) |
| ```pump.sell``` | mint, amount[, options] | Sells ```amount``` coins on the bonding curve (```all``` for the whole balance) with ```sell_v3```, with a minimum SOL output of the local quote × (1 − ```slippage```). See the sub-page `exchange.IO("pump.*", ...)`. | Same as ```pump.buy```: ```solAmount``` is the SOL received (protocol and creator fees deducted). |
| ```pump.holdings``` | [wallet] | The pump.fun coins held by a wallet (by default this exchange object's wallet): the token balances that have a bonding curve, valued on the curve. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("pump.*", ...)`. | ```[{mint, amount, quote, complete, price, value}]```: ```value``` is the quote (fees deducted) that selling the whole balance on the curve would return now; ```price``` and ```value``` are ```null``` once the curve is complete or when the balance exceeds what the curve can buy back (value graduated coins with ```exchange.IO("route", ...)```). |
| ```lp.pools``` | token[, quote] | Lists a token's Meteora DLMM, Raydium CLMM and Orca Whirlpools pools (against the given quote, or SOL, USDC and USDT) with fee, bin step and active bin (DLMM) or tick spacing and current tick (CLMM), current price, both token balances of the pool and TVL; 24h volume and fees and the USD TVL come from Meteora's data API (```dlmm.datapi.meteora.ag```), the Raydium API v3 (```api-v3.raydium.io```) and Orca's public API (```api.orca.so```) respectively, while prices, balances and the like are read on chain, Raydium's fee from the pool's AmmConfig account. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("lp.pools", ...)`. | ```[{id, protocol, dex, symbol, base, quote, fee, feeRate, feeRateNow, binStep, activeId, price, reserveBase, reserveQuote, tvlQuote, tvlUsd, volume24hUsd, fees24hUsd, enabled, rewards, empty}]```: ```protocol``` is ```meteora```; ```price``` is quote per token; ```fee``` is the base fee in millionths (the unit of Uniswap's ```fee```), ```feeRate``` the same as a ratio, and ```feeRateNow``` the current rate including the volatility surcharge; ```rewards``` are the pool's farm reward tokens ```[{mint, symbol}]```. (more below the table) |
| ```lp.select``` | token, budget[, options] | Picks a pool by rule. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("lp.select", ...)`. | One ```lp.pools``` row with an extra ```reason```. |
| ```lp.pool``` | poolId | Live state of a pool. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("lp.pool", ...)`. | ```{id, protocol, dex, tokenX, tokenY, symbolX, symbolY, decimalsX, decimalsY, price, fee, feeRate, feeRateNow, binStep, activeId, reserveX, reserveY, tvlUsd, volume24hUsd, fees24hUsd, enabled, rewards}```, where ```price``` is Y per X (the pool's own order). (more below the table) |
| ```lp.ticks``` | poolId[, lowerBinId, upperBinId[, step]] | The liquidity distribution over a bin range (DLMM has bins rather than ticks): both token amounts per segment, ```step``` being the segment width in bins (default 1). See the sub-page `exchange.IO("lp.ticks", ...)`. | ```{pool, activeId, binStep, price, tokenX, tokenY, symbolX, symbolY, segments: [{binLower, binUpper, priceLower, priceUpper, amountX, amountY, current}]}```, prices in Y per X. (more below the table) |
| ```lp.plan``` | params | A position plan (read-only, costs nothing). See the sub-page `exchange.IO("lp.plan", ...)`. | ```{params, symbol, pool, protocol, fee, feeRate, price, shape, strategy, budget, budgetUsd, binStep, activeId, lowerBinId, upperBinId, bins, positions: [{lowerBinId, upperBinId, priceLower, priceUpper, amountBase, amountQuote, share}], needBase, needQuote, haveBase, haveQuote, swap, shortfall, shareOfPool, volume24hUsd, estDailyFeesUsd, slippageBps, maxActiveBinSlippage, binArraysToCreate, rentSol, rentRefundableSol, warning?}```: ```swap``` is the swap needed before adding (```{side, amount, currency}``` or ```null```); ```shareOfPool``` is the plan's share of the active bin and ```estDailyFeesUsd``` = 24h volume × fee rate × that share (assuming the price stays in range); ```rentSol``` is the rent the positions lock, of which ```rentRefundableSol``` belongs to the position accounts (returned when they are closed) and the rest to new bin arrays (```binArraysToCreate```, not returned). (more below the table) |
| ```lp.simulate``` | plan[, payer] | Builds the complete add-liquidity transactions of the plan (creating bin arrays, the position, ATAs, wrapping SOL, adding liquidity, unwrapping) and runs them with the node's ```simulateTransaction``` (no signature check, nothing broadcast), one transaction per position. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("lp.simulate", ...)`. | ```{pool, protocol, payer, ok, positions: [{position, lowerBinId, upperBinId, amountBase, amountQuote, ok, err, error, logs, unitsConsumed, txBytes}], swapNeeded, shortfall, note}```: ```logs``` is the tail of the program logs and ```error``` the failure reason (DLMM, Raydium CLMM and Orca Whirlpool error codes with their names); Raydium and Orca rows carry ```tickLower``` and ```tickUpper``` instead of the bin fields, and ```position``` is the mint of the position NFT. |
| ```lp.add``` | plan | Adds liquidity by the plan. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("lp.add", ...)`. | ```{txHash, txHashes, swapTxHash, pool, protocol, symbol, positions: [{id, txHash, lowerBinId, upperBinId, priceLower, priceUpper, amountBase, amountQuote, rentSol, feeSol}]}```, with position ```id```s written ```meteora:address```, ```raydium:position NFT mint``` or ```orca:position NFT mint```; Raydium and Orca rows carry ```tickLower``` and ```tickUpper``` instead of the bin fields. |
| ```lp.increase``` | positionId, budget[, options] | Adds to a position, splitting ```budget``` (in the quote token) over the position's bin range at the current price and swapping first for whichever token is short. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("lp.increase", ...)`. | ```{txHash, swapTxHash, id, symbol, amountBase, amountQuote, feeSol}``` |
| ```lp.decrease``` | positionId, ratio[, options] | Withdraws a ratio (0 to 1, converted to basis points) from every bin of the position that has liquidity and claims all fees and farm rewards; the position stays. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("lp.decrease", ...)`. | ```{txHash, txHashes, positions: [{id, symbol, txHashes, principalBase, principalQuote, feesBase, feesQuote, receivedBase, receivedQuote, rewards, rentRefundSol, feeSol}], sells}```: ```received*``` come from the balances before and after the transactions, and the fee part is split off by the amounts claimable on chain before sending. |
| ```lp.collect``` | positionIds[, sell] | Claims fees and farm rewards (```claim_fee2``` and ```claim_reward2``` on DLMM, a zero-liquidity ```decrease_liquidity_v2``` on Raydium, ```update_fees_and_rewards``` + ```collect_fees_v2``` + ```collect_reward_v2``` on Orca), one transaction per position; with ```sell``` ```true``` the collected base token is sold for the quote. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("lp.collect", ...)`. | Same as ```lp.decrease```. |
| ```lp.remove``` | positionIds[, ratio[, sell]] | Withdraws liquidity and claims fees and rewards, each position in its own transactions; ```ratio``` defaults to 1, which withdraws everything and closes the position account (on Raydium, ```close_position``` burns the NFT and closes the NFT account, the NFT mint and the position account), returning its rent (```rentRefundSol```); below 1 only that share is withdrawn. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("lp.remove", ...)`. | Same as ```lp.decrease```. |
| ```lp.positions``` | [filter[, wallet]] | Every Meteora DLMM position of the wallet (found by owner with the node's ```getProgramAccounts```, which the node must serve) and every Raydium CLMM and Orca Whirlpools position (NFTs with amount 1 found with ```getTokenAccountsByOwner```, then their position accounts; on Orca positions in Position Bundles the wallet holds are listed too): bin range, in-range flag, current amounts of both tokens (from the position's share of each bin), value, uncollected fees and farm rewards, and the rent it locks. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("lp.positions", ...)`. | ```[{id, pool, protocol, symbol, fee, lowerBinId, upperBinId, activeId, binStep, width, priceLower, priceUpper, price, inRange, liquidity, amountBase, amountQuote, value, feesBase, feesQuote, feesValue, rewards, rentSol, feeOwner, closed}]```, with ```value``` and ```feesValue``` in the quote token, ```rewards``` as ```[{mint, symbol, amount}]``` and ```liquidity``` the sum of the bin shares. (more below the table) |
| ```lp.track``` | positionIds | Registers positions (```meteora:address```, ```raydium:NFT mint```, ```orca:NFT mint``` or the bare address, Raydium and Orca also accepting the position account address; verified to be positions of that protocol) so that ```lp.positions``` checks them as well (ownership is verified on chain each time; transferred-away and closed positions are not listed). (more below the table) | All position addresses remembered in this process. |
| ```bridge.chains``` | — | Chains supported by the bridge (LI.FI): EVM chains and Solana, cached for an hour. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("bridge.*", ...)`. | An array of ```{id, key, name, chainType, nativeToken}```, ```chainType``` being ```EVM``` or ```SVM```. |
| ```bridge.tokens``` | [chain] | Tokens LI.FI knows on a chain (Solana by default), cached for an hour. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("bridge.*", ...)`. | An array of ```{symbol, address, decimals, name, priceUSD}```. |
| ```bridge.quote``` | params | A bridge quote (read-only) from this exchange object's chain. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("bridge.*", ...)`. | ```{tool, toolName, fromChain, toChain, toChainName, fromToken, toToken, fromAmount, toAmount, toAmountMin, fromAmountRaw, toAmountRaw, toAmountMinRaw, fromAmountUSD, toAmountUSD, slippage, toAddress, feeCosts, gasCosts, executionDuration, approvalAddress, steps, transactionId, request}```: amounts are in token units (```*Raw``` in the smallest unit); ```toAmountMin``` is the amount guaranteed after slippage; ```feeCosts``` is ```[{name, amount, token, amountUSD, percentage, included}]``` (fees with ```included``` ```false``` are paid on top); ```gasCosts``` estimates source-chain gas; ```executionDuration``` is the expected time in seconds; ```approvalAddress``` is the contract to approve (```null``` for the native coin and on Solana); ```steps``` lists the steps (```cross``` bridges, ```swap``` swaps); ```request``` echoes the parameters. |
| ```bridge.simulate``` | params\|quote | Re-quotes, signs LI.FI's serialized transaction with this wallet and runs ```simulateTransaction``` (with signature verification) without broadcasting. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("bridge.*", ...)`. | The ```bridge.quote``` result plus ```simulated``` (```true```), ```unitsConsumed``` and ```signature```. |
| ```bridge.send``` | params\|quote | Bridges out: re-quotes → checks the balance → signs LI.FI's serialized transaction with this wallet (refusing one this wallet does not sign) → ```simulateTransaction``` → broadcasts through the Solana node. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("bridge.*", ...)`. | ```{txHash, tool, fromChain, toChain, toChainName, fromToken, toToken, fromAmount, toAmount, toAmountMin, toAddress, transactionId}```; ```txHash``` is the source-chain signature, whose state ```receipt``` returns. |
| ```bridge.status``` | signature[, options] | Bridge progress (LI.FI ```/status```) for the source-chain transaction signature returned by ```bridge.send```; ```options``` may give ```{toChain, bridge}``` to speed up the lookup. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("bridge.*", ...)`. | ```{status, substatus, substatusMessage, tool, sending, receiving, fromAddress, toAddress, explorer, bridgeExplorer}```: ```status``` is ```NOT_FOUND```, ```INVALID```, ```PENDING```, ```DONE``` or ```FAILED```; when ```DONE```, ```substatus``` is ```COMPLETED``` (delivered as quoted), ```PARTIAL``` (a different token arrived) or ```REFUNDED```; ```sending``` and ```receiving``` are ```{txHash, txLink, chainId, amount, amountRaw, token, timestamp}```, with ```receiving.amount``` and ```receiving.token``` being what actually arrived. |
| ```bridge.apiKey``` | [key] | Sets the LI.FI API key (header ```x-lifi-api-key```, for this exchange object only, never echoed); ```""``` clears it and no argument just queries. Without a key requests are rate-limited per outgoing IP, see below. See the sub-page `exchange.IO("bridge.*", ...)`. | Whether a key is set (a boolean). |

The rest of the longer descriptions in the table:

- ```lp.track```: Positions of all three protocols are found by owner, so registering is normally unnecessary; the command is kept for parity with Uniswap, and positions created by ```lp.add``` in this process are remembered automatically. Looking up another wallet's Orca position uses the node's ```getTokenLargestAccounts``` to find the NFT holder (public nodes rate-limit it tightly).

For the common command ```currency``` see `exchange.IO`.

The common command ```api``` is not supported (the call fails with an error and returns null).

##### Function Support

Not supported (the call fails with an error and returns null): `exchange.GetTickers`, `exchange.GetTrades`, `exchange.CreateConditionOrder`, `exchange.ModifyConditionOrder`, `exchange.CancelConditionOrder`, `exchange.GetConditionOrder`, `exchange.GetConditionOrders`, `exchange.GetHistoryConditionOrders`.

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: Native periods are 1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h, 12h, 1d (GeckoTerminal's timeframes); other periods of a minute or longer are synthesized by the docker, while second-level periods are unavailable (there is no trade feed to build them from).

##### Notes

| Function | Behavior on Jupiter |
| - | - |
| exchange.GetTicker() | Bid and ask are executable prices for about $1000 (two quotes); for small tokens that cannot absorb $1000 the size steps down to $100 and then $10, and the sell side shrinks further if needed; the actual sizes are in ```sizeQuote``` and ```bidSize``` of ```Info```. There are no 24h statistics: ```High```, ```Low``` and ```Open``` are the current price and ```Volume``` is 0 |
| exchange.GetDepth() | Derived from quotes at sizes increasing from about $1000, two quotes per level. Bid prices strictly descend and ask prices strictly ascend. The two sides are quotes taken at different moments in opposite directions and occasionally cross (best bid not below best ask): the crossing levels are then merged into one level around the mid of the two (best bid and best ask at the mid minus and plus 0.0001%, amounts kept), and the original best bid and ask are in ```crossed``` of ```Info```, which is ```null``` when the book did not cross |
| exchange.GetRecords() | K-lines come from GeckoTerminal's pool-level data: Jupiter is an aggregator, so the pool (on any DEX) holding exactly the two tokens (SOL as wSOL) with the largest USD liquidity on GeckoTerminal is used (searched among the top 20 pools of each token; the chosen pool is cached for an hour). Prices are that pool's trade prices (including the pool fee, so they may differ from the mid price of ```exchange.GetTicker()``` by about one pool fee) in quote per base, and ```Volume``` is in the base token; periods without trades repeat the previous close with zero volume, and the last bar may still be open. GeckoTerminal data lags by tens of seconds up to a minute and its public API allows about 10 requests per minute: bars of the same period are cached for a minute, requests queue inside the docker and wait and retry when rate-limited, and fail if that still does not succeed. Fails when no pool of the pair is found |
| exchange.GetMarkets() | Pairs of the tokens in the token table against USDC, USDT and SOL (routes are not verified pair by pair). The amount precision is the base token's decimals, the minimum quantity is one smallest unit, and the price precision is fixed at 8 |
| exchange.GetAssets() | Wallet balances of SOL and of the tokens in the token table, with separately held wSOL reported as ```WSOL```; holdings outside the token table are not in the balance list but in ```unlisted``` of ```Info``` (```{mint, amount}```) |
| exchange.CreateOrder() | Swaps immediately: a limit price is the worst acceptable fill, enforced on chain by the program through the slippage bound, and if the current quote cannot reach it the call fails without sending a transaction; market orders are protected by the slippage setting; a market buy is sized in the quote currency to spend. The order extra parameter ```slippage``` overrides the slippage for that order. Jupiter simulates the transaction when building it, so problems such as an insufficient balance fail immediately. Before broadcasting, the Solana node simulates it again on the latest state: if that simulation fails, nothing is sent and the connector quotes and builds the transaction again, up to 2 retries (from the second retry on it avoids the liquidity sources of the failed routes, never going beyond the ```exchange.IO("dexes", ...)``` restriction); if it still fails the call fails with the simulation's ```err``` and the relevant program logs in the error message. On success ```preflightRetries``` in ```Info``` is the number of retries. With the order option ```tif``` set to ```gtc``` it places a native Jupiter limit order instead of swapping (Trigger V2 with an API key and a USDC or USDT quote, otherwise v1; ```exchange.IO("trigger.api", ...)``` can force either), see "Limit orders" below |
| exchange.GetOrder() | The order ID looks like ```SOL_USDC,5VERv8…``` (the pair, a comma, then the transaction signature). A confirmed transaction is filled, with the filled amounts computed from the wallet balances before and after the transaction; a transaction that fails on chain is canceled (the fee is still charged); one still not included after its validity period (about one minute) is canceled. A transaction not sent by this program can only be queried once it has succeeded (the direction is inferred from the balance changes); one not yet confirmed or failed on chain returns an error. A limit order's ID is the pair plus the order account address (v1) or Jupiter's order UUID (V2), see "Limit orders" below |
| exchange.GetOrders() | Swaps sent by this program that are neither confirmed nor expired, plus all open limit orders of the wallet (not only those placed by this program; V2 limit orders only when an API key is set) |
| exchange.CancelOrder() | Limit orders only. Swaps cannot be canceled: a sent Solana transaction cannot be recalled, and one that is not included expires automatically after about one minute |
| exchange.ModifyOrder() | Changes the price (and the order extra parameter ```slippage```) of V2 limit orders only, see "Limit orders" below. v1 limit orders and swaps cannot be modified |
| exchange.GetHistoryOrders() | Filled and canceled limit orders, plus expired V2 orders (funds still in the vault, reported as pending; see "Limit orders" below), no swaps (query swaps with ```exchange.GetOrder()```). Without ```since``` and ```limit``` it returns the latest 10 v1 orders in each direction (buy and sell) and the latest 10 V2 orders; with ```since``` all created at or after it, and with ```limit``` until that many are collected. v1 and V2 are merged, newest created first |

- Request rate: Jupiter limits requests per second and returns 429 above the limit. The connector queues requests at the rate set with ```exchange.IO("rps", ...)``` (1 per second by default), and the exchange objects in one docker process that use the same Jupiter API address share this pace. With the default setting ```exchange.GetTicker()``` takes about 2 seconds and a 5-level ```exchange.GetDepth()``` about 10 seconds; for more speed, get a Jupiter API key and raise ```rps``` according to your plan.
- Fees: the Solana base fee and priority fee of each transaction (capped by ```exchange.IO("priorityFee", ...)```) are deducted from the SOL balance, and the order's ```Info``` contains ```fee```. The first time a token is bought, the wallet has to create an account for it, which takes a deposit of about 0.002 SOL; the deposit still belongs to the wallet and is not counted in the fill.

##### Pump.fun launches

```exchange.IO("pump.*", ...)``` trades coins on the pump.fun bonding curve (program ```6EF8rrecthR5Dkzon8Nwu78hRvfCKubJ14M5uBEwF6P```) directly, without Jupiter. Accounts, instructions and quote formulas follow pump.fun's official public documentation (the IDLs and docs of ```pump-fun/pump-public-docs``` on GitHub).

- New coins: ```pump.new``` discovers new coins on chain, and a strategy polls it in a loop (see the example below). Public nodes rate-limit per second and are slow (about 4 seconds for 20 transactions); for sniping, configure your own paid node in "Rpc Address".
- Only SOL-quoted coins are traded: pump.fun also has coins quoted in USDC or in another pump coin (```quote``` of ```pump.new```), for which ```pump.buy``` and ```pump.sell``` fail; cashback coins (no longer created) fail too and can be traded through Jupiter with ```exchange.Buy``` and ```exchange.Sell```.
- Price protection: a buy is exact input (spending ```solAmount```, fees included) with a minimum output of the local quote × (1 − ```slippage```); a sell's minimum SOL output is the local quote × (1 − ```slippage```). The default slippage is 5%, enforced on chain; when it cannot be met the whole transaction fails and only the network fee is charged.
- Fees: the protocol and creator fees follow the Pump Fees program's fee table, tiered by market cap (0.95% + 0.30% in October 2026; ```pump.info``` and ```pump.quote``` return the actual rates, and coins without a creator charge no creator fee), plus the Solana network and priority fees. The first buy of a coin creates its token account (a deposit of about 0.002 SOL, returned by default when ```pump.sell``` sells ```all``` and closes the account); a wallet's first pump.fun trade also creates its volume account (about 0.0018 SOL, not returned).
- Buying past the curve: when a buy's budget exceeds what the curve has left to sell (except on mayhem coins), the rest fills at the price of the PumpSwap pool the migration will create (pump.fun's "synthetic migration"), and ```crossesCurve``` of ```pump.quote``` is ```true```; after that the curve cannot be traded until the migration happens. On mayhem coins a buy beyond what is left fails.
- Graduation: for coins whose curve is complete (```complete```), ```pump.buy``` and ```pump.sell``` swap through this exchange object's Jupiter at market instead (pair ```MINT_SOL```, price protection by the call's ```slippage```, which Jupiter requires to be below 0.5) and return ```venue``` ```jupiter```; the ```priorityFee``` and ```computeUnitLimit``` options do not apply then (they fail), the priority fee cap is ```exchange.IO("priorityFee", ...)```, and ```dryRun``` is not available (quote with ```pump.quote```, which goes to Jupiter for graduated coins as well). In the short time after a curve completes and before it migrates, both routes can fail.
- Every transaction is simulated by the node before sending and is not sent when the simulation fails, with the reason in the error (pump.fun error codes with their names, such as ```BuySlippageBelowMinTokensOut```); broadcasting and deciding whether a transaction went out work as for swap orders, and waiting for confirmation works as for concentrated liquidity (an undecided outcome is reported as ```outcome is unknown``` with the signature, never as nothing happened).
- When sniping, pay enough priority fee (```options.priorityFee```), or under congestion the transaction may expire without being included.

Sniping loop example (JavaScript):

```javascript
var seen = {}
var start = Date.now()
while (true) {
    var coins = exchange.IO("pump.new", {limit: 20, since: start})
    for (var i = 0; coins && i < coins.length; i++) {
        var c = coins[i]
        if (seen[c.mint] || c.quote != "SOL" || c.mayhem) continue
        seen[c.mint] = true
        if (c.devBuy && c.devBuy.quoteAmount > 1) continue   // creator bought too much, skip
        var r = exchange.IO("pump.buy", c.mint, 0.01, {slippage: 0.2, priorityFee: 0.0005})
        if (r) Log("bought", r.tokenAmount, c.symbol, "for", r.solAmount, "SOL", r.txHash)
    }
    Sleep(1000)
}
```

Risks:
- Most new coins go to zero quickly; the creator or wallets bundled with it often buy in the creation transaction or the next few blocks and can dump at any moment (rug pull).
- Sniping bots and MEV compete hard: the order within a block depends on priority fees and tips, and a wide slippage invites sandwich attacks that fill at the worst price.
- The name, symbol and metadata link are whatever the creator chose and can impersonate well-known projects; go by the mint address.
- Protocol, creator, network and priority fees are paid on every buy and sell, so frequent in-and-out trading is costly.

##### Limit orders (tif gtc)

```exchange.CreateOrder(symbol, side, price, amount, {tif: "gtc"})``` (or ```exchange.Buy``` and ```exchange.Sell``` with the same order option) does not swap immediately but places a native Jupiter limit order, which Jupiter's keepers fill asynchronously once the price is reached. Without ```tif```, or with another ```tif```, orders behave as before (immediate swaps). There are two APIs:

| | Trigger v1 | Trigger V2 |
| - | - | - |
| Used when (```trigger.api``` at its default ```auto```) | No API key is set, or the quote is not USDC or USDT | An API key is set and the quote is USDC or USDT |
| Where funds sit | An on-chain order account (program ```j1o2qRpjcyUwEvwtcfhEQefh773ZgjxcVRry7LDqg5X```); open orders are public on chain | A vault in Jupiter's custody (Privy), one per wallet, shared by all V2 orders; orders are kept off chain by Jupiter and stay private until they fill |
| Trigger and fill | On the exchange rate of the two tokens, filled at the limit price (zero slippage by default); the amount received is guaranteed | On the base token's USD price; once reached, the order swaps at the market rate through Jupiter routing: the amount received is not guaranteed and fills may be partial; slippage is set automatically by Jupiter by default |
| Order ID | ```SOL_USDC,order account address``` | ```SOL_USDC,order UUID``` |
| Minimum | The side given or received worth at least 5 USD | The side given worth at least 10 USD |
| Expiry | Optional, none by default; Jupiter does not close an expired order, which stays open with its funds locked in the order account until canceled | Required, 30 days by default; an expired order no longer fills and its funds stay in the vault until withdrawn by canceling |
| Modify | Not supported | ```exchange.ModifyOrder()``` changes the price |

**With an API key the default is the custodial V2**: the funds of an order leave the wallet for a vault in Jupiter's custody. To keep the non-custodial v1, call ```exchange.IO("trigger.api", "v1")```; conversely ```exchange.IO("trigger.api", "v2")``` forces V2 even without an API key (Jupiter currently accepts V2 calls without a key, but its documentation requires one).

Jupiter has marked v1 as no longer developed (critical fixes only, no shutdown announced); new features go to V2. Existing v1 orders are not affected by the configuration and can still be queried and canceled (the shape of the order ID selects the API, regardless of ```trigger.api```; V2 orders need the API key or ```trigger.api``` set to ```v2``` to be queried, canceled or modified).

Common rules:

- Amounts: ```amount``` is in the base token; a buy gives ```amount × price``` of the quote token (rounded down to the smallest unit, never paying more), a sell gives ```amount``` of the base token (v1 also asks for ```amount × price``` of the quote token in return, rounded up, never receiving less). Market orders are not possible (a ```price``` of ```-1``` or ```type``` ```market``` fails).
- Order extra parameters: ```expiry``` is the expiry timestamp in milliseconds; ```slippage``` is an allowed slippage ratio (such as ```0.003```). v1 defaults to 0 (exact fills at the limit price), and a slippage raises the fill rate at the cost of filling below the limit; V2 lets Jupiter set it automatically from market conditions by default, and a given slippage is used as a fixed value.
- States: open is pending, open with fills is partially filled, fully filled is filled, and canceled is canceled. ```Info``` is Jupiter's raw order row.
- Expiry: Jupiter does not close expired orders for you, and the funds stay locked until ```exchange.CancelOrder()``` withdraws them (v1 returns the principal and the order account's rent; V2 withdraws from the vault). An expired order that has not been canceled is therefore still pending (or partially filled), with ```Info.expired``` ```true``` and ```Info.note``` saying it must be canceled to get the funds back. Expired v1 orders are still listed by ```exchange.GetOrders()``` (Jupiter keeps them open); Jupiter files expired V2 orders under history, so they are not in ```exchange.GetOrders()``` but are found by ```exchange.GetOrder()``` and ```exchange.GetHistoryOrders()```. After the cancel withdraws the funds the order is canceled.
- Canceling: for an order already filled or canceled ```exchange.CancelOrder()``` returns ```false``` with the reason in ```GetLastError()```.
- Every ```exchange.GetOrders()``` call requests Jupiter's v1 limit order list once (and the V2 list once more when an API key is set), paced by ```exchange.IO("rps", ...)```.
- Token-2022 tokens with the transfer fee or transfer hook extension cannot be used in limit orders (Jupiter does not support them).
- Use ```exchange.IO("trigger.simulate", ...)``` to simulate an order before placing it.

Trigger v1:

- Placing and canceling are on-chain transactions signed by the connector and broadcast through a Solana node; when the node's preflight simulation fails nothing is sent and the call fails. Each pays a Solana transaction fee and priority fee, and the first order in a token may create token accounts, whose deposits remain the wallet's. Canceling waits for the broadcast only; confirm the result with ```exchange.GetOrder()```.
- Fees: Jupiter deducts its fee from the token received (0.03% for stable pairs and 0.1% otherwise per its documentation; each fill record is authoritative). The order's ```AvgPrice``` is before fees, and the amounts actually received are in ```trades``` of ```Info```.
- ```exchange.GetOrder()``` looks in the open orders and then in the history; an order this program has just placed that Jupiter has not indexed yet is reported from its on-chain state (an existing order account means open).

Trigger V2:

- Authentication: the connector signs Jupiter's login challenge with the wallet's private key (only a message that starts with Jupiter's fixed login text and names this wallet) for a 15-minute access token, refreshed automatically and kept in memory only. A leaked token cannot move funds (withdrawals need a transaction signed by the wallet) but can cancel orders and change their prices.
- Placing: the connector looks up the wallet's vault and registers one if there is none (this creates a custodial account for the wallet at Jupiter; ```exchange.IO("trigger.vault", "register")``` does it ahead of time); it then has Jupiter build the deposit transaction and checks it instruction by instruction (the wallet pays the fee, only the System, Token, Associated Token Account, Compute Budget and Memo programs are called, the tokens leaving the wallet go only to the vault side and add up to exactly the order amount, and the only accounts created with the wallet's rent are the order's input account handed to the vault (Jupiter creates it with ```CreateAccountWithSeed``` based on the vault, and closes it after a cancel or fill with the rent returned to the wallet) and associated token accounts of the wallet and the vault), signs it, simulates it with the node first (nothing is sent and the call fails when the simulation fails), and hands it to Jupiter with the order parameters; Jupiter lands the deposit during that call and returns the order UUID. If that call fails the deposit may already have landed: the error names the deposit transaction signature; check it with ```exchange.IO("receipt", ...)``` and ```exchange.IO("trigger.vault")``` before retrying.
- Trigger: a buy buys when the base token's USD price falls to ```price``` or below, a sell sells when it rises to ```price``` or above. The quote token is taken as 1 USD (if USDC or USDT depegs, the trigger drifts accordingly). Jupiter does not check whether the price makes sense: a buy above or a sell below the market fills at once at the market rate.
- Amounts and fills: the order's ```Amount``` is the base token deposited for a sell and the quote token deposited ÷ price for a buy; ```DealAmount``` and ```AvgPrice``` come from the amounts actually used and received (the fee is already taken from the amount received and not listed separately on V2).
- Modifying: ```exchange.ModifyOrder()``` changes only the price (and ```slippage```), only for an open single order that has not started filling, and not the trigger price of a trailing order; the amount is fixed by the deposit and cannot change (an amount passed in must equal the original). A buy keeps the quote amount it spends when its price changes, so its ```Amount``` becomes amount ÷ new price.
- Canceling takes two steps: Jupiter stops the order (no more fills from then on) and builds a withdrawal transaction, which the connector checks (the wallet only pays the fee) and signs; Jupiter adds the vault's signature and lands it, and the unfilled tokens return to the wallet. If the second step fails the order waits for withdrawal (still listed by ```exchange.GetOrders()```), and canceling it again completes the withdrawal. Expired orders are withdrawn with ```exchange.CancelOrder()``` too.
- Custody risk: while an order is open its funds are in Jupiter's Privy-held vault, not in the wallet; they are not counted by ```exchange.GetAssets()``` (see ```exchange.IO("trigger.vault")```). Withdrawals depend on Jupiter building the withdrawal transaction and co-signing it, so they cannot be done alone while Jupiter's service is down. Jupiter still labels the V2 API beta, and its behavior may change.
- Fees: the wallet pays the network fees of the deposit and withdrawal transactions; fills are executed by Jupiter's keepers, who pay their network fees, and Jupiter's swap fee is already taken from the amount received. There is no integrator fee.
- Requests: queries and orders authenticate first (the token is cached in the process), using one or two extra requests of the rate limit; an API key restricted by endpoint permissions must include Trigger, otherwise those calls fail with 403.
- The order functions list all V2 limit orders of the wallet, including those placed elsewhere such as on jup.ag (each take-profit, stop-loss or OCO leg is listed as one order priced at its USD trigger, with the direction in ```triggerCondition``` of ```Info```). An order that triggers on a USD price but is not quoted in USDC or USDT, or that does not trigger on the base token's price, cannot be expressed as a price of its pair, and queries that meet it fail (a query for a given pair only looks at that pair's orders).

##### DCA

```exchange.IO("dca.create", ...)```, ```dca.list```, ```dca.cancel``` and ```dca.simulate```: with an API key and a USDC or USDT quote new DCA orders use Jupiter Trigger V2 DCA by default (custodial vault; ```exchange.IO("trigger.api", ...)``` applies as well: ```v1``` keeps Recurring v1, ```v2``` forces V2), otherwise the Recurring API v1 (time-based DCA, program ```DCA265Vj8a9CEuX1eb1LWRnDT7uK6q1xMipnNyatn23M```). Jupiter no longer maintains Recurring v1 (it still works); DCA has moved into Trigger V2. ```dca.list``` lists both (V2 needs the API key), and ```dca.cancel``` tells v1 (an address) from V2 (a UUID) by the shape of the DCA ID. DCA orders do not appear in ```exchange.GetOrders()``` and the other order functions.

- v1: the total is deposited into a DCA order account at once, Jupiter's keepers swap one installment every ```interval``` seconds, and the bought tokens are sent back to the wallet. At least 2 installments, each worth at least 50 USD; Token-2022 tokens are not supported; Jupiter takes a 0.1% fee from the tokens received. Creating and canceling are on-chain transactions with transaction and priority fees; canceling returns the remaining tokens to the wallet. Jupiter takes a few minutes to index a new DCA order; meanwhile ```dca.list``` lists the orders this program just created from their on-chain accounts (```indexed: false```), and ```dca.cancel``` cancels them all the same.
- V2: authentication, the vault, the deposit and the custody risk are as for V2 limit orders above. The total is deposited into the vault and the keepers swap one installment per round, sending the tokens received straight to the wallet and paying the network fees; slippage is set automatically by Jupiter from market conditions and cannot be specified; the fee is already taken from the amount received. At least 2 installments, each worth at least 10 USD, an interval of 60 seconds to 1 year, a start at most 30 days ahead, and at most 10 running DCA orders per wallet. With ```minPrice``` or ```maxPrice``` a round swaps only while the base token's USD price is in the range, and a round outside it moves to the next interval. DCA orders cannot be modified; canceling takes two steps (as for V2 limit orders), and rounds already filled are not reversed.

##### Concentrated liquidity (LP)

The ```exchange.IO("lp.*", ...)``` commands provide concentrated liquidity on Meteora DLMM pools (program ```LBUZKhRxPF3XUpBCjp4YzTKgLccjZhTSDM9YuVaPwxo```), Raydium CLMM pools (program ```CAMMCzo5YL8w4VFF8KVHrK22GGUsp5VTaW7grrKgrWqK```) and Orca Whirlpools pools (program ```whirLbMiicVdio4qvUfM5KAg6Ct8VwpYzGff3uctyCc```; how these two differ from DLMM is below): pool selection, planning and simulation, adding, increasing and decreasing, collecting fees and farm rewards, withdrawal and position queries. Command names, parameters and result fields follow the ```lp.*``` commands of the Uniswap exchange object, with these differences:

- Prices are discretized into bins rather than ticks: bin ```i``` has price (1 + binStep/10000)^i (scaled by the two tokens' decimals), ranges are given as ```lowerBinId``` and ```upperBinId``` (both inclusive), and the bin holding the current price is ```activeId```; ```range``` may be written ```{bins: [lo, hi]}```. The active bin holds both tokens, bins above it only X and bins below only Y, so the shape of a position is how much goes into each bin (```spot```, ```curve```, ```bidask```).
- A position is an account, not an NFT: its ```id``` is ```meteora:position address``` (the bare address is accepted too); a position holds at most 70 bins, and wider ```spot``` ranges are split into several positions.
- Rent: each position account locks its rent-exempt minimum (from the node's ```getMinimumBalanceForRentExemption```, about 0.042 SOL in October 2026), returned when ```lp.remove``` withdraws everything and closes it; bin array accounts (70 bins each) missing in the range are created first, and their rent (about 0.052 SOL each in October 2026) is not returned. ```rentSol```, ```rentRefundableSol``` and ```binArraysToCreate``` of the plan give these amounts. Holding a token for the first time also creates a token account (about 0.0015 SOL, still the wallet's).
- SOL is wrapped and unwrapped automatically: when one side of the pool is SOL, the transaction wraps the SOL to deposit into wSOL and closes the wallet's wSOL account at the end (wSOL already in the wallet turns back into SOL as well).
- Swaps go through this exchange object's Jupiter swaps (market orders, slippage per ```exchange.IO("slippage", ...)```).
- Every write transaction is simulated by the node before sending and is not sent when the simulation fails, with the reason in the error (DLMM, Raydium CLMM and Orca Whirlpool error codes with their names). The compute-unit limit is the simulated usage plus headroom, and the priority fee is the 75th percentile of recent fees paid by transactions writing the same accounts, capped by ```exchange.IO("priorityFee", ...)```. Broadcasting and the "may it have been sent" judgment are those of swap orders; commands return after confirmation, with actual amounts from the balances before and after the transaction. While waiting, every node is asked for the transaction status, and a transaction is reported expired (```expired without being included … nothing happened```, it really did not run) only when some nodes block height is past its last valid block height and a node past that point does not know it; a lagging or failing node never makes it look expired. When it is neither confirmed nor provably expired within 120 seconds the error says ```outcome is unknown``` and carries the signature: it may have landed, so check it with ```exchange.IO("receipt", signature)``` before retrying. When a nodes preflight reports ```BlockhashNotFound``` (it has not seen the blockhash yet; nothing was sent) the transaction is signed again with a fresh blockhash and resent, up to 2 times.
- Withdrawals have no minimum-output protection: DLMM withdraws the position's share of each bin, so the amounts depend on the bins' composition at that moment.
- Token-2022 tokens with a transfer hook are not supported, nor are positions whose fees go to another wallet (```feeOwner```); there is no ```lp.history```, ```lp.stake```, ```lp.unstake``` or ```lp.claim``` (farm rewards are claimed by ```lp.collect```, ```lp.decrease``` and ```lp.remove```).
- ```lp.positions``` finds positions by owner with the node's ```getProgramAccounts```; the official public node serves it, some nodes do not or rate-limit it, and then the call fails. Public nodes rate-limit per second and the connector backs off and retries; for frequent queries configure your own node.

How Raydium CLMM and Orca Whirlpools differ from DLMM above (they use the same tick model as Uniswap V3):

- Prices are discretized into ticks: tick ```i``` has price 1.0001^i (scaled by the two tokens' decimals), a position covers [```tickLower```, ```tickUpper```), and both ends are multiples of the pool's tick spacing (```tickSpacing```); a position in range holds both tokens, one out of range holds one. Shapes and ```layers``` are those of the Uniswap exchange object: ```curve``` and ```bidask``` consist of several positions.
- A position is an NFT: its ```id``` is ```raydium:NFT mint``` or ```orca:NFT mint``` (the bare mint or the position account address is accepted too); whoever holds the NFT owns the position. ```lp.positions``` finds positions from the NFTs with amount 1 in the wallet and needs no ```getProgramAccounts```. Token-2022 tokens with a transfer hook are not supported.
- Raydium: new positions are Token-2022 NFTs, and opening creates no metadata to keep the deposits minimal: rent for the position account, the NFT mint and the NFT account (about 0.0053 SOL together in October 2026), all returned when ```lp.remove``` closes the position. The TickArrays (60 tick spacings each) at the two ends of the range are created by the opening transaction when missing, and their rent (about 0.072 SOL each in October 2026) is not returned; ```tickArraysToCreate``` of the plan lists them. Adding and increasing fix the amount of one token (the SOL side first, otherwise the more valuable side) and cap the other at the planned amount × (1 + ```slippage```); when a price move pushes the other token beyond the cap the program fails with ```PriceSlippageCheck``` and nothing is sent. Withdrawals require at least the amounts at the current price × 0.99. Every initialized reward of the pool (even an ended one) is settled with each withdrawal or collection, and the reward tokens' ATAs are created first. Ticks beyond the pool's built-in range need the pool's TickArray bitmap extension account, and its absence is an error. Looking up a single position that is not in this wallet (```lp.track```) finds the NFT's holder by mint with the node's ```getProgramAccounts``` (the official public node serves it).
- Orca: new positions use a Token-2022 NFT (with the metadata extension, as the official Orca SDK does); older SPL Token NFT positions and positions in a Position Bundle can be queried, increased, decreased, collected and closed as well. Each position locks the rent-exempt minimums of the position account, the NFT mint and the NFT token account plus the rent of two ticks (about 0.0084 SOL in all in October 2026), all returned when ```lp.remove``` closes it; a tick array (covering 88 tick spacings) missing at either end of the range is first created as a dynamic tick array, and its rent (about 0.0019 SOL each) is not returned. Adding liquidity passes the two token amounts on chain as maxima (```increase_liquidity_by_token_amounts_v2```), and the program adds the most liquidity they allow at the execution price, failing when the price is outside the bounds implied by ```slippage```; withdrawals are protected by minimum amounts (those estimated at the current price less 1%). Decreasing or closing a locked position (```lock_position```) fails in simulation; only the main program deployment is supported (not Orca's immutable deployment). Pool statistics come from Orca's public API (```api.orca.so```); looking up a position that is not in this wallet finds the NFT holder with the node's ```getTokenLargestAccounts``` (public nodes rate-limit it tightly).

Monitoring and exits are left to the strategy: ```lp.positions``` reports whether each position is in range, its current value and uncollected fees, and the strategy decides when to rebalance or stop out.

Risks:
- Impermanent loss: the further the price moves from the entry, the lower the position is worth compared with simply holding; as the price rises the position sells X bin by bin, and as it falls it buys X.
- Once the price leaves the range the position holds a single token and earns no fees until the price returns.
- Rent locked when opening: the position account's rent (and the NFT's on Raydium and Orca) comes back on withdrawal, new bin arrays' and TickArrays' rent does not; a plan split into several positions locks rent for each.
- Every add, adjustment, collection and withdrawal is an on-chain transaction with fees and priority fees; frequent rebalancing can cost more than it earns.
- The estimated daily fees in a plan come from the past 24h volume and the plan's current share of the active bin; they do not predict future income.

##### Cross-chain bridge

```exchange.IO("bridge.*", ...)``` bridges tokens from this exchange object's chain to another chain through the bridges LI.FI aggregates (Across, Stargate, CCTP, deBridge, Mayan, Relay, NEAR Intents and more), between EVM chains and between EVM and Solana (from Solana). LI.FI supplies the quote and transaction, as a serialized transaction that the docker signs, simulates with ```simulateTransaction``` and broadcasts. Requests carry the integrator tag ```integrator=fmz``` and add no fee; fees in a quote such as ```LIFI Fixed Fee``` are LI.FI's and the bridges' own and are already deducted from ```toAmount```.

Typical flow: ```bridge.quote``` for a quote → ```bridge.simulate``` to simulate → ```bridge.send``` to send → ```bridge.status``` every 10 to 30 seconds until ```DONE``` or ```FAILED```.

- Bridging is asynchronous: when ```bridge.send``` returns, only the source-chain transaction has been broadcast; delivery takes seconds to tens of minutes (see ```executionDuration``` in the quote) and must be confirmed by polling ```bridge.status```; ```PARTIAL``` means a different token arrived on the destination chain and ```REFUNDED``` that the funds went back to the source chain.
- Cross-VM transfers (EVM↔Solana) require ```toAddress```, checked against the destination chain's address format; funds sent to a wrong address cannot be recovered.
- Risks: the security of bridge contracts and cross-chain messaging rests with each bridge; quotes move, and ```bridge.send``` re-quotes before sending; the destination wallet needs gas to use what arrives. Test with a small amount first.
- Rate limits: without an API key LI.FI limits by outgoing IP, ```/quote``` to 75 requests per 2 hours (```bridge.quote```, ```bridge.simulate``` and ```bridge.send``` use one each) and other endpoints to 100 per minute; strategies on the same docker share the quota. With a key set through ```exchange.IO("bridge.apiKey", key)``` the limit is 100 per minute. A rate-limited call fails with ```rate limited (HTTP 429 …)```.

##### Strategy examples

Complete runnable strategies: `Jupiter Limit-Order Grid` (native limit orders), `DEX Dollar-Cost Averaging` (native DCA), `pump.fun Sniping Strategy` and `DEX-CEX Arbitrage`; see `DEX Strategy Examples`.

##### exchange.IO("route", ...)

```
exchange.IO(k, symbol, side, qty)
```

Forms:

- `exchange.IO("route", ...)`

On a Jupiter exchange object, request a quote: returns the quote and route of a swap without placing an order.

Parameters:

- `k` (string, required): Selects what the ```exchange.IO()``` function does. Set it to ```route``` to request a quote.
- `symbol` (string, required): Trading pair, for example ```SOL_USDC```.
- `side` (string, required): Direction: ```sell``` sells ```qty``` units of the base currency, and ```buy``` buys ```qty``` units of the base currency.
- `qty` (number, required): Amount of the base currency.

Returns (object / null value): Returns ```{symbol, side, qty, route, quote, price, priceImpactPct, swapMode, baseQty}```: ```route``` lists the liquidity sources used, ```quote``` is the quote amount received for a sell or paid for a buy, ```baseQty``` the base amount actually sold or bought, ```price``` is ```quote``` / ```baseQty```, and ```swapMode``` is ```ExactIn``` or ```ExactOut```. Without a route these five are ```null```. A null value is returned when a token is unknown or the request fails.

Quote selling 2 SOL.

```javascript
function main() {
    var r = exchange.IO("route", "SOL_USDC", "sell", 2)
    if (!r) {
        Log("Quote failed:", GetLastError())
        return
    }
    if (r.route === null) {
        Log("No route")
        return
    }
    Log("Receive:", r.quote, "USDC", "Average price:", r.price, "Route:", r.route.join(" + "))
}
```

Quote buying 1 JUP and check the swap mode.

```javascript
function main() {
    var r = exchange.IO("route", "JUP_USDC", "buy", 1)
    if (!r || r.route === null) {
        Log("No route:", GetLastError())
        return
    }
    Log("mode", r.swapMode, "buys", r.baseQty, "JUP", "costs", r.quote, "USDC", "average", r.price)
}
```

```priceImpactPct``` is Jupiter's estimated price impact (a ratio, 0.001 = 0.1%).

Quotes use the same basis as orders: a sell is quoted as exact input (```swapMode``` ```ExactIn```); a buy is quoted as exact output for ```qty``` base units (```ExactOut```), and when there is no exact-output route (sources such as Meteora and PumpSwap do not support exact output) it is estimated with exact input instead, the same fallback as a limit buy, so ```swapMode``` is ```ExactIn``` and ```baseQty``` may differ slightly from ```qty```. Quotes do not include Solana transaction fees.

See also: `Jupiter`, `exchange.IO`, `exchange.IO("slippage")`, `exchange.IO("dexes")`, `exchange.IO("token")`, `exchange.CreateOrder`

##### exchange.IO("token", ...)

```
exchange.IO(k)
exchange.IO(k, name, mint)
```

Forms:

- `exchange.IO("token", ...)`

Register a token on a Jupiter exchange object, or list the token table.

Parameters:

- `k` (string, required): Selects what the ```exchange.IO()``` function does. Set it to ```token``` to register a token.
- `name` (string, optional): Token name used in trading pairs. It must not contain ```_``` or ```,``` and must not be the name of a built-in token.
- `mint` (string, optional): Token's mint address; its decimals are read from the chain.

Returns (object / array / null value): When registering, returns ```{symbol, mint, decimals}```. Without arguments, returns the token table as an array of ```{symbol, mint, decimals, native}``` (```native``` is ```true``` for the native coin SOL). A null value is returned when the mint address is not a token or the node fails.

Register a token and then query its market data.

```javascript
function main() {
    var t = exchange.IO("token", "MEW", "MEW1gQWJ3nEXg2qgERiKu7FAFj79PHvQVREQUzScPP5")
    Log("Registered:", t)
    Log(exchange.GetTicker("MEW_USDC"))
}
```

A registration lasts only for the current run. Without registering, a token can also be written in a pair by name (resolved against Jupiter's verified token list) or by mint address; when several tokens share a name, you must register it or use the mint address.

See also: `Jupiter`, `exchange.IO`, `exchange.IO("route")`, `exchange.IO("transfer")`, `exchange.IO("dexes")`

##### exchange.IO("transfer", ...)

```
exchange.IO(k, to, amount)
```

Forms:

- `exchange.IO("transfer", ...)`

Transfer SOL out of the wallet of a Jupiter exchange object.

Parameters:

- `k` (string, required): Selects what the ```exchange.IO()``` function does. Set it to ```transfer``` to make a transfer.
- `to` (string, required): Recipient's Solana address.
- `amount` (number / string, required): Amount of SOL; pass ```all``` to transfer the whole balance (minus the fee).

Returns (object / null value): When the broadcast succeeds, returns ```{signature, amount, lastValidBlockHeight}```. ```signature``` is the transaction signature; use ```exchange.IO("receipt", ...)``` to check whether it has landed. A null value is returned for an invalid address, an insufficient balance or a failed broadcast.

Transfer 0.1 SOL and wait for confirmation.

```javascript
function main() {
    var r = exchange.IO("transfer", "RECIPIENT_ADDRESS", 0.1)
    if (!r) {
        Log("Transfer failed:", GetLastError())
        return
    }
    Log(exchange.IO("receipt", r.signature, 60000))
}
```

Only SOL can be transferred; other tokens are not supported yet. After transferring the whole balance the wallet can no longer pay swap fees.

See also: `Jupiter`, `exchange.IO`, `exchange.IO("receipt")`, `exchange.IO("priorityFee")`, `exchange.IO("token")`

##### exchange.IO("receipt", ...)

```
exchange.IO(k, signature)
exchange.IO(k, signature, waitMs)
```

Forms:

- `exchange.IO("receipt", ...)`

On a Jupiter exchange object, query the status of a Solana transaction, optionally waiting until it is confirmed.

Parameters:

- `k` (string, required): Selects what the ```exchange.IO()``` function does. Set it to ```receipt``` to query a transaction status.
- `signature` (string, required): Transaction signature. For an order, pass the part after the comma in the order ID.
- `waitMs` (number, optional): Maximum wait time in milliseconds (at most 600000); the function returns early once the transaction is confirmed or fails. Omit it to check without waiting.

Returns (object / null value): Returns ```{signature, state, slot, confirmationStatus, err, fee, blockTime}```. ```state``` is ```success``` (confirmed), ```failed``` (failed on chain, with the reason in ```err```) or ```pending``` (not confirmed; when the node cannot find the transaction yet, ```visible: false``` is added). After confirmation ```fee``` (SOL) and ```blockTime``` (seconds) are included. A null value is returned when the node request fails.

Query the transaction status of an order.

```javascript
function main() {
    var id = exchange.CreateOrder("SOL_USDC", "sell", -1, 0.1)
    if (!id) return
    var r = exchange.IO("receipt", String(id).split(",")[1], 60000)
    Log(r.state, r.fee)
}
```

See also: `Jupiter`, `exchange.IO`, `exchange.IO("transfer")`, `exchange.IO("priorityFee")`, `exchange.IO("route")`

##### exchange.IO("slippage", ...)

```
exchange.IO(k)
exchange.IO(k, ratio)
```

Forms:

- `exchange.IO("slippage", ...)`

Set the slippage protection for market orders on a Jupiter exchange object.

Parameters:

- `k` (string, required): Selects what the ```exchange.IO()``` function does. Set it to ```slippage``` to set slippage protection for market orders.
- `ratio` (number, optional): Slippage ratio. Its valid range is ```[0, 0.5)``` and its default is ```0.005``` (0.5%). Omit it to query the current value.

Returns (number): Returns the current slippage ratio.

Set slippage protection for market orders.

```javascript
function main() {
    exchange.IO("slippage", 0.01)     // 1%
    Log("Slippage:", exchange.IO("slippage"))
}
```

For a market order, the slippage is deducted from the quote to give the minimum amount received, which the on-chain program enforces; if the price moves by more than the slippage before execution, the transaction fails (only the fee is lost) and the order is reported as canceled.

You can also set slippage for a single order by appending ```;{"slippage":0.01}``` to the direction parameter of ```exchange.CreateOrder()```. Limit orders do not use this setting: the connector computes the exact slippage from the limit price, since the limit price itself is the worst fill price.

See also: `Jupiter`, `exchange.IO`, `exchange.IO("route")`, `exchange.IO("dexes")`, `exchange.IO("priorityFee")`, `exchange.CreateOrder`

##### exchange.IO("priorityFee", ...)

```
exchange.IO(k)
exchange.IO(k, sol)
```

Forms:

- `exchange.IO("priorityFee", ...)`

When called as ```exchange.IO("priorityFee", ...)```, this function sets the priority fee cap for swap transactions on a Jupiter exchange object.

Parameters:

- `k` (string, required): Selects what the ```exchange.IO()``` function does. Set it to ```priorityFee``` to set the priority fee cap.
- `sol` (number, optional): Priority fee cap per transaction, in SOL. Its range is 0 to 0.1 and its default is 0.001. Omit it to query the current value.

Returns (number): Returns the current priority fee cap (SOL).

Raise the priority fee cap.

```javascript
function main() {
    exchange.IO("priorityFee", 0.005)
    Log("Priority fee cap:", exchange.IO("priorityFee"), "SOL")
}
```

The actual priority fee is estimated by Jupiter from current network congestion (a high tier) and never exceeds this cap. Once the transaction is confirmed, ```fee``` in the ```Info``` of the order returned by `exchange.GetOrder` is the fee actually paid for the transaction (SOL, base fee plus priority fee). If the cap is too low, transactions may fail to land in time during congestion and expire.

See also: `Jupiter`, `exchange.IO`, `exchange.IO("slippage")`, `exchange.IO("receipt")`, `exchange.IO("transfer")`, `exchange.CreateOrder`

##### exchange.IO("dexes", ...)

```
exchange.IO(k)
exchange.IO(k, sources)
```

Forms:

- `exchange.IO("dexes", ...)`

When called as ```exchange.IO("dexes", ...)```, this function restricts the liquidity sources that swaps go through on a Jupiter exchange object, for example to trade only on pump.fun, Meteora or Raydium.

Parameters:

- `k` (string, required): Selects what the ```exchange.IO()``` function does. Set it to ```dexes``` to restrict the liquidity sources.
- `sources` (string, optional): Comma-separated list of sources. It can use the group shorthands ```pump``` (Pump.fun, Pump.fun Amm), ```meteora``` (Meteora, Meteora DAMM v2, Meteora DLMM), ```raydium``` (Raydium, Raydium CLMM, Raydium CP, Raydium Launchlab) and ```orca``` (Whirlpool, Orca V1, Orca V2), or Jupiter source names (case-sensitive). An empty string ```""``` removes the restriction. Omit it to query the current setting.

Returns (array / null value): Returns the array of source names currently in effect (groups expanded; an empty array means no restriction). If a source name is not in Jupiter's source table, a null value is returned, the setting is left unchanged, and ```GetLastError()``` lists the available source names.

Trade a new token on pump.fun only.

```javascript
function main() {
    exchange.IO("dexes", "pump")
    exchange.IO("token", "POUT", "DB5QKorV9KHY54y73h5xWQqYyuD8P3jC1p5Ea8DBpump")
    var t = exchange.GetTicker("POUT_SOL")
    Log("Bid", t.Buy, "Ask", t.Sell, "via", t.Info.askRoute)
}
```

With a restriction in place, market data (```exchange.GetTicker()```, ```exchange.GetDepth()```), quotes and orders all go through these sources only; when no route can be found the call reports that there is no route. The "Liquidity Sources" setting in the exchange configuration is the initial value of the same setting.

See also: `Jupiter`, `exchange.IO`, `exchange.IO("route")`, `exchange.IO("slippage")`, `exchange.IO("priorityFee")`, `exchange.CreateOrder`

##### exchange.IO("rps", ...)

```
exchange.IO(k)
exchange.IO(k, n)
```

Forms:

- `exchange.IO("rps", ...)`

When called as ```exchange.IO("rps", ...)```, this function sets the rate of requests to the Jupiter API on a Jupiter exchange object.

Parameters:

- `k` (string, required): Selects what the ```exchange.IO()``` function does. Set it to ```rps``` to set the request rate.
- `n` (number, optional): Maximum number of requests per second. Its range is 0.1 to 500 and its default is 1. Omit it to query the current value.

Returns (number): Returns the current maximum number of requests per second.

Raise the rate when an API key on the Developer plan is configured.

```javascript
function main() {
    exchange.IO("rps", 10)
    var t = Date.now()
    exchange.GetDepth("SOL_USDC")
    Log("Depth took:", Date.now() - t, "ms")
}
```

Jupiter limits requests per second: about 0.5 to 1 per second without an API key, 1 per second with a free API key, and 10 to 150 per second on paid plans. The connector queues requests one after another, at least ```1/n``` seconds apart; if it still receives 429 it backs off and retries, and returns a null value after repeated failures. A value higher than your plan allows triggers rate limiting frequently.

See also: `Jupiter`, `exchange.IO`, `exchange.IO("route")`, `exchange.IO("token")`, `exchange.IO("receipt")`

##### exchange.IO("lp.pools", ...)

```
exchange.IO(k, token)
exchange.IO(k, token, quote)
```

Forms:

- `exchange.IO("lp.pools", ...)`

List a token's concentrated-liquidity pools on Meteora DLMM, Raydium CLMM and Orca Whirlpools, largest USD TVL first.

Parameters:

- `k` (string, required): Set to ```lp.pools``` to list pools.
- `token` (string, required): The token to look up: a name in the token table, a verified Jupiter token name or a mint address, for example ```SOL``` or ```JUP```. Every row uses it as the base token.
- `quote` (string, optional): List only pools against this quote token. Without it, pools against SOL, USDC and USDT are listed (excluding the token itself).

Returns (array / null value): An array of pools sorted by ```tvlUsd```, largest first (rows without TVL data come last). Every row has the common fields ```{id, protocol, dex, symbol, base, quote, fee, feeRate, price, reserveBase, reserveQuote, tvlQuote, tvlUsd, volume24hUsd, fees24hUsd, rewards, empty}``` plus fields of its protocol, see the remarks. A null value is returned when the token cannot be recognized or a request fails, with the reason in ```GetLastError()```.

List the 5 SOL/USDC pools with the largest USD TVL.

```javascript
function main() {
    var pools = exchange.IO("lp.pools", "SOL", "USDC")
    if (!pools) {
        Log("Query failed:", GetLastError())
        return
    }
    Log(pools.length, "pools")
    for (var i = 0; i < pools.length && i < 5; i++) {
        var p = pools[i]
        var grid = p.protocol == "meteora" ? "binStep " + p.binStep : "tickSpacing " + p.tickSpacing
        Log(p.dex, p.id, "fee", p.fee / 1e4 + "%", grid, "price", p.price,
            "TVL", Math.round(p.tvlUsd), "24h volume", Math.round(p.volume24hUsd))
    }
}
```

List the farm rewards of the 10 SOL pools with the largest TVL and whether they are being emitted (Meteora rows have no active).

```javascript
function main() {
    var pools = exchange.IO("lp.pools", "SOL")
    if (!pools) {
        Log("Query failed:", GetLastError())
        return
    }
    pools.slice(0, 10).forEach(function(p) {
        var names = (p.rewards || []).map(function(r) {
            var state = r.active === undefined ? "" : (r.active ? " (emitting)" : " (ended)")
            return r.symbol + state
        })
        Log(p.dex, p.symbol, p.id, "rewards:", names.length ? names.join(", ") : "none")
    })
}
```

###### Common fields
